sections.heading: How we match a tutor for IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai
paragraphs: Requests for IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai arrive in two waves, and they need different tutors. The first wave comes six or seven weeks out, when a parent wants the papers prepared for. The second comes in the fortnight after results, when a mock grade has landed badly and the family wants to know what it means. A tutor who is good at the first job is not automatically good at the second, because reading a marked script back is a separate skill from teaching a topic.

So the matching question is which wave you are in. Before mocks, we look for a tutor who will stop teaching new content at the right moment and switch to timed sections. After mocks, we look for someone who will ask for the script rather than the grade, go through it question by question, and come back with a short written list of what actually went wrong. Ask any shortlisted tutor which of those two they think they are being hired for. The answer tells you a great deal.

The practical part follows the usual order. 1. Send the subjects, the levels and the dates of the school mock block if you have them. 2. Tell us whether the scripts have been returned and whether you can get them. 3. Two or three profiles come back with afternoon or weekend slots, because mock fortnight breaks the usual evening pattern. 4. You speak to each tutor before booking. 5. The first session either builds the pre-mock timetable or performs the autopsy on the script, depending on the wave.

Where a household wants a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai because several mocks went badly at once, we will usually push back. Four weak mocks in one block more often reflects a timing or revision-method problem than four separate content problems, and that is one conversation with one tutor rather than four bookings. We would rather fix the method first and see which subjects are still standing afterwards.

2. Tell us whether the marked scripts can actually be obtained.

sections.heading: Which mocks matter: DP, MYP and IGCSE in Mumbai schools
paragraphs: A mock is set and marked by the school, not by a board, and that single fact explains most of the confusion around them. Two campuses can run a Diploma Programme (DP) mock on the same course with different paper selection, different marking severity and different assumptions about grade boundaries. The International Baccalaureate does not publish your child's mock grade and has no view on it. Only the school does.

The stakes differ by programme. For a DP2 cohort the mock carries real weight because it is a major input into the predicted grades the school sends to universities, which makes it the highest-consequence internal examination of the two years. For Middle Years Programme (MYP) students a mock is mostly diagnostic and worth treating calmly. At Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE a mock can carry a decision attached to it, because some schools use mock performance as evidence when confirming whether a child is entered at Core or Extended tier, and that entry decision shapes the range of grades available. Ask your school whether the mock plays that role before treating it as a dry run.

Level discipline matters in the preparation. A Higher Level (HL) mock and a Standard Level (SL) mock in the same subject are not the same paper, and a tutor preparing a child for the wrong one wastes the weeks that mattered. Our coverage line reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, and the operative words there are course and level rather than subject. Confirm which paper your child is actually sitting in the mock block, because schools occasionally run a shortened or combined version.

One thing a mock does not test is coursework, and that catches families out every year. Internal Assessment (IA) work, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) components sit outside the mock entirely, so a child can sit a strong mock block while an IA draft is three weeks late. If you are using the mock as a progress check, check the coursework position separately with the coordinator in the same week.
bullets: A mock is set and marked by the school, not by a board.
DP mocks feed predicted grades; MYP mocks are mostly diagnostic.
Ask whether an IGCSE mock informs the Core or Extended entry.
Confirm which paper and level the mock block actually uses.

sections.heading: What does a mock paper test that a class test does not?
paragraphs: Four things, and none of them is content knowledge. A mock tests breadth across a whole course rather than a recent unit, the decisions involved in choosing questions, the pacing of a full paper from first question to last, and the reading of command words under pressure. A child who scores well on unit tests and badly in a mock usually has a complete content base and no examination technique.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai sees the same pattern repeating. In the sciences, marks go on data handling and on explanations that state what happened without saying why. In Mathematics, method marks are lost because working is not written down, so a right answer reached badly scores less than a wrong answer reasoned well. In the essay subjects, the loss is almost always structure and the command word: a question that says evaluate answered as though it said describe will score in the lower band however much the student knows. In languages, timing on the longer writing task is the usual culprit.

Question choice deserves its own attention because it is pure technique and completely teachable. Where a paper offers options, students pick the question with the familiar topic rather than the one with the answerable question, and then write everything they know instead of what was asked. A tutor can rehearse this in twenty minutes a week: read all the options, mark the command word, sketch the answer in three lines, then choose. Children who do that in a mock stop losing whole bands in the real series.

Breadth is the other mock-specific problem. A class test covers what was taught in the last month, so a child can carry a forgotten first-year topic for a long time without consequence. A mock paper will find it. That is the single most useful thing a mock does, and it is why the weeks after one are worth more than the weeks before.
bullets: Mocks test breadth, pacing, question choice and command words.
Unwritten working in Mathematics loses method marks silently.
Evaluate answered as describe scores in a lower band regardless.

sections.heading: Mock weeks across Mumbai: school clusters and afternoon slots
paragraphs: Mock season changes the shape of the week, and that is the local story here. During the block, school days end early or stop entirely, so the useful slot moves from 7pm to the afternoon, and at 3pm this city is a different place. A tutor who could never hold an evening slot across the Western Express Highway can hold a four o'clock one comfortably. So mock fortnight is the one period when parents searching IB tutors near me in Mumbai should widen the radius rather than narrow it.

School clusters matter more than residential zones for this. In South Mumbai, families around Fort, Napean Sea Road, Breach Candy, Worli and Mahalaxmi are mostly at island campuses, and an afternoon session there avoids the Peddar Road and Haji Ali crawl entirely, with the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link useful for the rarer cross-city match and Metro Line 3 running underneath. In the Western Suburbs the heavy cluster runs from Bandra West and Santacruz West through Juhu to Goregaon East, with Kandivali East and Borivali further up; Metro Line 1 between Versova and Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 along the Dahisar to Andheri corridor make an afternoon crossing straightforward where the Western Line is crowded.

In the Central Suburbs the clusters sit around Powai, Ghatkopar, Bhandup and Mulund West, reached by road through JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway or on the Central Line. The Eastern Suburbs, from Wadala and Chembur out to Govandi and Vikhroli, have the Harbour Line, the Eastern Freeway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR), and a Chembur family can reasonably look at a tutor on the island for an afternoon slot in mock week even though an evening one would never hold.

Navi Mumbai and Thane work on their own clocks. In Navi Mumbai, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur and Kharghar are a few minutes apart on Palm Beach Road, so a node-to-node afternoon match is easy and the Atal Setu widens the weekend options for a paper review. In Thane, families in Thane West, Hiranandani Estate, Pokhran Road and Kasarvadavali should still favour a tutor on their side of Ghodbunder Road, though the afternoon version of that road is a different animal from the seven o'clock one. Families write to us from right across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and in this fortnight the right answer is usually the tutor who can be free at 4pm.

sections.heading: When do Mumbai schools run mock exams?
paragraphs: Each school sets its own mock window, so there is no city-wide answer and nobody should give you one. For a cohort sitting the May series, the mock block usually falls in the winter term, after the long Diwali break and before the spring revision term. For a cohort sitting the November series the school's window was built for May candidates, so an out-of-cycle student often needs a mock arranged specially. Your school examinations officer holds the actual dates, and they are the person to ask.

What families should ask for alongside the dates is the shape of the block. How many papers in how many days, whether they are sat in examination conditions or in classrooms, whether the full paper is used or a shortened version, how long until scripts come back, and whether scripts come back at all. Those answers change the preparation more than the dates do. A block of eight papers in five days needs stamina work in the fortnight before; the same eight spread over three weeks does not.

Standards vary between campuses, which is why mock grades travel badly between families. Parents at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, JBCN International School in Borivali and in Oshiwara, Witty International School in Malad, Billabong High International School in Santacruz, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul are all comparing numbers produced under different conditions. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here; we work from your child's script and your school's own marking, not from a comparison.

The other school conversation worth having early is about predicted grades. They are issued by the school, informed by the mock and by everything else the teachers have seen, and a tutor has no part in setting them. If a mock grade is going to affect a university application, the discussion belongs with the subject teacher and the counsellor in the fortnight after results, while the script and the reasoning are still fresh. Going in with a marked paper and three specific questions works far better than going in with a complaint.

Ask how many papers in how many days, and in what conditions.

sections.heading: Home tuition or online classes for the weeks around mocks
paragraphs: Home tutoring leads for the paper work, and most IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai happens at a dining table for a physical reason. A marked script is a paper object covered in a teacher's handwriting, and IB home tuition in Mumbai means a tutor sitting next to your child with that script flat on the table, a pen in hand and the mark scheme beside it. Scanning eight papers to send ahead of a video call is possible and almost nobody does it. The same session at home needs no preparation beyond finding the folder.

Online earns its place in the timed-paper half of the work. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can set a paper, start a shared timer, stay silent for the duration and then mark it live on screen, which is a well-suited use of the format and saves two crossings in a week when every afternoon counts. It also makes a short session practical: fifteen minutes on tomorrow's paper structure during the mock block itself is worth having and is not worth a commute in either direction.

The hybrid that works around mocks is specific enough to name. In the weeks before, run the teaching and the timed papers wherever is convenient. During the block, go online for short daily contact and nothing more. In the fortnight after, go back home for the script autopsy, because that session needs the paper, the mark scheme and two people looking at the same page. Agree that pattern when you book rather than renegotiating it mid-block.

Honest trade-offs, as always. Home classes cost travel time and therefore fee, and during mock fortnight they also cost flexibility, since a session fixed for Tuesday afternoon cannot move when the school changes a paper date. Online is flexible and loses the shared page. Neither mode helps if the household treats mock week as normal: the child needs the quiet room, an early night and somebody else answering the door.
bullets: Script review needs the paper on a table, so do it at home.
Online suits timed papers: shared timer, silence, live marking after.
Short daily online contact during the block beats a long session.

sections.heading: Who marks your child's mock, and how is a tutor checked?
paragraphs: Your child's mock is marked by their own subject teacher in most schools, which is worth knowing before anybody argues with a grade. That teacher has the class standard, the paper and the context; what they do not always have is time to annotate every lost mark. IB Gram checks a tutor's identity, qualifications and teaching history with a reference call before any introduction, and for this work we also check whether they have marked to published criteria themselves.

That last check is the one that matters for mock work. A tutor who has examined or who has taught the course long enough to mark a paper against the scheme will tell you why a four-mark answer scored two. A tutor who has not will tell you the answer was incomplete, which you already knew. Ask directly: have you marked this paper type against the published scheme, and will you show me how the marks fall on one of my child's answers?

Run your own checks beyond that. Ask an IB private tutor in Mumbai how they would spend the first session if the script has not come back yet, because there is a real answer involving the question paper alone and a vague one. Ask what they will not do, which should include writing your child's coursework and predicting a grade. No honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade off the back of a mock, and anybody who talks about outcomes before reading a script is guessing in front of you.

Then the practical household checks, which do not change for mock season except in timing. A home tutor arriving at 4pm on a weekday needs the same standing gate pass or visitor entry as one arriving at 7pm, and daytime entry sometimes needs a different approval in a society that logs school-hours visitors separately. Sort it before the block starts, agree who is at home in the afternoon, and agree what happens to a slot when the school moves a paper.
bullets: Most mocks are marked by your child's own subject teacher.
Ask whether the tutor has marked this paper type to the scheme.
Ask them to show the marks falling on one real answer.
Daytime society entry can need a separate approval from evening entry.

sections.heading: How to read a mock paper back, and what a mock score does not tell you
paragraphs: The grade on the front is the least useful number on the paper. Real IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai starts after the mock, with the script open and every lost mark sorted into one of four causes: content never taught, content taught and forgotten, method understood but misapplied, and marks lost to timing or to a misread command word. Those four demand completely different responses, and a plan that treats them as one thing fails.

Work through it in order. Content never taught is not your child's problem and not the tutor's first priority either; note it, tell the school, and check whether the mock covered material the class had not reached, which happens more often than families assume. Content taught and forgotten is the cheapest fix available and belongs in short weekly retrieval work rather than in re-teaching. Method misapplied is the expensive one, because the child believes they know it, and it needs supervised practice on the same question type until the method is automatic. Timing and command-word losses are technique, and they move fastest of all: usually within three or four sessions, which is why a page of them in a mock is good news.

Now what a mock score cannot tell you. It cannot tell you a grade, because the school chose the papers and set the marking severity and may have used its own boundaries. It cannot tell you about a topic the paper never asked about. It cannot tell you whether your child was unwell that week. And a single harsh mock cannot tell you more than a term of marked class work, so when the two disagree, treat the disagreement itself as the finding and go and ask the teacher which one surprised them. The honest output of a mock is the distribution of lost marks, not the total.

The fortnight after the block is the whole opportunity, and it is short. The script is fresh in your child's memory for about ten days, after which they genuinely cannot remember what they were thinking in question seven, and the autopsy degrades into guesswork. So ask for the scripts early, sit down with an IB home tutor in Mumbai while the memory holds, produce one page of written actions per subject, and then re-sit one full paper under time three or four weeks later to see which of the four causes actually moved. That one page per subject is the most valuable document a mock produces.
bullets: Sort every lost mark into one of four distinct causes.
Forgotten content is cheap to fix; misapplied method is not.
Timing and command-word losses move within three or four sessions.
A mock score reflects the school's paper choice and marking severity.

sections.heading: What home classes can change between mocks and the real series
paragraphs: In the first fortnight, expect a document rather than a difference. An IB tutor in Mumbai doing this work properly should hand you one page per subject: the four causes with your child's actual lost marks under each, what will be done about each, and in what order. If the first two sessions produce encouragement and no page, the work has not happened.

By four to six weeks the test is a re-sat paper, the same paper type under the same time limit, compared with the mock section by section. Technique losses should be visibly down, because they are the fastest to move. Forgotten content should be down if retrieval practice happened. Misapplied method may barely have shifted, and that is normal rather than a failure; it is the slowest of the four and the one that needs the most supervised repetition. Parents who look only at the total will miss all of that.

Across the stretch between mocks and the real series, the honest limits. We do not guarantee grades and nobody can predict one from a mock. The variables that remain are the work done between sessions, the school's own teaching, the papers that turn up on the day and your child's health in the exam fortnight. Parents often ask us to find the best IB tutor in Mumbai after a bad mock, and the more useful request is a tutor who can read a script, because that skill is specific and checkable while the superlative is not.

If nothing has changed six weeks after the mock, the match is wrong and the clock is now expensive. Say what is missing: no written page, no re-sat paper, sessions that have become homework supervision. A replacement after mocks still has the remaining term to work with, and the new tutor should start from the same script rather than from the previous tutor's notes. Leaving it until the next set of internal exams wastes the one diagnostic your child already paid for in a week of papers.
bullets: First fortnight: one written page per subject, not encouragement.
Four to six weeks: the same paper type re-sat under time.
Technique improves first; misapplied method is the slowest to move.
Grades are not guaranteed, and no mock predicts one.

sections.heading: Starting mock preparation in Mumbai this fortnight
paragraphs: Send three things and the match is usually quick: the subjects and levels, the mock block dates if the school has issued them, and whether the marked scripts are in your hands yet. The third one decides what the first session is for. With scripts, it is an autopsy. Without them, it is a timetable built from the question papers and the last set of class marks.

Prepare the table before the session rather than during it. The question papers, the marked scripts, the subject file, a highlighter and a blank sheet per subject. Where a school returns scripts only on request, ask for them in writing early, and where it does not return them at all, ask whether your child may read their paper in school and note the question numbers where marks went. Even a list of question numbers is enough to start.

Expect the tutor to spend the first session mostly reading and asking your child what they were thinking, which can look like very little teaching for the money. It is the part that makes the next six weeks efficient. Where several subjects went wrong at once, all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai are not the answer; one tutor diagnosing the method is, and the subject bookings follow from what they find.

One last thing to settle before anybody books. Confirm with the school which examination session your child is entered for and which paper the mock used, because mock preparation for a cohort sitting in a few months looks nothing like mock preparation for a cohort a year out. Establish the real entry first, in writing, and the plan after that is straightforward.
bullets: Send subjects, levels, mock block dates and script availability.
Lay out papers, scripts, file, highlighter and a blank sheet.
Ask in writing for scripts early; a question-number list will do.
One diagnostic tutor first, subject bookings after the findings.

faqs.question: How long before mocks should a tutor start?
faqs.answer: Six to seven weeks is the useful window for IB mock exam preparation in Mumbai, and the shape of it matters more than the length. The first few weeks close the content gaps the class has already covered but your child has not consolidated, the middle weeks move to timed sections, and the last two weeks are full papers with no new material at all. Starting two weeks out is still worth doing, but it becomes technique work only: question choice, pacing, command words and the mechanics of sitting a paper. Ask the school for the mock block dates first so the countdown is built on the real timetable rather than on a guess.

faqs.question: My child's mock grade is far below their class marks. Which one is right?
faqs.answer: Probably neither on its own, and the gap between them is the actual finding. Class marks measure recent material in short tests; a mock measures the whole course under time, so a wide gap usually points at breadth and pacing rather than at understanding. Get the script and sort the lost marks by cause before drawing any conclusion. Then take the paper to the subject teacher and ask one question: was this result a surprise? If it was, something specific happened in that room on that day. If it was not, the teacher has been seeing something the class tests did not show you.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come home for an afternoon slot during mock week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and mock week is the easiest fortnight of the year to arrange it. School days finish early or stop during the block, so a 3pm or 4pm session is possible for the first time, and afternoon traffic across this city is nothing like the evening peak. That widens your choice of tutor considerably. Two conditions: tell the tutor the block dates as soon as the school issues them, because every family in the cluster wants the same afternoons, and check that whoever is at home can let the tutor in during school hours. A slot nobody can open the door for is not a slot.

faqs.question: Will my building let a tutor in for a daytime slot during mocks?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but it can need a separate approval from an evening visit. Several societies log school-hours visitors differently, some require a resident present rather than domestic staff, and a few run an app-based pass that has to be issued each time. Sort this in the week before the mock block, not on the first afternoon. Ask your society office for a standing entry naming the tutor, the days and the time window, and send the tutor whatever the gate will want to see. During mock fortnight a tutor stuck at the gate for twenty minutes costs you a paper review you cannot reschedule.

faqs.question: Do mock results decide predicted grades?
faqs.answer: They inform them heavily but they do not decide them, and the decision is the school's alone. Predicted grades are issued by your child's teachers using the mock, class work, coursework progress and their own judgement of trajectory, which is why a single weak paper in one subject rarely moves a prediction by itself and a consistent pattern does. No tutor has any role in setting a prediction, and you should be sceptical of one who implies otherwise. If a prediction matters for an application, book time with the subject teacher and the school counsellor in the fortnight after results, with the marked script in hand.

faqs.question: What do we do with the marked mock script?
faqs.answer: Take it apart within ten days, while your child can still remember what they were thinking. Go question by question and put every lost mark into one of four buckets: never taught, taught and forgotten, method misapplied, or lost to timing and command words. Write one page per subject listing what falls where and what will be done about each. Then put the script in the subject file rather than the bin, because it is the comparison point when the same paper type is re-sat in a month. Families who file the grade and lose the paper have thrown away the only diagnostic the week produced.

faqs.question: Should we book extra sessions during the mock fortnight itself?
faqs.answer: Shorter ones, not extra ones. During the block the only useful work is on tomorrow's paper: fifteen or twenty minutes on its structure, the question types and the timing plan, plus a check that equipment and the timetable are sorted. Long teaching sessions in the middle of a mock block cost sleep and return very little, and reading back a paper already sat raises anxiety without changing a mark. Keep the heavy work for the fortnight after results. Where a tutor wants to add two-hour sessions during the block itself, ask them what the student is meant to do with the material that night.

faqs.question: How much does mock preparation cost in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the same factors as any other engagement, plus one specific to this work. IB tuition fees in Mumbai move with board and level, with subject scarcity, with travel distance, and with session length and frequency. The mock-specific factor is marking time: a tutor who reads and annotates a full script between sessions is doing unpaid work unless it is priced in, so ask whether script review is included in the session rate or charged separately. Get the per-session rate, the travel assumption and the marking arrangement in one written message before the first session, and ask what a short mock-week session costs.

faqs.question: Does a weak mock at a Powai school mean a tier change at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not by itself, and the decision sits with the school rather than with you or a tutor. Some schools do use mock performance as part of the evidence when confirming whether a child is entered at Core or Extended tier, so a weak mock can start that conversation. Ask the examinations officer directly what the entry currently says and what would change it, and ask the subject teacher what they would need to see to keep an Extended entry. Then build the next six weeks around that answer. A tier decision taken on one paper, without asking what caused the lost marks, is a decision taken too early.

faqs.question: The tutor wants to stop teaching new content before mocks. Is that right?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a good sign rather than a worrying one. In the last two weeks before a paper, new content displaces the rehearsal that actually converts knowledge into marks, and a topic learned three days before a mock is rarely available under time pressure. The right use of those weeks is full papers, mark schemes read properly and the question types your child loses marks on. Any genuinely missing topic should be noted for the weeks after mocks instead. A tutor still introducing new material the week before the block has not planned the six weeks that preceded it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Kharghar for a weekend paper review session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the weekend is the right time to ask for it. Navi Mumbai matches well node to node, so a tutor from Nerul, Belapur or Panvel reaches Kharghar easily on Palm Beach Road or the Sion-Panvel Highway, and a weekend crossing from the island city over the Atal Setu is realistic in a way the same trip at 7pm on a Wednesday is not. A script review is the ideal session to put on a Saturday morning: it needs ninety unhurried minutes, the papers spread out on a table and nobody watching the clock for a school bus.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: IB Gram matches on three things: the art form your child is actually doing, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) year they are in, and how far a tutor can realistically travel on a weekday evening. You send the school, the year, the art form and your locality. We come back with two or three verified tutors and you speak to each one before anything is booked. An IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai is matched to the art form first, because visual arts, music, drama and dance are not interchangeable and a painter is no help to a child building a dance composition.

The art form question matters more here than in almost any other MYP subject group. A tutor who studied fine art can read a sketchbook and talk about mark-making, but will not hear why a student's recorder piece sits awkwardly in its register. Within visual arts there is a further split: a printmaker, an illustrator and a sculptor teach different things and notice different problems. We ask which medium the current unit uses before we shortlist, and if the school has set a unit no available tutor has worked in, we say so rather than sending someone to improvise in front of a thirteen-year-old.

The second filter is distance, and in Mumbai that is a question about roads rather than kilometres. A tutor living in Chembur can take a standing Tuesday slot in Govandi and hold it for a whole term. The same tutor offered Bandra at 6pm will cancel by week four. We match within a corridor wherever the art form allows it, and when a specialism is scarce enough that nobody nearby covers it, we say that plainly and offer online sessions or a weekend home slot instead of pretending the weekday run across the city will hold.

sections.heading: The MYP years, the eight subject groups, and where arts sits
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs five years, usually Years 6 to 10 in a Mumbai school's own numbering, and it covers eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, design, and physical and health education. Arts is one group holding two broad families, visual arts and performing arts, and performing arts in most Mumbai schools means music, drama or dance. A student may stay with one art form for the whole programme or rotate through two or three in the early years before settling.

What changes across the five years is not the criteria but the expectation sitting behind them. In MYP Year 1 a student may be asked to look at one artist and try something similar. By Year 4 the same student is expected to run an enquiry: find practitioners doing something relevant to their own question, test techniques, keep a record, and explain what the testing changed. By Year 5 the written reflection is read as seriously as the finished piece, and students who have only ever been praised for neat work find that shift uncomfortable. It is a change of job, not a change of difficulty.

Two things sit outside this page. The Year 5 personal project is its own piece of work with a school-appointed supervisor, and we cover it separately. MYP eAssessment is a school decision: some Mumbai schools enter Year 5 students for external assessment and others report on internally moderated work, and only your school's MYP coordinator can confirm which route applies. Requests reach us in many shapes, from a MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai to MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai parents describe in one line, and the internal label we file them under is MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai, which is unwieldy but accurate. What we need from you is narrower: art form, year, locality.

sections.heading: Criteria A to D in MYP arts, and what each one is really asking
paragraphs: MYP arts is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, and they run in the order a real project runs: investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. Your school publishes the current wording and the band descriptors on the task sheet it hands out, and the IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so take the bands from the sheet in your child's folder rather than from any summary, including this one. What does not change is the shape. Two of the four criteria are about thinking, one is about making, and one is about looking back honestly.

Here is the gap in practice. A Year 4 student in Khar West is cutting a series of lino prints about the Mithi River. For the investigating criterion she has to show she looked at practitioners doing something related, named them properly, and said what she took from them and what she rejected. For the evaluating criterion she has to say what the finished prints did not manage to do. Most students write the first reasonably and the second as an apology. A tutor's job is to make her say, in one plain sentence, what the third pull taught her that the first two did not.

The commonest pattern that IB MYP arts home tuition in Mumbai has to fix is a folder of competent work with almost nothing written around it. The making is fine. The student can talk about it fluently when asked a direct question. None of it is on the page, and a moderator reads pages. A tutor who knows the criteria will spend the first few weeks mostly on writing and talking, which can feel to a parent like the art has stopped happening. It has not. The art was never the missing part, and saying so early saves an argument in February.
bullets: Criterion A: investigating practitioners, naming what was taken and rejected
Criterion B: developing skills through recorded, dated experiments
Criterion C: the making or the performance itself
Criterion D: evaluating honestly, including what the work failed to do

Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali and Borivali are all covered, with Metro Line 1 linking Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 running Dahisar to Gundavali. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts Wadala and Chembur closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests, which is why a few SoBo-based arts tutors will take an Eastern Suburbs evening.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai school calendars set the MYP arts deadlines?
paragraphs: The Mumbai IB school year runs roughly June to April, and MYP arts deadlines cluster in three places: a first summative task in August or September, an exhibition or performance window somewhere across October to December, and a final submission with written reflection in February or March. Your school's own assessment calendar is the only authority on the actual dates. Ask the arts teacher for it in June, and put the three clusters in a shared family calendar before anything else gets booked into those weeks.

Families using IB Gram have children at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School in Goregaon East (JVLR), Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, JBCN International School, Parel, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, NES International School in Mulund West and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools, or with the International Baccalaureate organisation. We name them because their calendars and their art rooms are what a tutor has to plan around, nothing more.

The pressure point most families miss is the October to November stretch, when a school arts exhibition, the Diwali break and the mid-year reporting cycle land on top of each other. A Year 5 student with a performance in the first week of November stops making new work for three weeks beforehand, and the journal entries stop with it. A tutor who has worked a Mumbai school year before will pull the written reflection forward into September so that November is only about the performance. IB home tuition in Mumbai is at its most useful in September, not in March, and that sequencing is worth more than extra hours in January.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online sessions or a mix for MYP arts in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tutoring leads for MYP arts because the work cannot travel. A half-finished canvas, a wet clay piece, a sketchbook with loose inserts and a practice pad do not go into an autorickshaw. An IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai sits where the work already is, sees the actual desk the child uses, and can tell inside ten minutes whether the problem is skill, time or a working surface that is too small. Home tuition also means the tutor meets the folder in its real state rather than the tidied version carried to a centre. Ask for a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai and we will come straight back asking which art form.

The practical questions at home are space, noise, neighbours and storage. In a two-bedroom flat in Chembur or a tower in Kandivali East the working surface is usually the dining table, which means everything comes out and goes away inside the session. Wet work needs a drying spot where nothing will be moved: the top of a cupboard, a spare chair, a balcony shelf out of the sun. Keep home practice to water-based and dry media, digital work and air-drying clay. Anything needing ventilation, heat or power tools, which includes kilns, solvents, spray and most casting, belongs in the school art room or workshop under the art teacher's supervision.

For music and drama the constraint is sound. Most Mumbai societies have quiet hours written into the rules and neighbours who enforce them earlier than the rules say. Practice mutes, electronic kits, headphone amplifiers and a short agreed window work better than a conversation with the secretary after a complaint has been logged. Drama students can do most of their text and character work quietly and save full-volume runs for the school hall. Tell the tutor the constraint on the first call so the session plan is built around it, rather than discovering it at seven on a Tuesday with a neighbour at the door.

Online carries the parts of arts that are talk: looking at photographed work, interrogating the thinking, planning the next piece, researching practitioners, reading a draft reflection. It does not carry physical technique, and a camera lies about scale, surface and colour. Hybrid is the honest default for most families here, with home sessions in the weeks when there is making to watch and online in the weeks when the work is written. A tutor who tells you everything works equally well through a screen is overselling, and we would rather lose a booking than let that stand.

sections.heading: How tutors are checked, and the line nobody crosses
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram gives us government photo identity, their degree or diploma certificates, and evidence for any teaching or examining claim they make. We speak to them about the subject before they are listed, and for arts that conversation is practical: we ask what they would do with a Year 4 folder holding strong drawing and three sentences of reflection. Claims we cannot check are removed rather than published with a hedge. A verified IB private tutor Mumbai families meet through us has been through the same checks whatever the art form, and you see the background before you speak to them.

The rule that matters most in arts is simple and is not negotiable. The work must be the student's own. A tutor may demonstrate a technique on their own paper, ask hard questions, critique what is in front of them and teach a skill the student has decided they need. A tutor may not draw into the work, retouch it, write or rewrite any part of the process journal or the artist's statement, choose the subject for the student, or supply research the student then presents as their own. Every artist, image or source used has to be credited in the journal by name and by where it was found.

Parents help most by not helping with the making. A piece a parent finished at eleven at night is a piece the student cannot write about honestly, and the written reflection is exactly where that surfaces. What is genuinely useful: protect the slot, keep the materials stocked, and sit in on the first session so you can hear how the tutor talks about the criteria. Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade, offers to produce sample work your child can copy, or wants to deal with the school on your behalf. None of those three are tutoring.

sections.heading: What makes a process journal count as assessed work?
paragraphs: A process journal counts as assessed work because it is the evidence of thinking that a finished piece cannot show on its own. It records what the student tried, what failed, what a work provoked in them, which decisions they took and why. A moderator reads it as an argument, not as decoration. It is not a scrapbook, and a page of washi tape with three pasted images under it carries less than a smudged page holding two sentences of real reasoning. An IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai spends more time on these pages than on any canvas.

Take the Khar West lino prints again. A scrapbook page shows the finished print and the words inspired by Japanese woodblock. A journal page shows a photograph of the second pull where the ink flooded the fine lines, one sentence saying the paper was too absorbent, a note of the paper she switched to, and a line about why the flooded print turned out more interesting than the clean one and what she decided to do about that. The second page takes four minutes to write. It is the whole difference between describing and reasoning, and it is the part no tutor is allowed to write for her.

Working regularly beats working in bursts, and the journal is where that becomes visible to someone else. Ten minutes at the end of each making session, dated, produces a record that reads as thinking in motion. A weekend of backfilling in February produces fourteen entries in the same pen, the same mood and the same handwriting pressure, and anyone who has read a hundred journals can tell. The fix is mechanical rather than motivational: the journal comes out before the materials go away, not after dinner, and the tutor builds that into the last ten minutes of every session.

The other thing a tutor works on is the join between research and the student's own making. Looking at an artist is not research until the student can say what they took and what they refused. A page on a printmaker is worth nothing if the next page does not show a drawing arguing with them. Every source has to be credited: the name, where the student saw it, and what it changed in their thinking. A journal that lifts an image without a credit is a problem no finished piece can repair, and it is far easier to credit as you go than to reconstruct it in March.
bullets: Date every entry and write it before the materials go away
Keep the failed experiment and say what it taught
Photograph work in progress, not only the finished piece

sections.heading: What should change after four weeks of MYP arts home tuition?
paragraphs: After four weeks you should see four dated journal entries you did not have to ask for, and your child should be able to answer the question what were you trying to do in this one without looking at you first. That is the whole four-week test. Nothing about the finished work needs to look different yet, and if a tutor is showing you markedly better finished pieces in the first month, ask carefully whose hands made them.

By the end of a term there should be a visible line of enquiry: three or four pieces that argue with each other rather than three unrelated exercises, and written reflection in the student's own voice, awkward sentences included. Across a full assessment cycle the realistic change is that the student can run the process without being driven through it: choose a question, find practitioners, test, record, make, and say what did not work. Some students get there within two terms and some use the whole Year 4 to Year 5 stretch, and both are ordinary.

We do not guarantee grades, and anyone in Mumbai who does is selling something other than tutoring. Outcomes depend on the school's standards, its moderation, the student's own hand and a year of work we see one hour of each week. If the tutor is not working out, tell us in week two or three rather than week ten: say specifically what is not happening, we talk to the tutor once, and if that does not fix it we move you to another tutor from the same shortlist without charging for the handover session.

sections.heading: Starting with an IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have four things ready before the first session: the process journal exactly as it is and untidied, two or three recent pieces including one the student dislikes, the school's current task sheet with its criteria wording, and the assessment calendar. The untidied journal is the important one. A tutor handed the cleaned-up version spends two weeks discovering what the real one would have shown in ten minutes, and those two weeks come out of September.

The first session is diagnostic and mostly conversation. The tutor will ask the student to talk through one piece from start to finish, will read two journal pages aloud and ask what each sentence is doing, and will usually set one small making task simply to watch the hands work. At the end you get a short plan in writing: what the next four weeks cover, what happens inside the sessions and what the student does between them.

Then the practical part. Agree a fixed weekly slot, because a moving slot is the most common reason arts tuition quietly fades out by November. Send the tutor's name and photograph to your society office so the gate pass is standing rather than argued at the intercom every week. Decide where wet work dries. Agree who buys materials, so nobody arrives to find nothing to work on.

If you are still comparing options, searches for the best IB tutor in Mumbai and for IB tutors near me Mumbai will hand you plenty of listings and very little that is checkable. Three questions sort them quickly: which art form do you actually teach, what have you taught at MYP, and what will you refuse to do to my child's work.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai actually teach?
faqs.answer: Technique, criteria and thinking, in that order of visibility and the reverse order of importance. An IB MYP arts home tutor in Mumbai will teach a skill the student has decided they need, such as cross-hatching, a breath technique or blocking a scene. Most of the hour goes on the parts that stay invisible in the finished piece: what the student was trying to do, why a decision was taken, what the next test should be, and how to write that down so a moderator can follow it. The tutor does not make any part of the work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Kharghar or Panvel for an evening arts session?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is already in Navi Mumbai. We match Kharghar and Panvel families node to node, with tutors living around Belapur, Nerul, Vashi or Kharghar itself, because a tutor crossing the Atal Setu or coming down the Sion-Panvel Highway from the island city twice a week will not hold the slot past the first month. Evening slots between six and eight are the busiest and go first, so ask early in the school year. Weekend mornings are easier to secure and often better for arts, since a longer session suits making.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy art materials before the first home session?
faqs.answer: No. Bring what your child already uses and nothing more. The first session is diagnostic, and the tutor needs to see the real working kit, including the brush that has lost its point and the sketchbook with torn pages. After that session the tutor gives you a short list tied to the current unit, usually three or four items. Materials for MYP arts are not expensive when bought to a purpose. The expensive version is a large set bought in advance and mostly unused, which also tells the tutor nothing useful about how your child works.

faqs.question: Our flat is small, so where should my child work at home?
faqs.answer: Pick one surface and one storage box, and keep both fixed. In most Mumbai flats that means a corner of the dining table plus a box that lives under a bed, which is enough for drawing, water-based painting, digital work and air-drying clay. The fixed part matters more than the size: a student who has to negotiate for space loses twenty minutes of every session and eventually stops starting. Find a drying spot out of the sun where nothing will be moved. Anything needing ventilation, heat or power tools stays in the school art room.

faqs.question: Is the process journal marked, or is it just preparation?
faqs.answer: It is assessed, not preparation. In MYP arts the journal is where the investigating and evaluating criteria are evidenced, so a student with strong finished work and a thin journal is presenting half the case. Your school's task sheet says how it wants the journal submitted, whether physical, digital or both, and that sheet is the authority. What the journal needs is dated entries written close to the work, failed experiments kept rather than removed, named sources, and sentences that say why rather than what. Four honest minutes after each session beats an hour of decoration.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help with the final piece if my child runs out of time?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the one request we turn down flatly. A tutor may not draw into the work, retouch it, rewrite the reflection or supply research the student presents as their own, whatever the deadline looks like. What a tutor can do when time is short is help the student cut the plan down to something they can genuinely finish, then write honestly about why the scope changed, which the evaluating criterion rewards far more than a rescued piece. A parent who finishes the making leaves a student with nothing of their own to reflect on.

faqs.question: How do society gate passes work for a weekly tutor slot?
faqs.answer: Most Mumbai societies issue a standing pass once you register the tutor in writing. Send the office the tutor's full name, photograph, phone number and the fixed day and time, and ask for a recurring entry rather than a visitor log entry every week. Complexes in Powai, Kharghar and along Ghodbunder Road in Thane tend to be the strictest and also the quickest once registered. Do this in the first week. The most common cause of a cancelled second session is a tutor standing at the gate while nobody answers the intercom.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for an arts tutor?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a number we cannot stand behind. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the programme and year, the scarcity of the art form, the tutor's teaching and examining background, the session length, and travel distance for home sessions. Performing arts specialists who can teach to MYP criteria are scarcer than visual arts tutors across most of the city, and scarcity moves a rate more than anything else does. Tutors quote directly and you agree the rate with them before the first session, so nothing sits hidden in the middle.

faqs.question: Will an online arts tutor work for a student in Thane or Mulund?
faqs.answer: For some of the work, yes. Online carries research, planning, questioning and the reading of written reflection perfectly well, and an IB online tutor in Mumbai can cover those weeks without anyone crossing Ghodbunder Road at seven in the evening. What online does not carry is physical technique and accurate judgement of scale, surface and colour through a camera. For a Thane or Mulund family the usual answer is hybrid: home sessions in the making weeks, online in the writing weeks. Anyone who tells you everything works online is overselling the format.

faqs.question: My child has not kept a process journal before. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with one page about the piece they are working on right now, not with a catch-up exercise. Have them photograph the current state, write three sentences saying what they were trying to do, what actually happened and what they will change, then date it. Repeat after every session. A journal that begins in Year 4 and is honest from that point reads better than one backfilled to look complete. The tutor builds the habit into the session structure so the writing happens before the materials go away.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and we replace them. Say specifically what is not happening, for example the journal is still empty, or the sessions have become drawing lessons with no reference to the criteria. We speak to the tutor once, because a fair number of these are fixable in a single conversation. If the next session does not change, we move you to another tutor from the same shortlist and you do not pay for a handover session. Three weeks is a sensible point to raise it; week ten is too late to change a term.

faqs.question: Does a tutor replace what the school art teacher does?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who behaves as though they do will cause problems. The school art teacher sets the unit, holds the criteria, supervises anything needing a workshop, and is the person whose judgement feeds the school's reporting. A tutor works alongside that: reinforcing technique, pressing on the thinking, and getting the journal written. We ask tutors not to contact the school, and never to tell a student their teacher is wrong about a task. Where there is a disagreement about what a task requires, the task sheet settles it.

sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups, and what Year 1 to Year 5 changes online
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans five years and eight subject groups: arts, design, sciences, mathematics, individuals and societies, language and literature, language acquisition, and physical and health education. Arts holds visual arts on one side and performing arts, meaning music, drama or dance, on the other. A student may carry one art form through all five years or sample several early on. Which art form it is matters far more online than the subject group label does, because a camera treats a drawing, a monologue and a keyboard motif completely differently.

Year by year, online suitability moves. A Year 1 or Year 2 student works best in short concrete blocks with a parent in the flat, and forty focused minutes is a full session. By Year 3 and Year 4 the enquiry has started, and this is where screen sessions earn their place: finding practitioners, arguing about them, planning the next test, writing it up. By Year 5 the written reflection carries the case to a moderator, and reading a draft together line by line is something a screen does as well as a room. The exceptions are the weeks before a performance or an exhibition, which need a hall and a teacher in it.

Two topics belong elsewhere. The Year 5 personal project is separate work with a school-appointed supervisor, and we cover it on its own page. Whether your school enters Year 5 students for MYP eAssessment or reports on internally moderated work is a school decision, and the MYP coordinator is the only person who can confirm it. Parents reach us through every phrasing going, from a MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai to MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai families describe in half a sentence, and our internal label reads MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai. The useful version is shorter: art form, year, unit.

sections.heading: Which MYP arts criteria a screen genuinely serves
paragraphs: MYP arts runs on four criteria labelled A to D: investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. Two of them are mostly language, and language travels down a wire intact. Investigating is reading, looking, arguing and recording. Evaluating is saying what the work failed to do and why. A screen serves both of those completely. Developing and creating are hands, posture, pressure and breath, and a screen serves them partially at best. Take the current band wording from your school's task sheet rather than from any summary, because the IB revises its subject guides on its own schedule.

A worked example from a Nerul family. A Year 3 student is building a two-bar motif on a keyboard and the tutor is joining from Andheri West. Over a phone microphone the tutor hears the notes, loses the dynamics, and cannot tell whether the unevenness is the player or the compression. What the tutor can still do is the part that gets marked: ask what the motif is supposed to make a listener feel, ask why the second bar repeats instead of answering, and get those two answers written into the process journal in the student's own words. The uneven touch is a problem for the music teacher in a room.

This split is the honest reason IB MYP arts online tuition in Mumbai is a good buy for some units and a poor one for others. A visual arts unit in its research fortnight is close to ideal online. The same unit in its final build week, where the student needs someone to watch how a brush is being held, is not. We will say which one you are in. A tutor who claims both weeks are equally served by a camera is either inexperienced or selling, and neither is useful to a fourteen-year-old with a submission date.
bullets: Criterion A: investigating, which is reading and arguing, carries fully online
Criterion B: developing skills, which a camera shows only partly
Criterion C: creating or performing, best watched in the same room
Criterion D: evaluating honestly, which a screen serves completely
Band descriptors come from the school task sheet, not from summaries

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai online sessions beat home tuition, and where they do not
paragraphs: IB Gram covers Mumbai, Maharashtra, and online changes the map most at the edges. A family on Ghodbunder Road in Thane, at Kasarvadavali or Majiwada or off Pokhran Road, has a small local pool of MYP arts specialists and an hour of traffic between them and anybody else. Panvel and Kharghar sit the same way at the other end. For those households an IB MYP arts online tutor in Mumbai is not a compromise, it is the only way to reach a drama or dance specialist at all, and the weekly session survives monsoon in a way a road-dependent one does not.

In South Mumbai the calculation is different. Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Fort, Babulnath, Tardeo and Peddar Road households are close to plenty of tutors, and the Coastal Road, Metro Line 3 and the Western Line from Churchgate keep them close. Here online tends to be used for the research and reflection weeks and home tuition for the making weeks. Across the Western Suburbs, from Juhu and Santacruz up through Andheri West, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar East, the Western Express Highway, Metro Line 1 and Metro Lines 2A and 7 make short hops easy and long ones punishing, so the mix tilts by how far north you are.

The Central Suburbs have their own quirk. Powai and Chandivali hang off the JVLR with no station, so a Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar tutor reaches them by road and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) decides whether a Kurla booking survives July. Online removes that entirely for the weeks it suits. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Wadala, Bhandup and Mulund are strung along the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Freeway and the Eastern Express Highway beside them, and families there often run one screen session midweek and one home session at the weekend.

Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines between them. The Atal Setu and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link have shortened some crossings on paper, but a tutor making either crossing twice a week in term time tends to stop by the second month. That is precisely the trip online deletes. We still ask every Navi Mumbai family whether a local tutor exists for the art form, because if one does, a home session beats a screen for the making weeks every time.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai school calendars shape an online arts schedule?
paragraphs: The Mumbai IB year runs roughly June to April, and three stretches shape an online arts schedule. June to September is research and planning, which is the strongest online period of the year. October to December carries exhibitions, concerts and the mid-year reporting cycle, when the student needs the school art room and the hall more than a screen. January to March is submission and reflection, where reading a draft together on a shared screen is worth more than another making hour. Your school's assessment calendar is the only source for the actual dates, so ask for it in June.

Families booking through IB Gram have children at Bombay International School in Babulnath, the Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, JBCN International School, Borivali, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any of these schools or with the International Baccalaureate organisation. We name them because their calendars and their device rules are what an online schedule has to fit around.

Two school-side details catch online families out. The first is device policy: several Mumbai schools keep student laptops managed, which can block screen sharing or a drawing app the tutor planned to use, so check before the first session rather than during it. The second is the February squeeze, when submission dates, mock weeks for older siblings and the family internet all collide at eight in the evening. Book the arts slot outside the peak if you can. A Saturday morning online session in February is calmer, longer and far more productive than a contested Tuesday at eight.
bullets: June to September: research and planning, the best online stretch

sections.heading: Online, home tuition and the hybrid most Mumbai families settle on
paragraphs: Online leads on this page because it is what you searched for, and it earns the lead in the research, critique and writing weeks. It also solves scarcity and traffic at once. What it cannot do is put a person next to the work. Most families who start with screen sessions end up on a hybrid within a term, and we would rather set that up deliberately in week one than let it happen by accident in November. Ask for a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai and we will quote the same shortlist, simply with travel in it.

Home tuition is the right call in three situations. The first is a making week, where a tutor needs to see pressure, grip, posture or breath. The second is a student in MYP Year 1 or Year 2 who disengages from a screen in twenty minutes and does not from a person. The third is a household where the only quiet corner is also the only place the router reaches, which is more common in Mumbai flats than anyone admits. An IB home tutor in Mumbai costs travel time, and that cost is worth paying for a fortnight rather than a year.

The hybrid pattern that holds is simple: one standing online slot every week for the thinking, plus a home session booked in blocks around the making weeks and the fortnight before a submission. The online slot keeps the journal moving all year. The home blocks fix technique when it needs fixing. IB home tuition in Mumbai booked this way costs less travel and loses less to traffic than a weekly home slot nobody can keep through monsoon, and the student never goes three weeks without being asked what they were trying to do.

One thing we will not do is pretend the modes are interchangeable to keep a booking. If a tutor tells you a technical problem can be solved on camera when it cannot, that is a bad tutor rather than a flexible one. Our tutors are asked to say plainly, in the session, when something needs a room. You will hear sentences like this one is a school art room problem, and that is the service working rather than failing.
bullets: Online leads for research, critique, planning and reflection drafting
Home sessions for making weeks, posture, grip, breath and pressure
Younger students often hold attention better with a person in the room
A standing online slot plus home blocks around submissions is the usual pattern
MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai families book run on the same shortlist
