faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Powai on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Powai is one of the areas where this is arranged most often. Powai has no railway station of its own, so tutors reach Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali and the lake-side complexes by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar using JVLR. That makes the time of day matter more than the distance. A six o'clock arrival from Andheri East is usually comfortable; a seven-thirty arrival in the same direction is not. We match Powai families with tutors who already live or teach on that corridor, and we ask you to fix one standing slot rather than moving it week to week.

faqs.question: What does home tuition for MYP individuals and societies actually cover in a session?
faqs.answer: A typical hour works on one real piece of the student's current coursework, not a parallel syllabus. The tutor usually opens with the research question, checks whether the student can state it and defend its size, then moves to whatever stage the work has reached: finding sources, evaluating two sources against each other, organising notes, or shaping an argument from evidence already gathered. Sessions close with one specific task for the week. What the hour does not contain is the tutor writing, dictating or supplying text for the assessed piece, which is a boundary set by MYP academic honesty expectations and by us.

faqs.question: Our society gate needs visitor approval. How does that work for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Arrange it once as a standing entry rather than as a fresh request every week. Most Mumbai housing societies allow a resident to register a recurring visitor with the gate or on the society's visitor app, usually with a name, a phone number and a photo identification reference. Tell us at matching time if your society requires this, because a tutor who is turned away once at the gate tends to become a tutor who reschedules. For societies with a stricter protocol, some families prefer sessions in the clubhouse study room, which also removes the question of who else is at home.

faqs.question: My child reads widely but still scores in the middle. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the issue is that the work describes rather than investigates. Individuals and societies rewards a question that can actually be answered, sources that have been weighed against each other, and a conclusion built from the evidence rather than chosen in advance. A well-read student often writes a confident summary of what happened and never shows the thinking the criteria are asking for. This is not a weakness in the child and it is not a sign of being behind. It is a specific skill nobody has taught yet, and it is the most common reason families book this kind of support.

faqs.question: Would an online session work as well as a home session in Kharghar?
faqs.answer: For an organised Year 4 or Year 5 student, often yes; for a Year 1 or Year 2 student, usually not. Online is genuinely strong for this subject because a tutor can share a screen, open a source beside the student's draft and comment next to the student's own sentences. Kharghar families gain from it in particular, since the pool of tutors who have marked MYP individuals and societies work is wider across the city than within the node. Many Navi Mumbai families run one home session a week with a short online check-in midweek, which keeps the travel sane and the sequence intact.

faqs.question: How many sources should a Year 3 investigation use?
faqs.answer: There is no universal number, and any tutor who gives you one without seeing the task sheet is guessing. The school's own task sheet and the current MYP subject guide set the expectation, and it varies by year group, by unit and by the kind of question. What is consistent is that range matters more than count: a student who has used a statistics table, a contemporary account and a piece of published scholarship has shown something a student with five similar websites has not. Ask the subject teacher or MYP coordinator for the expectation on that specific task.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help write the investigation itself?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the method, model an example on a different topic, question the student about their reasoning, mark a draft and give written feedback on it. A tutor may not write any part of the assessed work, supply sentences to be pasted in, build the bibliography or complete the reflection. The student signs an academic honesty declaration for this work and the signature has to be true. If a tutor offers to produce the piece, that is the point to end the arrangement, whatever the deadline pressure looks like that week.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we do not publish a price list because an honest one cannot exist. Rates move with the level, since MYP and Diploma Programme work are priced differently; with the scarcity of the specialism, as an experienced individuals and societies marker is rarer than a general humanities tutor; with session length and weekly frequency; with travel, as a tutor crossing from Bandra to Mulund is pricing an hour of road time; and with whether sessions are at home or online. Ask for the rate, the session length and the travel assumption together, in writing, before the first session.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Tell us at the four-week mark rather than waiting. First, check what you are measuring: in month one you should be looking for a stated research question, a reason for its scope and notes with references recorded as the student went, not for a higher grade. If those are absent, something is wrong with the match. Describe what specifically is not happening and a new shortlist comes back, usually within a few days. Changing a tutor in week five costs a fortnight; leaving it until month five costs a year of habits that never formed.

faqs.question: The tutor is good but the evening commute keeps cancelling sessions. Can we fix it?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth fixing rather than tolerating. The three worst evening corridors in Mumbai for this are Ghodbunder Road in Thane, the Western Express Highway north of Andheri, and the Peddar Road stretch in South Mumbai. Three fixes work: move the slot earlier or to a weekend morning, switch that session to online for the weeks it keeps failing, or rematch with a tutor on your own side of the corridor. A cancelled session every third week does more damage to this subject than a slightly less experienced tutor who actually arrives.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram promise a better grade?
faqs.answer: No. We do not guarantee grades, and we will not place a tutor who promises a specific grade to a family. What a tutor controls is one or two hours a week of method, feedback and practice. What a tutor does not control is the work done between sessions, the school's own marking, the student's other six subject groups, or how any given unit lands. We are an independent platform and not affiliated with any school named on this page. What we do commit to is a verified subject specialist, a clear first-session plan, and a replacement if the match is wrong.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist an individuals and societies online tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: The shortlist starts from a document, not a description. When a family asks for an IB MYP individuals and societies online tutor in Mumbai, the most useful thing in the first message is a photograph or scan of the last marked piece of work with the teacher's comments visible. Everything else follows from it: whether the school is teaching integrated humanities or split disciplines, which criteria the task was assessed against, what the teacher is already asking for, and whether the gap is in the research or in the writing. A sentence like "she needs help with history" sends us back asking for the same document a day later.

We then filter on three things in order. Specialism first, because individuals and societies spans history, geography, economics and civics and a tutor is rarely equally strong across all of them. Marking experience second: the tutor has to be able to open a draft, read it once, and tell you in plain words which criterion strand it is sitting under and why. Online teaching ability third, and this is a real skill rather than an assumption. A tutor who talks for fifty minutes to a camera is worse online than they are in a room. A tutor who gets the student to annotate the source on screen while they watch is better online than they are in a room, because you can both see the same words at the same moment.

A trial call comes before any booking. Ask the tutor what their screen looks like during a session, what the student will be doing with their hands for most of the hour, and what gets left behind at the end. The answers tell you a great deal. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not place a tutor who promises a specific grade to a twelve-year-old's parent. What the trial should establish is simpler: that your child spoke more than they listened, and that something written exists at the end that was not there at the start.

sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups and where a screen genuinely helps
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers Years 1 to 5 and divides learning into eight subject groups, of which individuals and societies is the one holding history, geography, economics and the social sciences. Across those eight groups, online support is not equally useful. A subject built on apparatus and a bench loses something on a screen. A subject built on reading documents, weighing them and writing about them loses almost nothing, because the raw material is already text and images that can sit side by side in a browser window. That is the honest reason this particular request works well online, and it is worth knowing before you pay for anything.

The assessment is organised around four criteria covering knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Three of those four are visible on a screen in a way that is hard to achieve across a table. When the tutor and the student both have the draft open, a comment can sit directly beside the sentence it refers to, and the student can see exactly which line triggered which remark instead of trying to map spoken feedback onto their page afterwards. An MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai working this way leaves a marked document behind that the student can reread on Thursday. Parents sometimes paste a long phrase into the search bar, something like "MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai", and this is the service behind it.

Year 5 brings the personal project, which is largely self-directed and therefore the point at which online support either proves itself or does not. A student who has been meeting a tutor weekly on a screen for two years has a working file, a habit of writing things down where someone else can see them, and someone to show a plan to. A student who has only ever been told things in person has notes nobody has read. There is no single correct number of sessions or hours here; what your school expects of the personal project is set out in its own guidance and the current subject guide, so ask the MYP coordinator rather than a forum.

sections.heading: Evaluating a source together on one shared screen
paragraphs: Here is what a strong online hour actually looks like. The tutor puts a source on screen, a photograph of a public notice, a page of census figures, a newspaper column from the period, and gives the student control of the pointer. The student is asked who made this, for whom, when, and what it would be good evidence of. Not whether it is reliable, which is the question that produces the empty answer, but what it is good evidence of, which produces a real one. A statistics table is good evidence of what an administration chose to count. A memoir is good evidence of how one person remembered something. Both are useful and neither is a verdict.

The screen earns its place at the next step, which is annotation. The student highlights the phrase that tells them who the audience was and types one line next to it. The tutor watches it happen live and can stop the pointer at the moment the student skips a step. Across a table, the tutor sees a finished annotation and has to guess at the thinking. On a shared document, the thinking is visible in real time, and that is where the useful interruption happens. By the fourth or fifth source most students stop needing the prompt questions and start asking them unprompted, which is the whole point of the exercise.

There is a care point in this subject that matters more at thirteen than at seventeen. Many topics in individuals and societies are ones where historians and economists genuinely disagree, and some touch on history, religion and community questions where families and communities hold strongly different views. A tutor's job is not to hand a student a conclusion on any of that. It is to teach them to say who argues what, on what evidence, and where the disagreement actually sits, and then to let the student reason in their own voice. Students who learn to represent a disagreement fairly score better on the thinking criterion than students who learn to argue hard for one side, and they are also being taught something worth having.

sections.heading: Online sessions and home tuition across the six zones of Mumbai
paragraphs: Online removes most of the geography problem, which is why so many families reach for it, but it does not remove all of it and the remaining part is worth naming. Matching an IB MYP individuals and societies online tutor in Mumbai, Maharashtra means the tutor can live anywhere in the city, so a family in Panvel is choosing from the same pool as a family in Bandra. In South Mumbai, where parents around Napean Sea Road, Breach Candy, Marine Lines, Colaba and Lower Parel are used to short distances and long signal waits on Peddar Road, online usually replaces an evening that was being lost to the Coastal Road and the Western Line between Churchgate and Mumbai Central anyway.

In the Western Suburbs the gain is largest for families off the main spine. Versova, Oshiwara, Goregaon West, Vile Parle and Jogeshwari sit awkwardly for tutors travelling the Western Express Highway or the Link Road, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 only help those near a station. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali have no station of their own and are reached by road along JVLR from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, so a seven o'clock online slot is often the only version of a seven o'clock session that reliably happens. The Santacruz Chembur Link Road helps a Kurla match in daylight and not much after it.

The Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West, are served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway towards Wadala. Navi Mumbai families in Airoli, Vashi, Seawoods, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel gain most of all, since the Atal Setu and Palm Beach Road have improved crossings without making a weekday island-to-node commute pleasant. In Thane, Ghodbunder Road between the station, Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Kolshet and Kasarvadavali decides everything, and the online slot simply sidesteps it. Families who search IB tutors near me Mumbai are often better served by widening the pool than by shrinking the radius. Even so, a great many of these households run MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai tutors deliver in person once a week, with the screen covering the second session.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai school year does to an online schedule
paragraphs: Mumbai international schools mostly run June to April, and an online schedule meets that calendar differently from a home one. June and July are the easy months, when a weekly slot is simple to hold and the tutor can work on method. From late July the first summative tasks arrive and the slot starts competing with everything else. The heavy stretch runs October to November, then again in February and March, when final unit work and, in Year 5, the personal project exhibition land close together. The useful thing about an online arrangement is that an extra half hour can be added in a crowded week without anyone crossing the city for it.

The schools generate their own rhythms. Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School at Goregaon East on JVLR both run the Primary Years Programme, MYP and Diploma Programme, so their MYP calendars are built as preparation for Diploma Programme work. Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Chembur, Singapore International School in Dahisar East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai sit on IB or Cambridge International Education pathways and set their own submission weeks. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools. They are named here because their calendars are what families are scheduling around.

Monsoon is the part no planning document mentions and every Mumbai parent knows. Between June and September, a heavy afternoon can close a school early, flood a stretch of the Western Express Highway or the Sion Panvel Highway, and remove a weekday evening entirely. An online slot survives most of that, with the honest exception of a power or connectivity failure at either end. The practical fix families use is an agreed fallback: if the link drops for more than a few minutes, the session moves to a named slot later that week rather than being written off. Agreeing that once at the start saves a term of small negotiations.

sections.heading: Online, home classes or both for a Year 4 student?
paragraphs: Take home tuition seriously before choosing online, because for the younger end of the MYP it is often the better buy. A Year 1 or Year 2 student left with a laptop and a research task will drift within ten minutes, and an adult in the room is the cheapest attention mechanism ever invented. IB home tuition in Mumbai for this subject typically runs as one weekly session at the family's table, with the tutor arriving with the task sheet already read. An IB home tutor in Mumbai also sees things a camera does not: a student who has not opened the file all week, a notebook with nothing in it, a phone face-up beside the laptop.

Online becomes the stronger option from around Year 3 upwards, and the advantages are specific rather than general. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can pull up an archive page, a data table and the student's draft in three windows and move between them in seconds. Feedback lands as comments inside the document instead of as remarks the student has to remember. The pool of tutors who have actually marked MYP individuals and societies work is far larger citywide than within any one node, which matters most in Panvel, Dahisar East or Kasarvadavali. Recording a session, where the tutor agrees to it, gives the student something to rewatch before a deadline.

Most families who stay the course end up hybrid, and the usual shape is one longer session in person and one short screen session midweek. The in-person hour does the teaching; the midweek twenty minutes checks that the notes exist and that the question has not quietly drifted back to being enormous. There is one counterweight worth stating plainly. A good deal of MYP assessed work is still produced by hand, under supervision, in class. A student who has only ever written in a document with autocorrect and a tutor's comments alongside can be slower and less fluent on paper. Ask any online tutor how they build handwritten practice into the term, and treat a vague answer as a real answer.

sections.heading: How is an online tutor checked, and what should you watch yourself?
paragraphs: Every tutor is verified before a family sees a profile, and the checks are the same whether they teach on a screen or at your table. Identity is confirmed against government photo identification. Degrees and teaching qualifications are checked against the documents. The subject interview is the part that filters hardest: the candidate is given a sample MYP investigation and asked to mark it against the criteria and justify each judgement out loud. Online candidates get one extra step, a live screen-share task, because the ability to run a document, a source and a conversation at once is not something you can infer from a CV. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents find through a building group has usually had none of this.

Online teaching also has a supervision dimension that in-person teaching does not, and it matters because MYP students are young. Sessions should happen in a shared family space rather than behind a closed bedroom door. The parent's contact details, not only the student's, should be on the booking. Communication between tutor and student belongs on the channel the family can see, not on a personal messaging app. These are ordinary precautions for a twelve- or thirteen-year-old and a reasonable tutor will expect them rather than resent them.

Then there is the checking only you can do, and the simplest version is to walk past twice. Once in the first ten minutes, to hear whether the student is talking. Once near the end, to see whether something is being written. Ask your child after a fortnight to explain their current research question without looking at anything. Look at the shared document yourself and see whose sentences are in it. A tutor may teach, model, question and mark, and may never write, dictate or supply any part of assessed work. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade; IB Gram does not guarantee grades and neither should anyone working through us.

sections.heading: The shared file of sources and arguments that grows across the year
paragraphs: The single most useful artefact an online arrangement produces is a file that nobody has to carry. One shared document, opened in the first session and still open in April, with a row for every source the student has used: where it came from, what it is good evidence of, which unit it belonged to, and one line in the student's own words about what it showed. It takes two minutes per source and it compounds. By February a Year 4 student has a reference list that already exists, a record of what they thought at the time, and something to show a teacher when asked how the research was done.

That file is also where an IB MYP individuals and societies online tutor in Mumbai does the quiet work that a weekly hour alone cannot. Between sessions the tutor can leave a comment on a half-finished row. The student can drop a link in during the week and get one line back. None of that is a lesson and none of it is billed as one, but it keeps the thread alive across six days instead of restarting from cold every Tuesday. The rule that makes it work is mechanical: the reference goes in before the note, every time, from the first source of the year.

The second half of the file is the argument column, kept deliberately apart from the evidence column. Students at this age collect a position early and then shop for quotations that support it. Splitting the document stops that happening by making it visible: on one side what the source says, on the other what the student thinks it means, and the gap between them is where the thinking criterion lives. A tutor working on screen can sort, colour and reorder those rows in front of the student, which is a conversation that is genuinely hard to have on paper.

The last thing the file teaches is how to search rather than how to receive. A twelve-year-old asked to research anything will type the essay title into a search bar and take the first three results, or paste the question into a chatbot and accept the paragraph it returns. A tutor sitting on a shared screen can stop that in the moment: try three different phrasings, show why a library catalogue and a newspaper archive return different things, show what a results page looks like when the search term is too broad. An IB tutor Mumbai families hire for this subject is partly being hired to teach a research method that the student will still be using in the Extended Essay four years later.

sections.heading: Keeping a thirteen-year-old producing in a short block
paragraphs: Attention is the real constraint online, not teaching quality, and the fix is structural. A sixty-minute screen session for a Year 3 student works far better split into two or three blocks with a visible output at the end of each: a research question rewritten, one source annotated, one paragraph restructured. The student should know at the start of each block what will exist at the end of it. Tutors who run this way report fewer lost sessions than tutors who plan an hour as a single stretch, and students stop asking how long is left, because the answer is always the length of the current block.

At four weeks, judge the arrangement on outputs and not on marks. The student should be able to state their research question unprompted, point to two sources in the shared file and say what each is good for, and show something written that they produced during a session. No summative grade will usually have moved in that window, because in most Mumbai schools nothing will have been marked yet. At one term, compare the teacher's comments on two successive investigations. Movement tends to show in the investigating and thinking criteria first, because those respond to method, and in communication later, because writing improves slowly at any age.

The limits are worth stating. A tutor controls an hour or two a week and controls nothing about what happens between Wednesday and Sunday. Students move at different speeds, which is normal and not a judgement on any child. A Year 2 student and a Year 5 student are different situations with different timelines. Connectivity will fail sometimes. Some of what looks like a subject problem is a sleep problem or a timetable problem and a tutor will usually say so if asked directly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a service that did would be selling you something it cannot deliver.

If it is not working, four weeks is enough to know and the signals are easy to read. The student cannot say what last week covered. The shared file has not changed. Sessions have drifted into the tutor talking while the student listens. Tell us what specifically is wrong and a replacement shortlist comes back, usually within a few days, and the new tutor is given the shared file so nothing restarts from zero. Changing at week five costs a fortnight. Leaving it until February costs the term.

sections.heading: Booking an online or home tutor for MYP in Mumbai
paragraphs: Start with three attachments and two sentences. The attachments are the last marked piece of individuals and societies work with comments, the current task sheet if one exists, and the school timetable if the student has free periods worth using. The two sentences say the year group and school, and what you have actually noticed at home: that the work is being finished suspiciously fast, that the research question keeps changing, that the writing describes rather than argues. A request for a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai parents can also run partly online begins with exactly the same material.

Then settle the practical side before the first session rather than after it. Agree the platform and check it works on the device the student will actually use, which is often a school-issued laptop with restrictions on it. Decide where in the house the sessions happen, in a shared room rather than a bedroom. Fix the fallback slot for a dropped connection. Confirm whether sessions are recorded and who may watch them. Families who also want in-person work should say which zone they are in at this point, because the home tuition side of the match is geographic even when the online side is not.

The trial session has a fixed shape and you should expect it. The tutor reads the marked work beforehand, opens with the student's own task rather than a test, shares a screen both ways, and finishes by sending you two short paragraphs: what the student can already do, and what the next four sessions will cover. You decide afterwards whether to continue. If you would rather not, say so and a different shortlist comes back. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school, and we do not guarantee grades.

On cost, which is usually the second question: no figure appears on this page because no honest figure could. What you pay moves with the year group and level, with how scarce the specialism is, with session length and weekly frequency, and with travel where any part of the arrangement is in person. Online sessions carry no travel component, which is one of the reasons families in Panvel, Kasarvadavali and Dahisar East choose them. Ask for rate, length and any travel assumption in writing before you begin.

faqs.question: Does online really work for a thirteen-year-old, or should we book home classes instead?
faqs.answer: It works from about Year 3 upwards if the session is structured in short blocks with something written at the end of each. Below that, home tuition is usually the better choice, because a twelve-year-old with a laptop and a research task needs an adult in the room more than they need a better explanation. The difference is not teaching quality, it is attention. Ask any prospective online tutor how they break up an hour and what the student will have produced by the end of it. A vague answer to that question is the most reliable warning sign available to you.

faqs.question: Can we mix online sessions with a tutor who travels to our home in Chembur?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common arrangement families settle into. The usual pattern is one longer in-person session at home each week plus a short midweek screen check of twenty to thirty minutes. For Chembur that works particularly well, because tutors reach you along the Eastern Express Highway, the Harbour Line and the Eastern Freeway comfortably in daylight and far less comfortably at seven in the evening. Tell us at matching time that you want both, since the in-person half of the match is geographic and the online half is not, and we shortlist for the tighter constraint first.

faqs.question: Our building has poor connectivity in the evening. What happens to a dropped session?
faqs.answer: Agree a named fallback slot in the first week and the problem mostly disappears. The standard arrangement is that if the connection fails for more than a few minutes, the session moves to a fixed alternative time later in the same week rather than being counted as delivered or lost. Mumbai monsoon evenings between June and September are the usual culprit, along with power interruptions at either end. If the failures become weekly, that is a signal to move the slot to a morning or to switch to home tuition, and either change can be made without starting the match again.

faqs.question: My child enjoys the reading but the marks sit in the middle. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because the writing describes what happened instead of investigating a question. Individuals and societies rewards a question narrow enough to answer, sources weighed against each other, and a conclusion assembled from evidence rather than decided in advance. A student who reads widely often produces a confident summary and never shows the reasoning the criteria are looking for. This is a skill gap, not a sign that anything is wrong with your child, and it is the most common reason families book this subject. It tends to respond quickly once someone names it.

faqs.question: Will the tutor write any part of the investigation?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach method, model an example on a different topic, question the student about their reasoning, mark a draft and leave written feedback on it. A tutor may not write sentences for the assessed piece, dictate text, build the bibliography or complete the reflection. On a shared document this boundary is easier to police than on paper, because you can see version history and you can see whose comments are whose. If any tutor offers to produce the work, end the arrangement that day regardless of what the deadline looks like.

faqs.question: How do we stop a student just pasting the question into a chatbot?
faqs.answer: Teach searching as a visible skill during sessions rather than banning anything. A tutor sharing a screen can have the student try three different phrasings of the same query, compare what a library catalogue returns against a general search, and look at why a results page changes when the question is narrowed. Then the shared file requires a line in the student's own words about what each source showed, which a pasted paragraph cannot supply. Schools treat unacknowledged use of generated text as an academic honesty matter, so this is worth building into the habit early rather than policing later.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the Year 5 personal project?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of a screen, because the personal project is largely self-directed and what a student needs most is someone to show a plan to each week. The tutor can review the process journal, question the goal, check that the product and the research are actually connected, and keep the record of sources honest. What the tutor cannot do is contribute to the product or write the report. Your school's own personal project guidance sets the requirements and timelines, so work from that document rather than from general advice.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for online sessions?
faqs.answer: Four factors, and we publish no price list because an honest one cannot exist. Rates move with the year group and level, since MYP and Diploma Programme work are priced differently. They move with scarcity, as a tutor who has genuinely marked MYP individuals and societies work is rarer than a general humanities tutor. They move with session length and weekly frequency. Travel is the fourth, and online removes it, which is usually the main reason an online rate differs from a home rate for the same tutor. Ask for all of it in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Is a recorded session something we should ask for?
faqs.answer: Ask, but treat it as optional rather than essential. Recordings help a student revisit a source evaluation before a deadline and help a parent understand what is actually being taught, which is harder to judge online than across a room. Not every tutor agrees to being recorded and that is a reasonable position. If recordings are made, agree who holds them, where they are stored and for how long, and keep them inside the family. For a student in Year 1 or Year 2 in particular, a shared family space and a parent within earshot matter more than any recording does.

faqs.question: There has been no change after a month of online tutoring. What now?
faqs.answer: Tell us at four weeks rather than waiting for a report card. First check what you are measuring: in month one, look for a stated research question, two annotated sources in the shared file and something written during a session, not for a higher grade. If those are missing, the match is wrong. Describe exactly what is not happening and a new shortlist comes back within a few days, and the shared file goes to the next tutor so nothing is lost. Changing in week five costs a fortnight. Changing in February costs the term.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram promise my child will score higher?
faqs.answer: No. We do not guarantee grades, and we will not list a tutor who promises a specific grade to a parent. A tutor controls one or two structured hours a week. A tutor does not control the work done between sessions, the school's own marking, the other seven MYP subject groups competing for the same evenings, or how a particular unit happens to land. We are an independent platform and are not affiliated with any school named here. What we do commit to is a verified specialist, a trial session on real work, and a replacement if the fit is wrong.

sections.heading: Where individuals and societies sits among the eight MYP subject groups
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across Years 1 to 5 and organises learning into eight subject groups. Individuals and societies is the group that carries history, geography, economics, civics and the social sciences, usually taught as an integrated course in the early years and increasingly as distinct strands later. It sits between the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), and it is where students first meet formal research expectations.

What makes this group distinctive is that it is assessed on a research process rather than on recall of content. Students are asked to investigate a question, find and evaluate sources, organise information, construct an argument supported by evidence, and reflect on the process. The marking criteria have letters rather than topic names for exactly that reason, and the wording of those criteria is revised by the IB on its own cycle, so your school's MYP coordinator and the current subject guide are the authority on structure rather than anything quoted on a tutoring page.

The research skills built here are also what the Year 5 personal project draws on, and later what Diploma Programme coursework assumes a student already has. A student who learns to evaluate a source properly in Year 2 is doing work that pays off repeatedly. A student who gets through the Middle Years Programme on fluent writing and good general knowledge usually hits the wall later, at the point where fluency stops being enough.

An IB home tutor in Mumbai working in this group should therefore spend very little time delivering content. The content is in the textbook and the student can read. What needs teaching is the method, and the method is invisible to most students until somebody makes it explicit.

sections.heading: Source evaluation, taught before anything else
paragraphs: The first thing a competent tutor teaches in this subject is how to interrogate a source, and it is taught early because everything else depends on it. A student who cannot ask where a piece of information came from will keep writing confident essays built on whatever the first search result said. The method is a short set of questions and it can be learned at eleven: who made this, when, for whom, what were they in a position to know, what would they have wanted the reader to think, and what does it leave out.

The useful teaching move is to put two sources side by side that disagree, and to resist the urge to say which is right. A factory owner's account of a working day and a worker's account of the same day will differ. The task is not to decide who was the better person. The task is to notice that each had access to different information and different reasons to emphasise different things, and to say what each source is good evidence for. A worker's testimony is strong evidence about how the day felt and weak evidence about company-wide output. That sentence, in a student's own words, is the skill.

The same discipline applies to numbers, which students treat as neutral and are not. A figure has a collector, a definition and a date. A survey has a sample and a question wording. Students who learn to ask who counted this, and how they decided what to count, stop writing sentences that begin with the word statistics as though that settled anything.

None of this requires a tutor to hold a position on anything contested. People disagree about history, about religion and about public questions, often sincerely and on the basis of different evidence and different values. The job of a tutor in individuals and societies is to teach a student how to describe a disagreement accurately, identify what each side treats as evidence, and write about it without pretending the disagreement does not exist. A tutor who uses these sessions to push an opinion is doing the subject harm, and we treat that as a removal issue.

sections.heading: Home tuition and online coverage across the six zones of Mumbai
paragraphs: An IB MYP individuals and societies tutor in Mumbai is not distributed across the city the way a science tutor is, and families notice it as soon as they start calling around Mumbai, Maharashtra. In South Mumbai the supply is comfortable: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Malabar Hill and Worli are well served, partly because of the concentration of IB and IGCSE schools on the island and partly because the Western Line and Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and BKC make short internal journeys workable. Home classes here are usually straightforward to arrange, allowing for the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak.

The Western Suburbs are the deepest pool in the city. Bandra, Khar, Santacruz, Juhu, Vile Parle, Andheri and Goregaon all have specialists, and matching works best along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway rather than across them. North of Malad, through Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar, a dedicated individuals and societies specialist is harder to find within a reasonable radius even with Metro Lines 2A and 7 open, so families there often run online sessions on weekdays and home tuition at the weekend.

In the Central and Eastern Suburbs the practical constraint is study space more than travel. Powai and Chandivali sit off JVLR with no station of their own, reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar; Kurla, Vikhroli, Chembur, Govandi, Bhandup and Mulund run along the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway shortening the Chembur and Wadala run into town. sections.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid for a research-based MYP subject?
paragraphs: Home tuition has a specific advantage in this subject that it does not have in maths: the tutor can see the research the student has actually gathered. The open tabs, the printed article with nothing underlined, the notebook with three facts copied out in full sentences. Most young students doing research are collecting rather than selecting, and the collecting is physically visible on a table. An IB home tutor in Mumbai spots that in the first ten minutes. On a screen, the student shows the tutor only the finished paragraph.

Home classes also help with the single most common failure mode, which is a student who reads for an hour and writes nothing. Having an adult in the room saying write one sentence about that now, before you read anything else, changes the hour completely. That intervention is harder to deliver over video because the tutor cannot see what the student is actually doing between sentences.

Online is genuinely strong for the marking half of the work. A shared document where the tutor watches an argument being typed, comments in the margin and asks why a sentence claims more than its evidence supports is an excellent teaching environment, and it is quick to arrange in a deadline week. For families north of Malad, in Kharghar or beyond Majiwada on Ghodbunder Road, an IB online tutor in Mumbai with real humanities depth beats a nearer generalist who treats the subject as general knowledge, and an IB MYP individuals and societies tutor in Mumbai working by screen is a better buy than a science graduate taking the subject on.

Most families end up hybrid: home tuition in Mumbai for the research and planning sessions where physical materials matter, online sessions for drafting and marking. Whichever mode you pick, the boundary is identical. A tutor may question, explain, teach method and mark practice work, and must never write, draft or supply any part of work submitted for assessment. In a subject assessed on writing, that line is easy to blur and we state it in writing to every tutor.

sections.heading: How is a humanities tutor in Mumbai checked, and what should you ask?
paragraphs: Identity, qualification and subject history are verified before any profile reaches a family, and for this group we add two checks. The first is whether the tutor has taught the Middle Years Programme rather than only Diploma Programme history or economics, because the MYP research process is a teaching problem of its own and a strong DP teacher may skip the step a Year 2 student is stuck on. The second is how the tutor handles disagreement, which we ask about directly.

That second check deserves explaining. In individuals and societies a tutor will meet contested questions about history, religion and public life every term. The correct professional stance is to teach the student how to describe a disagreement accurately, identify what each side counts as evidence, and write about it fairly. It is not the tutor's role to tell a child what to conclude. An IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for years is someone whose instinct is to ask the student what the evidence supports, not to supply a verdict. We ask every IB MYP individuals and societies tutor in Mumbai how they would handle that moment, and the answer is usually decisive.

Your own checks are quick. Ask the tutor how they would teach a student to evaluate a source, and listen for a method rather than an adjective. Ask what they do when a student's essay is fluent and unsupported, which is the commonest version of the problem. Ask how they handle a topic where reasonable people disagree. And ask what they will not do: the answer should name assessed work explicitly, without hedging.

Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade, offers to draft a submission, or describes the subject as easy marks for a student who reads a lot. That last one is the tell. A tutor who thinks individuals and societies rewards general knowledge has not understood what is being marked and will spend your money teaching content the student could have read.

sections.heading: Describing, explaining and arguing: three levels a young student writes at
paragraphs: Almost every piece of weak writing in this subject can be placed on a three-step ladder, and naming the step out loud is the fastest diagnostic a tutor has. Description says what happened: the population of the area increased. Explanation says why, with a mechanism: the population increased because work was available and transport made daily travel possible. Argument says what follows and defends it against an alternative: the available work mattered more than the transport, because the increase began before the line opened.

Students arrive fluent at level one and are marked as though they are at level three, which is why so many of them feel the marking is unfair. They wrote a lot, it was accurate, and it scored poorly. The honest explanation to give a thirteen-year-old is that the marks are not for how much you know, they are for what you did with it, and the gap between those two things is the whole subject.

Moving a student up the ladder is mechanical and it works. Take one of their own descriptive sentences and ask why until a mechanism appears, then make them write the mechanism down in their own words. Then ask what someone who disagreed would say, and make them write that too, with the evidence that person would point to. Most students can produce a genuine level-three paragraph within two or three sessions of this. What takes longer is doing it without being prompted.

The reason opinions without support score so poorly is the same reason the ladder exists. An unsupported opinion is a conclusion with the working removed, and the working is what is being assessed. A student who writes that a policy was unfair has asserted a conclusion. A student who writes that two sources describe different outcomes for different groups, names which source says what, and then says which group the evidence suggests bore the cost, has shown their reasoning. The second student may reach a more cautious conclusion and will score better for it.

This is also the thing a tutor should diagnose first, before touching content, structure or vocabulary. Ask the student to read their own paragraph and say which of the three levels each sentence is at. Students who can do that labelling, even hesitantly, usually fix themselves fast. Students who cannot see the difference need the ladder taught explicitly, and that is a six-week job rather than a one-session job.

sections.heading: What progress in a research subject looks like at four weeks and one term
paragraphs: At four weeks the marker worth watching is what your child does when handed something to read. A student who has had four sessions on source evaluation starts asking out loud who wrote this and when, sometimes irritatingly. That habit is the whole early gain and it will not appear on any report. It is also the step that makes every later improvement possible, so judging the tutoring by the September grade is judging it before anything measurable could have happened.

By the end of a term the writing should carry evidence inside the sentences rather than in a list at the end. You should see the word because doing real work, a paragraph that names an alternative view and answers it, and research notes that select rather than copy. A reliable test at home: ask your child to explain their argument in three sentences without reading. A student who can do it has an argument. A student who can only read it aloud has a collection of facts arranged attractively.

Across a full year the payoff shows in the Year 5 personal project and in how the student handles any unfamiliar question, which is the point of teaching method rather than content. Report grades usually lag the visible skill by a reporting cycle, because a report averages work produced before the sessions began.

What will not happen: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade. An IB MYP individuals and societies tutor in Mumbai can teach a student to interrogate a source, to explain rather than describe and to defend a claim. A tutor cannot read for the student, cannot submit on their behalf and cannot write any part of the assessed work. If a student is doing nothing between sessions, six weeks of good teaching will make that visible, which is unwelcome but useful information to have in September rather than in February.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP individuals and societies tutor in Mumbai actually teach?
faqs.answer: Method, not content. An IB MYP individuals and societies tutor in Mumbai spends sessions on how to evaluate a source, how to turn a description into an explanation, how to build an argument that answers an alternative view, and how to choose a research question that can actually be answered. The topic in the textbook is something your child can read. What is being marked is what they did with it, and that is invisible to most students until a tutor names it. Content gaps get filled along the way, but they are rarely the reason a student is stuck.

faqs.question: My child writes a lot and still scores poorly. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the writing is description where explanation or argument was required. Saying what happened, accurately and at length, is the level most students arrive at and the level that scores lowest. The fix is mechanical: take one of their sentences, ask why until a mechanism appears, make them write the mechanism down, then ask what someone who disagreed would say and make them write that too with its evidence. Most students can produce a properly argued paragraph within a few sessions. Doing it unprompted takes longer, usually a term.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help write the research assignment?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may question, explain, teach method and mark practice work, but must never write, draft, rewrite or supply any part of work your child submits for assessment. In a subject assessed almost entirely on writing, that line is easy to blur and we state it in writing to every tutor and every family. What a tutor can legitimately do is mark an earlier draft the way a teacher would, explain why a sentence claims more than its evidence supports, and send the student back to rewrite it in their own words. Report any tutor who offers otherwise.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for this subject?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them is a published rate we could quote honestly. Level, since Middle Years Programme work usually sits below Diploma Programme teaching. Scarcity, which matters more here than in the sciences because humanities specialists are unevenly spread across the city. Travel, since an evening crossing of Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway is priced into the hour. And session length and frequency. Online sessions remove the travel component. Ask for a range at shortlist stage and compare the same session length across tutors.

faqs.question: How will a tutor handle a topic where people strongly disagree?
faqs.answer: By teaching your child to describe the disagreement accurately rather than by picking a side. Reasonable people differ about history, about religion and about public questions, often sincerely and on the basis of different evidence and different values. The skill being assessed is the ability to say what each side treats as evidence, what each source is in a position to know, and what a careful conclusion would and would not claim. A tutor who uses sessions to push a personal opinion is doing the subject active harm, and we treat it as grounds for removal from the platform.

faqs.question: Is online as good as home tuition for research skills?
faqs.answer: For drafting and marking, online is genuinely excellent, because a shared document lets the tutor watch an argument being built and comment at the exact sentence where it overreaches. For the research stage, home classes have the edge, since the tutor can see the printed article with nothing underlined and the notebook with three facts copied out whole. Most families run both: home tuition for planning and research, online for drafting weeks and deadline crunches. North of Malad and beyond Majiwada, online is often the better of the realistic options.

faqs.question: My child picked a research question that cannot be answered. What now?
faqs.answer: Change it early, which is the single most valuable thing a tutor does in the first fortnight. Questions like whether a policy was good have no answerable shape, because nothing can be gathered that settles them. A question about what changed for a specific group, in a specific place, over a specific period, with sources that exist, can be investigated. Rewriting the question takes one session and saves four. If the school has already approved the question, the tutor works with the teacher's framing rather than around it.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, and you do not need to build a case. Fit in humanities is specific: some tutors are excellent at content and poor at coaxing a vague paragraph into an argument, which is nobody's fault but is not what you are paying for. One sentence about what was not working changes who we shortlist next. The replacement begins with the same diagnostic session on your child's own writing, so you are not paying twice for an hour of orientation. Most mismatches are visible by the third session.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the house, though not in the room. For Middle Years Programme students we ask that home tuition happens in a shared space such as a dining area or study, with the door open and a parent or another adult at home. That is standard practice for a younger student and no reasonable tutor objects to it. Sitting inside the session tends to make a thirteen-year-old perform rather than think, and in a subject where the student has to risk a wrong answer out loud, that costs more than it gains.

sections.heading: Where Language Acquisition sits in the MYP, Years 1 to 5
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs across Years 1 to 5, usually from about age eleven to sixteen, and every student studies eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Language Acquisition is the group for a language the student is learning in addition to their strongest school language. It is a separate subject from Language and Literature, and the two are marked against different criteria with different expectations, which is why a child who is a confident reader in English can still find the Language Acquisition writing task hard.

A MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai may cover several of those eight groups for one student; this page is about the language one on its own. Families who want MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai wide, taking in Mathematics and Sciences as well as a language, are usually better served by a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai siblings can share, booked as a block. Our own internal listing line for that is the unlovely "MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai", and all it means is a tutor cleared to teach more than one group across the five MYP years. For Language Acquisition specifically, we prefer a specialist, because criterion marking in a language is not a skill that transfers from a Physics classroom.

MYP marking is criterion-based. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each with its own published descriptors, and schools report them separately instead of collapsing everything into one percentage. This is the single most useful thing a parent can understand about the programme. When a report shows three strong criteria and one weak one, that is not a mixed signal. It is a precise instruction about where the next term of work should go. A tutor who treats all four criteria as one undifferentiated subject wastes most of the hour.

Year 5 adds the personal project, an independent piece of work with its own supervision and its own deadlines, and it lands in the same months as the heaviest language assessment of the MYP. Families underestimate this collision every year. A Year 5 student in Powai who is also preparing a Language Acquisition oral in the same fortnight as a personal project checkpoint is not disorganised when things slip. The calendar genuinely stacks.

Phase placement, and whether a student sits Language Acquisition or Language and Literature at all, is a decision the school makes with the family. A tutor can describe what each course asks for and can tell you honestly what the workload looks like, but the recommendation belongs to the MYP coordinator who knows your child's work. Ask for the current subject guide at that conversation rather than relying on anything written online, including this page.

sections.heading: What does MYP Language Acquisition actually assess?
paragraphs: MYP Language Acquisition is assessed against four separate criteria, and they are usually described as listening comprehension, reading comprehension, speaking, and writing. They are marked independently. A student can be strong in two and weak in two within the same term, and that pattern is normal rather than a warning sign. The published descriptors change on the IB's own revision cycle, so ask your school for the current subject guide before planning anything around them.

The split matters because the four skills draw on different machinery. Listening runs at someone else's speed and gives you no second look. Reading lets you go back over a sentence as many times as you like. Speaking is produced live with no editing. Writing is produced slowly but is judged on accuracy that speech gets forgiven for. A child who has spoken a language at home since birth often sails through the two oral criteria and then meets a written task that asks for correct spelling, consistent tense and a recognisable text type. That is a mechanical gap, not evidence that the child does not know the language.

The second thing families miss is that these tasks always name a purpose and an audience, and the marks follow whether the student wrote to them. A task that says write a letter to the school principal is not asking for a nice paragraph about the topic. It wants a greeting, an address to a named reader, a register that is not the one used with friends, and a sign-off. Students lose real marks on beautifully written text that ignores the brief. We teach this from the first session: read the task line, underline the audience, underline the purpose, and only then start planning the content.

Visual material is part of the comprehension criteria too. Students are asked to respond to images, posters, advertisements and captions, not only to continuous prose, and the response has to use evidence from what they saw. Practising this is quick and almost nobody does it at home.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar that sets your child's language deadlines
paragraphs: Most IB schools in Mumbai run a June to March or early April year, with a long break around Diwali in October or November and a shorter one in late December. That shape produces two predictable pressure ridges for Language Acquisition. The first falls in the weeks before the Diwali break, when first-term criterion tasks and interim reports land together. The second falls from January into March, when final tasks, oral recordings and the Year 5 personal project all come due inside the same short run of weeks. Families who book help in January are usually already inside the second ridge.

Schools run their own calendars, so the exact dates differ, but the families we work with attend a recognisable set of them. Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School at Goregaon East (JVLR) both run the full IB continuum including the MYP. Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo and B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade shape the South Mumbai and Western Suburbs picture. JBCN International School has campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur; NES International School is in Mulund West, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. Podar International School runs in Santacruz and Powai.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with any of those schools, or with the International Baccalaureate organisation. We name them only because their calendars are what your tutor has to work around, and because a tutor who has taught students from a particular campus already knows how that campus schedules its oral assessment windows.

The practical move is simple. At the start of each term, ask your child's language teacher for the assessment dates and which criteria each task covers, then give that list to the tutor in the first session. Most of the panic we see in February comes from a recorded speaking task that the family learned about eight days before it was due. Oral assessment is the one component that cannot be rescued by a weekend of effort, because the skill it measures only builds with repeated practice over weeks.

sections.heading: Home, online or hybrid for MYP Language Acquisition in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default for this subject at this age. An IB MYP language acquisition home tuition slot in Mumbai puts an adult in the room who can see that the student has stopped reading and started guessing, can hear hesitation before the student admits to it, and can hand over a pen for a handwritten paragraph without a file transfer. Thirteen-year-olds also stay on task better with someone physically present. The honest cost is travel: a home tutor can serve a limited radius, so your choice of tutor is smaller than the whole city, and a 7pm slot in Kandivali is harder to fill than a 5pm one.

Online works well for this subject for a narrower set of needs, and genuinely better for some. If you want a specific language that nobody teaches within reach of Panvel or Kasarvadavali, an IB online tutor in Mumbai reaches you in a way that no amount of travel budget will. Online is also strong for listening practice, because authentic audio and video can be shared and replayed instantly, and for live written correction in a shared document. What it loses is handwriting. Much MYP writing assessment is still done by hand under time pressure, and a student who has only ever typed with a spellchecker arrives at that task unprepared.

Hybrid is what most families land on by the second term without planning it. One home session a week for the written and handwritten work, one shorter online session for listening and speaking practice, and the recurring error list shared between the two. It also absorbs Mumbai's weather and traffic without losing the week: when Ghodbunder Road is flooded in July, the session moves online rather than disappearing.

Whichever mode you pick, insist that the tutor's notes are written down somewhere you can see. The format matters less than the fact that it exists. Families who can point to what was covered six weeks ago make much better decisions about whether to continue than families relying on a verbal update at the door.

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they reach your flat in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Before an IB MYP language acquisition home tutor in Mumbai is shown to any family, IB Gram checks government photo identity against the name on the profile, checks the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and speaks to at least one professional reference who has seen the person teach. For language tutors we add one more step, because speaking a language and teaching it to a twelve-year-old are not the same competence. We ask for a short marked sample: an anonymised student paragraph with the tutor's corrections and a written comment explaining the correction to the student. A tutor who only circles errors in red fails that step.

There are things the platform cannot check, and you should do them yourself in the first fortnight. Ask the tutor directly which MYP years they have taught and whether they have ever marked against the criteria rather than only prepared students. Ask what they will do in the first four sessions and listen for whether the answer is specific. Sit within earshot of the first session, not in the room, and listen to the ratio: if the tutor is talking for most of the hour, the student is not practising the language. Ask to see the error log after three weeks.

There is one boundary we hold absolutely. A tutor may teach, explain, model, set practice tasks and mark finished work. A tutor may never write, draft, translate or supply any part of a task that will be assessed by the school. That includes polishing a paragraph until the words are no longer the student's own. If a tutor offers to help in that direction, end the engagement and tell us. It is academic misconduct, it is the school and the student who carry the consequences, and it also hides the exact information the teaching needs.

Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade by a specific month. Language progress at this age is uneven and depends heavily on how much the student reads and speaks between sessions. An honest tutor will tell you what they expect to change and what they cannot predict.

sections.heading: The error log, and a small core of structures that beats wide shaky vocabulary
paragraphs: The most useful thing a language tutor builds in the first month is not a vocabulary list. It is an error log, and an IB MYP language acquisition home tutor in Mumbai should have one started by the third session. It is a running record, kept by the student in their own handwriting, of the mistakes that particular student keeps making. Not general grammar weaknesses. Theirs. After three pieces of writing you usually find the same four or five items repeating: the adjective agreement that is always missed, the one past tense that collapses under pressure, the preposition after a particular verb, the sentence that is translated word for word from English and comes out wrong. Five recurring errors fixed properly move a writing mark further than twenty general grammar exercises, because the general exercises spend most of their time on things the student already does correctly.

The log works because the student writes it, not the tutor. Before submitting any piece of writing, the student reads it once against their own list, checking only for those five things. This is a two-minute habit and it is the single clearest improvement we see at the four-week mark. It also changes what the tutor marks: instead of handing back a page of corrections that nobody reads, the tutor marks against the student's own list and adds at most one new item.

The same logic applies to vocabulary and structure. A thirteen-year-old with forty words they can deploy accurately under pressure outperforms one with four hundred they half-remember. We build a small, reliable core first: a handful of sentence frames for giving an opinion, a handful for sequencing events, a handful for agreeing and disagreeing politely, and the connectives that hold a paragraph together. Those frames work across every topic the course throws at them, so the student walks into an unseen task with something to start with instead of a blank page. Breadth is added on top of that core, not instead of it.

Oral work is the part families leave until it is too late, and it is the part that only responds to time. Students who record themselves for a few minutes a week from October are unrecognisable by February. Students who start in February are not. A home tutor can set this up in ten minutes: a phone voice memo, a prompt card, ninety seconds of talking, then listening back once and noting one thing to fix. Nobody needs to listen to the recordings except the student and, occasionally, the tutor. We will say it again because it matters: the tutor may coach the oral and mark the written work, but never writes or supplies any part of what the school assesses.
bullets: An error log the student writes by hand, from their own repeated mistakes
Five recurring errors fixed beats twenty general grammar worksheets
A two-minute self-check against the log before every submission

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one exam cycle realistically look like
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process changes, not mark changes. The student should be able to tell you what their four or five recurring errors are without looking. They should be reading the task line for audience and purpose before writing. They should have a few voice memos recorded. If none of that has happened after a month of weekly sessions, something is wrong with the match and you should say so rather than waiting for the term to end.

At one term the marks usually start to move, and they move unevenly. Writing accuracy tends to respond first, because the error log attacks it directly and the gains are mechanical. Speaking fluency follows if the recording habit held. Listening is the slowest of the four and often shows nothing for a full term before moving suddenly, which is frustrating but normal. Reading comprehension depends almost entirely on whether the student read anything in the language outside class, and no tutor can manufacture that in an hour a week.

Across a full year, the honest picture is that steady weekly work plus genuine practice between sessions produces real, visible improvement in most students. It does not produce it in all of them at the same speed, and it does not produce it at all if the sessions happen and nothing happens in between. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor on the platform is permitted to. Anyone who promises a specific grade by a specific date is telling you something they cannot know.

If a tutor is not working out, you do not need a reason you can defend. Tell us in writing, stop the sessions, and we will look again with what we learned from the first attempt, which usually makes the second match faster and better. The most common cause of a bad fit at this age is not competence. It is pace: a tutor pitched at a sixteen-year-old's attention span losing a twelve-year-old in the first twenty minutes. That is fixable by changing the person, and it is nothing to do with the child.

sections.heading: Starting with an IB MYP language acquisition home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have four things ready before the first session and you will save a fortnight. The most recent school report showing the four criteria separately. Two pieces of your child's own recent written work in the language, uncorrected. The term's assessment dates from the language teacher. And a realistic view of which weekday evenings genuinely work, including the ones that collapse because of football practice or the drive back from school.

The first session is a diagnostic. The tutor will ask the student to read a short unseen text and talk about it, write a short response under a loose time limit, and listen to a clip at normal speed. Nothing is taught in that hour that is not learned from watching. At the end, the tutor writes a short note: which of the four criteria is actually weakest, what the first four or five recurring errors look like, and what the first six weeks will target. You get that note whether or not you continue.

From the second session the pattern settles: a short review of the error log, work on one criterion, a piece of production with immediate correction, and a small task for the week that takes under fifteen minutes a day. The weekly task is where the progress actually comes from, and the tutor's job includes making it small enough that it happens.

You can book an IB MYP language acquisition home tutor in Mumbai, online sessions, or a mix of both, change the mix later, and ask for a different tutor at any point. Send the language, the MYP year, the school and the area, and we will come back with names rather than a brochure.
