sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar sets the deadlines for written work
paragraphs: Mumbai IB schools mostly run an April to March year, and the MYP assessment load does not spread itself evenly across it. The first term opens in April with light work, disappears into the monsoon settling-in weeks of June and July, and then compresses: by late September and October a student can have an analytical essay, a creative piece and an oral all landing inside a fortnight, usually at the same time as the first round of parent-teacher conferences. The Diwali break interrupts rather than relieves it, because work set before the break is due shortly after it, and the second term from November to March carries the heavier end-of-year tasks and, in Year 5, the personal project.

Families at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School at Goregaon East (JVLR), JBCN International School, Parel and NES International School in Mulund West all work to variations of that rhythm, as do families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC and Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo. The dates differ by school, the shape does not. If you are booking a tutor in response to an October mark, you are booking at the busiest point in the calendar and you should expect the first month to be triage rather than a clean build from first principles.

The useful move is to book against the calendar rather than against a single disappointing mark. A student who starts in June with no deadline in sight can spend four weeks learning how to plan a comparative response properly, which is exactly the work that cannot be done in the week the essay is due. Parents who come to us in June and July tend to get more out of a term than parents who come in the second week of October, and the tutor pool is also wider because fewer standing slots have been taken.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. We name schools because their calendars and their coursework patterns are the context a tutor has to work inside, not because we have any arrangement with them. A tutor works to your child's school's deadlines and to the criteria their teacher uses, and if the school has issued its own guidance on how outside support should work, that guidance takes precedence over anything a tutor suggests.

sections.heading: Home classes, online, or a mix: which suits a MYP writer?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it earns that position for a specific reason: a MYP student who is thirteen or fourteen writes more when another person is sitting at the table. The subject's real work is drafting, and drafting is the activity students avoid most convincingly when nobody can see the screen. An IB MYP language and literature home tutor in Mumbai sitting across the dining table can say 'write the first two sentences now, I will wait', and the sentences get written. That single dynamic is why most families here start with home classes and only move off them for a reason.

Home sessions also fit the household. A parent can hear the last ten minutes without hovering, the printed copies of the text are already on the shelf, and the tutor sees the actual working conditions, which in a Mumbai flat might be a shared bedroom with a younger sibling and a television in the next room. A tutor who has seen that will give different homework from one who has not. The trade-off is honest: home tuition costs travel time, it is harder to reschedule at short notice, and in heavy monsoon weeks a cancelled session is a lost week rather than a shifted hour.

Across the MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai families arrange tend to run weekly, and a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai parents share across siblings is common enough, though for this group we would still push you towards a single-subject specialist. An IB online tutor in Mumbai works better for this subject than parents expect, because annotation and marking both live naturally in a shared document, and it is the right answer when the pool for your language of study is thin in your zone or when the only tutor who fits teaches from Thane and you are in Nerul. It is the weaker answer for a younger MYP student who needs a person in the room to keep writing. A good compromise is hybrid: a fortnightly home session for the long drafting work and oral rehearsal, with shorter online sessions in between for feedback on a draft that already exists.

Whatever the mode, insist that sessions are built around the student's own writing rather than around the tutor talking about a text. If an hour passes and your child has not written anything, that hour taught less than it should have. Ask after the first month whether the balance of talking and writing has shifted towards writing. For most students it should have, and for a student whose issue is confidence rather than technique, it should have shifted early.

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they reach your Mumbai flat?
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram goes through the same checks before any family sees them: government photo identity verified against the name on the profile, the claimed qualification evidenced, a stated record of having taught MYP Language and Literature at the year level they are offering, and at least one contactable reference from previous tutoring or teaching work. We also ask for a short piece of sample marking on an anonymised student response, because a tutor's written feedback tells you more in two minutes than a curriculum vitae tells you in ten. A tutor whose feedback reads 'good effort, work on structure' is not going to move a student forward.

Verification is not the whole story, and the checks a parent runs themselves are the ones that matter most. An IB private tutor Mumbai families find through a neighbour's recommendation has been checked by exactly nobody, which is worth remembering before you skip the questions below. In the first session, ask the tutor to explain what the four assessment criteria for this subject are asking for, in their own words, without reading from a sheet. Ask which text types your child's school has set this year and what the difference in plan is between two of them. Ask how they handle a draft. Those three answers separate a tutor who has taught the MYP from a tutor who has taught English.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, offers to 'polish' an assessed piece, or suggests the school's marking was wrong before they have seen the criteria. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor can, because the marking is done by the school's teachers against published criteria and moderated by the IB. What a tutor can do is make the student's work better, which is a different and more reliable proposition. An IB MYP language and literature home tutor in Mumbai who leads with results claims rather than with method is the wrong hire.

For home visits there is a second layer that families here handle well already. Register the tutor at the society gate as a standing weekly visitor rather than a daily guest, so the entry is routine and nobody is kept waiting at the barrier for fifteen minutes. Keep sessions in a shared room, not a bedroom. Have an adult or household staff member present in the flat. None of this implies suspicion of a particular person; it is simply what sensible supervision of a minor looks like, and good tutors expect it and prefer it.

sections.heading: Drafting, redrafting, and the line a tutor must never cross
paragraphs: The skill this subject is really assessing is redrafting. A first draft is a student finding out what they think; a second draft is the student organising it for a reader. Most MYP students never experience the second step, because school deadlines allow one pass and the feedback arrives after the mark. Home tuition is useful here precisely because it can insert the missing step: write a draft on Tuesday, get it questioned on Thursday, rewrite it over the weekend, submit on Monday. A student who has done that cycle six times by March writes differently from one who has submitted six first drafts.

Which brings us to the boundary, and it is not a soft one. A tutor may teach, explain, model on a different text, question, and mark. A tutor may not write, rewrite, dictate, correct line by line, or supply any part of a piece that will be assessed. The distinction is easy to apply in practice. 'Your second paragraph makes two points at once; which one is the paragraph about?' is teaching. 'Try this sentence instead' on an assessed draft is writing the student's work for them, and if it goes in, the student has submitted something that is not theirs. The IB treats authenticity seriously and so should the family paying for the help.

Good feedback on an assessed draft therefore looks like questions and categories, not replacement text. A tutor can mark a paragraph 'evidence quoted but not analysed' and the student fixes it. A tutor can model the same move on a poem the school has not set, then hand the pen back. A tutor can run the planning stage out loud, because planning is the teachable part and the words on the page will still be the student's. What a tutor should not do is open the document and start typing, however much time it would save on a Sunday night.

Parents sometimes ask where proofreading sits. For an assessed piece, pointing out that there is a run-on sentence somewhere in the third paragraph is support; fixing it is not. It feels pedantic and it is not. A student who learns to find their own run-on sentences has gained the thing the criteria are measuring, and a student whose tutor has quietly cleaned the piece has a better mark this term and no new skill. If you want one test of whether a tutor is on the right side of this line, read the marked draft: if the tutor's handwriting contains sentences that could be lifted into the essay, something has gone wrong.
bullets: Build a real redraft cycle: draft, questioned, rewritten, submitted

Feedback as categories and questions, not as replacement sentences

sections.heading: What progress realistically looks like at four weeks and one term
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look at whether the student can produce a usable plan for a set task in under ten minutes, and whether they can say in one sentence who the piece is for and what it is meant to do. Those two habits are the earliest honest signal, they are visible to a parent without any knowledge of the subject, and they arrive well before any change in a report. If a month has passed and your child still starts writing at the top of a blank page with no plan at all, raise it with the tutor directly and ask what the plan for the next month is.

At one term, expect the written work to be better organised and the feedback from school to change in character: fewer comments about structure, more comments about depth of analysis. That is progress even if the mark has not moved yet, because the criteria are separate and a student usually fixes organisation before they fix interpretation. Expect the oral work to be less frightening, because it has been rehearsed. Expect a slightly longer attention span for reading, which for a Mumbai student juggling tuition, a commute and a sport is not a small thing.

At one full year, the realistic outcome is a student who can approach an unfamiliar text type, work out what shape it wants, and produce a competent version without being taught that particular form first. That is the transferable skill, and it is what makes the next programme survivable. It is also why the drafting discipline matters more than any single essay: the student who has rewritten twenty pieces has internalised something the student who has revised twenty sets of notes has not.

The honest limits. Progress in writing is slower and less linear than progress in a quantitative subject, and a student can do genuinely better work and see the same mark for a term, because the criteria descriptors are wide. Some students need a different tutor, not more sessions. Some need fewer activities rather than more tuition. We do not guarantee grades and nobody reputable will, because the marking is the school's and the moderation is the IB's. No IB tutor Mumbai parents hire can change that, and the ones who claim otherwise are selling something else. What we commit to is a verified tutor, an honest read on whether the match is working, and a straightforward replacement when it is not.
bullets: Four weeks: a usable plan in ten minutes and a one-sentence audience statement
One term: school feedback shifts from structure comments to analysis comments

sections.heading: Booking an IB MYP Language and Literature home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Typing IB tutors near me Mumbai into a search box returns everybody and tells you nothing about who has marked this subject, so skip that step. To get a useful shortlist, have four things ready. First, the most recent marked piece of work with the teacher's comments on it, photographed or scanned; this is the single most valuable document in the whole process and it saves the first session from being a diagnostic conversation. Second, the list of texts the school has set this year. Third, the school's own calendar of upcoming assessed tasks, if you have it. Fourth, your honest availability, including whether the student has a sport or a music class that already owns two evenings.

The first session then does something specific rather than general. The tutor reads the marked piece against the criteria, identifies the one or two things that would most change the next piece, and sets a short writing task to test that read. No new text is introduced, nothing is pre-taught, and the student should leave with something written rather than a list of resources. If a first session ends with a reading list and no writing, ask why. An IB MYP language and literature home tutor in Mumbai who starts with a reading list has started in the wrong place for a student who is already reading.

From there, a standing weekly slot is the usual pattern, with the tutor's marking turned around between sessions so the student rewrites against comments rather than against memory. Families in Powai, Chembur and Kharghar often prefer a slightly later start to clear the evening traffic; families in South Mumbai often prefer an early weekend slot because the weekday compression is worse there than the distance suggests. Tell us the constraint and it goes into the match rather than becoming a problem in week three.

If the tutor is not right, say so after two or three sessions rather than after two months. Nobody is offended, the replacement is straightforward, and the context you have already given us does not have to be repeated. What the new tutor receives is the same brief plus what the first month showed, which usually makes the second match faster and better than the first.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP Language and Literature home tutor in Mumbai do in the first session?
faqs.answer: The first session reads one already-marked piece of your child's work against the assessment criteria and sets a short writing task based on what it shows. The tutor is looking for the gap between what the student understood and what the page delivered, which is usually a planning problem rather than a reading problem. Expect the student to write something in that first hour. A session that ends with a reading list and no writing has started in the wrong place, because reading is rarely the limiting factor in this subject.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Kharghar or Panvel for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is matched from inside Navi Mumbai rather than pulled across the creek. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are short runs from each other along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, so a node-to-node match holds for a full term. A tutor commuting from the Western Suburbs over the Atal Setu for a 7pm slot will start rescheduling by the second month, which is worse for the student than a slightly less senior tutor nearby. We will say which situation you are in before you book.

faqs.question: How do we handle society gate access and building security for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor with your society office as a standing weekly visitor rather than entering them as a fresh guest each week. Most Mumbai complexes will issue a recurring pass once a resident confirms the day and time, and it removes the ten or fifteen minutes that otherwise disappears at the barrier. Share the tower and flat number, the preferred gate, and whether visitor parking is available, because a tutor arriving by car in a building without visitor parking will be late every week. Good tutors expect to be registered and verified.

faqs.question: Can the tutor write or improve my child's essay before it is handed in?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach, explain, question and mark, but may never write, rewrite or supply any part of a piece that will be assessed. That includes replacing sentences, dictating a thesis, or quietly correcting the grammar in a draft that is about to be submitted. A tutor can tell your child that a paragraph quotes evidence without analysing it; your child then fixes it. The IB treats authenticity seriously, and work that is partly the tutor's is a risk to the student, not a shortcut for them.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for this subject?
faqs.answer: Rates depend on the tutor's experience with the MYP specifically, the year group, the language the course is taught in, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs. Language and Literature in a language with a smaller tutor pool in your zone, such as Marathi or French, will price differently from English. Home sessions carry travel that online sessions do not. We will not quote a figure here because any number we invented would be wrong for somebody; ask for the range on your specific shortlist and it arrives before you commit.

faqs.question: How do you prepare a student for a task written under timed conditions?
faqs.answer: By making the planning minutes automatic. In a timed task the first few minutes decide the piece, and most students either skip planning entirely or spend so long on it that they run out of writing time. A tutor drills a repeatable planning routine against a clock until the student can produce a usable outline quickly, then practises writing to that outline under the same time limit. The first few attempts are deliberately scrappy. What improves is not speed of writing but the quality of the decision made in the first five minutes.

faqs.question: My child has an individual oral coming up. Is that something a tutor can help with?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the part families leave latest. Spoken tasks in MYP Language and Literature are assessed work, and preparing one means rehearsing out loud with timing and feedback on pace, signposting and eye contact, not writing a script and reading it. A tutor should schedule rehearsal a fortnight ahead, record one run so the student hears themselves, and work on the transition points where nerves show. The tutor can question the content and mark the delivery, but the words remain the student's own.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than online for a Year 2 or Year 3 MYP student?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, for one reason: a twelve or thirteen-year-old writes more when a person is in the room. Home classes let the tutor say 'write the opening now' and wait, which is the single hardest thing to achieve over a screen with a younger student. Online is a strong option when the tutor pool for your language is thin in your zone, or for an older, self-directed student. Many families run a hybrid: a longer home session for drafting, shorter online sessions for feedback on work already written.

faqs.question: Does my child's school need to know we have hired a tutor?
faqs.answer: You are not obliged to tell the school, but it usually helps. A teacher who knows outside support is in place can be clearer in written feedback and can say which criterion to work on next, which makes the tutoring sharper. Some Mumbai schools publish their own guidance on outside academic support, and where they do, that guidance takes precedence over anything a tutor suggests. IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with any school, so the relationship with the school stays entirely yours to manage.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we re-shortlist. The useful window is two or three sessions, not two months, because by then you know whether the student is writing more and whether the feedback is specific. We do not ask you to justify the decision or to have a difficult conversation with the tutor yourself. The replacement receives the original brief plus what the first weeks showed, which usually makes the second match quicker. A mismatch of working style is common and is not a judgement on either person.

faqs.question: Do you cover Language and Literature in languages other than English?
faqs.answer: We match tutors for the language your child's school teaches the course in, which in Mumbai most often means English but also includes Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati and French at various schools. Availability varies sharply by zone: a Hindi Language and Literature tutor is easier to place in the Central Suburbs than a French one is in Panvel. Which language course a student is placed in is a decision the school makes with the family, and a tutor works within that decision rather than arguing with it.

faqs.question: We live on Ghodbunder Road in Thane. Will a tutor realistically commute there every week?
faqs.answer: Only if the tutor is based in Thane, which is how we match it. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so a Ghodbunder Road slot works best either at a later start or at a weekend. Mulund-based tutors sometimes cross over via the Eastern Express Highway. A tutor coming from the Western Suburbs is not a sustainable weekly arrangement, and we would offer hybrid instead of pretending otherwise.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB MYP Language and Literature online tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Tell us the Middle Years Programme (MYP) year, the language the course is taught in, and one concrete thing you have seen. Not 'she needs help with English' but 'the feedback on her last two pieces both mentioned organisation' or 'he writes two strong paragraphs and then the piece falls apart'. For an online match we also want two practical details that do not come up for home tuition: where in the flat the student will sit for sessions, and whether they will be on a laptop or a tablet. A tablet with a detachable keyboard is a worse drafting surface than it looks, and a session run from the dining table with the family's evening happening behind it goes differently from one run at a desk.

The sequence is short. 1. You send the MYP year, school, language of study, the pattern you have noticed, and the device and space the student will use. 2. Teaching online as a deliberate practice means the tutor arrives with the text already in a shared file, has a marking convention they can explain in a sentence, and knows how to keep a twelve or thirteen-year-old producing rather than nodding. A tutor who simply turns their camera on and talks for an hour is running a home session badly over a worse channel. An IB MYP language and literature online tutor in Mumbai should be able to tell you, before you book, what the student will have written by the end of the first hour.

We do not describe a child to a tutor in terms of ability. The brief is about texts and tasks: which pieces have been set, what the teacher's comments said, what the student finds hardest to start. A student who produces a thin response in September is almost always a student who has not yet been shown the shape of that response, and a tutor who begins from that assumption gets further in a month than one who begins from a deficit story.

sections.heading: What the MYP asks of a writer in Years 1 to 5
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers five years and eight subject groups, and Language and Literature is the group a student takes in a language they already use confidently. It is not a remedial course and it is not a grammar course. It asks a student to read closely, work out how a text produces its effects, and then produce writing of their own that is shaped for a named reader and a stated purpose. Which language course a student is placed in, and in which group, is settled by the school together with the family, and a tutor works inside that decision.

The age range is the thing parents underestimate. A MYP Year 1 student is around eleven; a Year 5 student is around fifteen. The same course description sits over both, but a tutor who teaches an eleven-year-old the way they teach a fifteen-year-old will lose the room in twenty minutes. Online makes this sharper, because a younger student on a screen has an entire internet one keystroke away and a tutor who is talking rather than setting work has already lost. The upside is equally real: a younger student who is asked to type two sentences right now, with the tutor watching the cursor, usually writes them.

Assessment is criterion-based and the school's teachers do the marking, with the IB moderating samples. The four criteria for this group cover analysing a text, organising a response, producing the student's own text, and using language. A general MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai can help with the framework across subjects, and parents who ask for an all-round MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai schools would recognise usually narrow the request once they see how different the writing group is from the quantitative ones.

Mumbai students bring an advantage into this subject that is worth naming. A child who moves between English at school, Hindi or Marathi in the building, and a third language at home has a working sense of register, idiom and audience that monolingual students build slowly and self-consciously. The job is to point that existing sense at the page, which is a very different project from fixing something. Indian English is a full variety with its own conventions, and a tutor's work is to teach a student to choose a register for a reader, never to tell a child the way they speak is wrong.

sections.heading: Why does an essay subject teach better on a screen than a problem subject?
paragraphs: Because the artefact is the same object for both people. In a writing subject the thing being taught is a document, and a document shared on a screen is genuinely shared: both cursors are in the same paragraph, the tutor can highlight the exact clause that is doing too much work, and the student sees the highlight appear in real time. Compare that with a problem subject, where the working lives on paper, gets photographed, arrives rotated and half-lit, and the tutor spends the first five minutes asking which line is which. The screen is a worse channel for handwriting and a better one for text.

Line-by-line annotation is the clearest example. A tutor opens the poem or the extract the school has set, and the two of them work down it together: a comment on the verb in line three, a highlight on the repeated sentence opening, a margin note asking why the writer broke the stanza there. The student's own annotations go into the same file in a different colour, so by the end of the session there is a marked-up text that exists permanently and can be reopened the night before the assessment. On paper, that annotation lives in one copy in one school bag.

Marking behaves the same way. A comment anchored to the student's third sentence lands where the error is, and the student reads it while looking at their own words. A general note at the foot of a page saying 'analysis needs developing' is read, agreed with, and forgotten by Thursday. Anchored comments also let a tutor mark in categories: the same three-word tag repeated at every point where evidence is quoted but not analysed is a pattern a student can see, and seeing the pattern is most of the fix.

The limits are real and parents should hear them. Oral rehearsal is harder online, because the eye contact is wrong and the pauses land differently; it works, but it needs recording and playback to substitute for a listener in the room. Reading a long novel together is not a good use of a session either way. And the counterweight that matters most in Mumbai schools gets its own treatment further down this page: a great deal of assessed writing is still done by hand, under time, in a hall, and a student who only ever composes by typing will feel that difference.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai zones gain most from online, and which should just book home tuition?
paragraphs: Online earns its place where travel would otherwise decide the tutor. In Navi Mumbai, a family in Panvel or the far side of Kharghar has a genuinely smaller local pool than one in Vashi or Nerul, and the Atal Setu has not changed what a weekday evening crossing from the island city does to a tutor's week. In Thane, the Ghodbunder Road stretch out to Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate is the clearest case in Mumbai, Maharashtra: a tutor near Thane station can be twenty minutes away off-peak and an hour away at seven in the evening, so the same tutor who is impossible on Tuesday is easy online on Tuesday. Airoli has a version of the same problem across the Trans-Harbour Line.

The far north of the Western Suburbs behaves similarly. Dahisar, Borivali and Kandivali East sit at the top of the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, and although Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the run to Andheri much more tolerable, a tutor based in Bandra is still not going to hold a Dahisar slot through a monsoon. Families in Malad and Goregaon are in the middle: often fine for home tuition, often better served online if the language of study narrows the pool. Oshiwara and Lokhandwala sit close enough to the Andheri cluster that either mode works.

Then there are the zones where we would usually tell you to book home classes instead. South Mumbai is small: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Tardeo and Worli are all within a short run of each other, and the Coastal Road has helped, so a resident tutor is realistic and an eleven-year-old is better served in the room. The Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz and Juhu belt along Link Road has the deepest tutor pool in the city. In the Central Suburbs the Powai and Chandivali cluster is dense enough that tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar along JVLR without much trouble, and Kurla, Ghatkopar and Vikhroli sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway.

The Eastern Suburbs are the mixed case. Chembur, Govandi and Wadala are better connected than the map suggests because of the Eastern Freeway and the Harbour Line, so home tuition is usually workable, while Bhandup and Mulund families often prefer online in the second half of the week. An IB MYP language and literature online tutor in Mumbai removes the travel variable entirely, which is why we will sometimes recommend it even to a family who asked for a home tutor, and will sometimes argue the other way for a Year 1 or Year 2 student who needs a person at the table.

sections.heading: Mumbai school terms, submission portals, and the handwritten task
paragraphs: The Mumbai IB year runs April to March, and the writing load concentrates rather than spreads. April and May are light, the monsoon weeks of June and July are the only real build time a tutor gets, and from late September a student can face an analytical piece, a creative task and a spoken assessment inside a fortnight. The Diwali break moves deadlines rather than removing them. The second term from November to March carries the heavier end-of-year work, and in Year 5 the personal project runs alongside everything else.

Most IB schools in the city now run coursework through an online portal, which changes what a tutor can see and what a parent can check. Task sheets, criteria and teacher comments usually live in the same place, and a student who can open that portal during a session gives the tutor the single most useful document in the subject: the school's own wording of the task. Families at Oberoi International School at Goregaon East (JVLR), Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, JBCN International School, Borivali and NES International School in Mulund West all work this way, with variations. Ask your child to open the task sheet in the first session rather than describing it from memory.

The counterweight to all of this is the handwritten task. A large share of assessed and practice writing in Mumbai schools still happens on paper, in a hall, against a clock, and a student who has spent a year composing only by typing will find their hand slower than their thinking and their planning habits wrong for the format. A good online tutor schedules handwritten work deliberately: the student writes a timed piece on paper, photographs it, uploads it, and it is marked with the same anchored comments. Typing is the teaching surface; handwriting is the performance surface, and both need practice.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. Schools are named here because their calendars and their coursework systems are the environment a tutor has to work inside. Where a school has published its own guidance about outside academic support, that guidance comes first, and a tutor who suggests working around it should be declined on the spot.

sections.heading: Online, home classes or hybrid for a thirteen-year-old
paragraphs: Start with the honest comparison. Home classes put an adult at the table, and for a MYP student of eleven to thirteen that is still the most reliable way to make writing actually happen. Most families who search for home tuition in this subject are right to. Online wins on three specific things: the shared document, the removal of travel, and access to a tutor who teaches your child's language of study when the local pool is thin. It loses on presence, and presence is the whole game for a younger student who would rather be doing anything else.

So the first question is not 'which is better' but 'what is the obstacle'. If the obstacle is that nobody good can reach Panvel on a Wednesday, online solves it. If the obstacle is that your thirteen-year-old will not start writing unless someone is sitting there, a screen does not solve it and a home tutor does. If the obstacle is that the student writes but the writing is unstructured, both work, and the shared document gives online a genuine edge because the feedback sits where the problem is.

Hybrid is the pattern most of our MYP Language and Literature families settle into by the second term. A longer home session every other week for drafting, oral rehearsal and the handwritten timed practice, with shorter online sessions in between for marking and redrafting work the student has already produced. It costs less travel than weekly home classes, it keeps a person in the room often enough to matter, and the between-sessions marking is faster to turn around because nobody is carrying paper.

Whichever mode you choose, judge it on output. An IB MYP language and literature online tutor in Mumbai should leave a visible trail: a document with the student's writing in it, comments against specific sentences, and something the student rewrote. If after four sessions the shared folder contains notes the tutor made and nothing the student wrote, the format is being used as a lecture hall. Say so, and if it does not change, re-shortlist. The same test applies to home classes, where it is easier to mistake a pleasant hour for a productive one.

sections.heading: How are online tutors checked, and what should a parent watch for?
paragraphs: Every tutor is verified the same way whether they teach online or in your flat: government photo identity matched to the profile name, evidence of the claimed qualification, a stated record of teaching MYP Language and Literature at the year level offered, and a contactable reference. For this subject we also ask for sample marking on an anonymised response, because written feedback is the product. A tutor whose sample feedback is three generic encouragements and a tick is not going to change how your child writes, however strong the qualification looks.

The parent-side checks for online are different from the home-visit ones and take about ten minutes. Sit in on the last fifteen minutes of the first session. Ask to be added as a viewer on the shared folder, which any reasonable tutor will do without hesitating. Confirm that sessions happen on the scheduled platform and that there is no separate private messaging channel with your child; routine contact about a minor should be visible to you. Keep the student working in a shared room rather than a bedroom with the door shut. None of this is distrust of a person, it is what supervision of a minor normally looks like, and good tutors set it up themselves.

On the subject side, ask three questions in the first session and listen to the answers. What are the four criteria for this group asking for, in your own words? Which text types has this school set this year, and how does the plan differ between two of them? How will you mark a draft without writing any of it? A tutor who has taught the MYP answers all three without reaching for a document. A tutor who has taught English in general will answer the first and struggle with the second.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, or who offers to tidy up a submission before it goes to the portal. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because the marking belongs to your child's school and the moderation belongs to the IB, and no IB tutor Mumbai parents hire sits anywhere near that process. An IB MYP language and literature online tutor in Mumbai who leads with outcomes rather than with method has told you what they are selling. An IB private tutor Mumbai families find through a neighbour may be excellent, but nobody has checked them, which is worth a thought before you skip the questions above.

Sample marking requested, because feedback is the thing you are buying

sections.heading: The shared document: annotating, planning, and a technique file that grows all year
paragraphs: Here is what a well-run online hour in this subject actually contains. It opens with the text, not with talking. Tutor and student work down an extract together, and the annotation is split by colour: the student marks what they notice, the tutor marks what they want noticed. The student goes first on each section, always, because a tutor who annotates first has done the thinking and the student has watched. Ten minutes in there should be more of the student's colour on the page than the tutor's, and if there is not, the session is running backwards.

Then planning, before either person writes a sentence of prose. The plan lives in a scratch file, not in the document that will eventually hold the assessed piece, and this separation is deliberate: it keeps the tutor's typing permanently outside anything that will be submitted. A plan for a comparative response is built around points of comparison rather than around one text and then the other. A plan for a speech is built around what the audience should feel at three moments. The tutor can type freely here, because none of it is the student's assessed writing, and the student then closes the scratch file and writes their own prose in their own document.

The marking convention matters more than the platform. Comments anchored to the student's own sentences, written as questions rather than corrections: 'what is this paragraph about?', 'evidence quoted, where is the analysis?', 'who is this sentence for?'. Repeated tags make patterns visible. What a tutor must never do is use suggestion mode, track changes, or direct typing on a document holding assessed work, because a suggestion accepted with one click is the tutor's sentence in the student's piece. A tutor may teach, question and mark; a tutor may never write or redraft any part of assessed work, and online makes the temptation to just fix it one keystroke stronger than it is on paper.

The thing that compounds across a year is the technique file. One document, started in April, in which every technique the student meets gets a heading, a one-line definition in the student's own words, an example from a text they actually studied, and a sentence they wrote using it. By February that file is thirty or forty entries long, it is entirely theirs, and it is a far better revision resource than any printed glossary because every example comes from their own reading. Families who book an IB MYP language and literature online tutor in Mumbai and keep that single file going get more out of the year than families who run better individual sessions without one.
bullets: Student annotates first in their own colour; the tutor responds to it
Plan in a scratch file so the tutor's typing never touches assessed work
Comments anchored to sentences and phrased as questions, not corrections

sections.heading: What a term of online sessions should change for a Mumbai MYP student
paragraphs: At four weeks the honest measures are behavioural, not numerical. Can the student produce a usable plan quickly for a task they have just been given? Do they open the shared document themselves before the session starts? Has the technique file got entries in it that the student wrote rather than the tutor? Those three things are visible to a parent with no knowledge of the subject and they show up long before any change in school feedback. If none of them has happened in a month, that is a conversation to have directly with the tutor.

At one term, look at the character of the teacher's comments rather than the mark. Comments usually move from structure towards interpretation as a student improves, because organisation is the easier thing to fix and it gets fixed first. The mark may well sit still while this happens, which is normal and not a sign that the tuition failed. Also watch the handwritten work: if the student has been doing timed paper practice, the gap between their typed and handwritten pieces should be narrowing.

At a year, the outcome worth aiming at is independence from the tutor's prompts. The student meets an unfamiliar text type, works out what shape it wants, plans it without being asked to, and produces a competent version. That is the skill that survives into the next programme, and it is why the drafting cycle matters more than any individual essay. A student who has rewritten twenty pieces against anchored comments has built something a student who revised twenty sets of notes has not.

The limits, stated plainly. Writing improves unevenly and sometimes invisibly for a term. Online suits some thirteen-year-olds and defeats others, and if yours is in the second group the right answer is home tuition rather than more online hours. We do not guarantee grades and no reputable tutor will, because the marking is the school's work and the moderation is the IB's. What we commit to is a verified tutor, a straight answer when a match is not working, and a replacement without a negotiation.

One term: school comments shift from organisation towards interpretation

sections.heading: Starting with an online MYP Language and Literature tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Typing IB tutors near me Mumbai into a search box returns everyone and tells you nothing about who has marked this subject at your child's year level. Instead, send us four things: the MYP year and school, the language the course is taught in, a photograph of the most recently marked piece with the teacher's comments visible, and the evenings that are genuinely free. If you can also say which device the student will use and where they will sit, the match gets better, because a tutor who knows the student is on a tablet at the dining table will plan the hour differently.

The first session should produce an artefact. The tutor reads the marked piece against the criteria, names the one or two changes that would most improve the next piece, annotates a short extract with the student, and sets a timed writing task. By the end of the hour there should be a shared folder with a marked-up text and something the student wrote in it. If the hour produces only a conversation and a resource list, ask why before booking a second.

After that the usual pattern is a weekly slot with marking turned around between sessions, so the student is always rewriting against comments rather than against memory. Families in Panvel, on Ghodbunder Road and in Dahisar typically run fully online; families in Bandra, Powai and South Mumbai more often run hybrid, with a fortnightly home session for the drafting and oral work. Across the MYP subject groups home classes Mumbai families arrange still outnumber online ones, and a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai parents share between siblings is common, though for this group a single-subject specialist is worth the extra arrangement.

If the match is wrong, say so at two or three sessions rather than at two months. Re-shortlisting is routine, no explanation is required, and the next tutor gets the original brief plus what the first weeks showed. That second match is usually faster and better, because by then you know something specific about how your child works that you did not know when you started.

Mention the device and the room; it changes how the hour is planned

faqs.question: Does an IB MYP Language and Literature online tutor in Mumbai really work for a thirteen-year-old?
faqs.answer: It works when the tutor runs the hour as production rather than explanation. A thirteen-year-old online will write if the tutor sets a short timed task, watches the cursor move in the shared document, and says nothing until it is done. The same student will drift if the tutor talks about a poem for forty minutes. Ask a prospective tutor what the student will have written by the end of session one. If the answer is vague, the format will not save them, and home classes are the safer choice at that age.

faqs.question: Can we switch to a home tutor later if online is not landing?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a fair number of families do after the first term. Tell us and we re-shortlist from the pool that can actually reach your building, which is a smaller pool and may mean a different person rather than the same tutor in a different format. Some families keep both: a fortnightly home session for drafting and oral rehearsal, with shorter online sessions for marking in between. The brief you gave us at the start carries over, so the switch does not restart the process.

faqs.question: We are on Ghodbunder Road in Thane and evening travel is impossible. Is online the answer?
faqs.answer: For that stretch, usually yes. A tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, which means a weekday slot either starts late or quietly collapses by the second month. Online removes the variable entirely and widens the pool to the whole city. If you would still prefer a person in the room, a weekend home session plus online sessions midweek is the arrangement that holds best for Ghodbunder Road families.

faqs.question: Will the tutor type into my child's essay?
faqs.answer: No, and you should check this. A tutor may teach, question and mark, but may never write or redraft any part of a piece that will be assessed, and online makes that easier to violate because suggestion mode is one click away. Our tutors plan in a separate scratch file and leave comments anchored to the student's sentences in the submission document, never edits. If you open the shared folder and find tracked changes or accepted suggestions on an assessed draft, raise it with us immediately.

faqs.question: How do you handle the fact that exams are still handwritten?
faqs.answer: By scheduling handwritten practice on purpose. Typing is the teaching surface because it makes annotation and marking work; handwriting is the performance surface because that is how a timed task in a hall actually happens. A good online tutor sets a paper piece under time, has it photographed and uploaded, and marks it with the same anchored comments. Students who only compose by typing find their hand slower than their thinking in the first timed task of the year, and the fix is practice, not panic.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for online sessions?
faqs.answer: On the tutor's experience with the MYP specifically, the year group, the language the course is taught in, and session length. Online removes travel from the equation, which is one of the variables that makes home tuition cost more in far nodes, so the difference tends to show up most for families in Panvel, Dahisar or on Ghodbunder Road. Scarce languages price differently from English in any mode. We will not invent a figure here; ask for the range on your actual shortlist before you commit.

faqs.question: What does the shared document actually contain by the end of a term?
faqs.answer: A set of annotated extracts in two colours, the student's drafts with anchored comments beside specific sentences, the scratch files from planning, and the technique file. The technique file is the one worth protecting: a running list where each technique has a definition in the student's own words, an example from a text they studied, and a sentence they wrote themselves. By February it is thirty or forty entries long and it beats any printed glossary for revision, because every example came from their own reading.

faqs.question: My child is strong in Hindi at home but studies Language and Literature in English. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is an advantage, not a problem. A student moving between languages develops a working sense of register and audience that the criteria explicitly reward, and that monolingual students usually build later and more self-consciously. Indian English is a full variety with its own settled conventions; the tutor's job is to teach a student to choose a register deliberately for a given reader, not to treat how a family speaks as an error. Which language course a student is placed in is the school's decision with the family.

faqs.question: Can oral and presentation tasks be prepared over a screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one adjustment: record the run-through. Eye contact and pause length do not read correctly over video, so the tutor works from a recording the student makes and plays back, which also lets the student hear their own pace. Rehearsal should be booked a fortnight before the task, not the night before, because the first run is always too fast and the second is always too slow. The tutor questions the content and coaches delivery, while the words stay the student's own.

faqs.question: What should supervision look like during an online session at home?
faqs.answer: Keep the student in a shared room with the screen visible rather than behind a closed bedroom door, be added as a viewer on the shared folder, and make sure all scheduling and contact runs through you rather than through a private channel with your child. Sit in on the last fifteen minutes of the first session. Good tutors set these conditions up themselves and never object to them. None of it implies suspicion; it is simply the normal shape of an adult working with a minor.

faqs.question: How quickly should marking come back between sessions?
faqs.answer: Before the next session, every time. The point of an anchored comment is that the student rewrites against it while the piece is still live in their head, and marking that arrives at the start of the following lesson has already lost most of its value. Agree the turnaround explicitly when you book. If drafts are stacking up unmarked by the third week, that is the clearest early signal of a tutor who has taken on more students than they can mark for, and it is worth raising straight away.

faqs.question: Is a general IB home tutor in Mumbai enough, or do we need a subject specialist?
faqs.answer: For this group, a specialist. A tutor who covers several MYP subject groups can genuinely help with study habits and with the shape of the programme, and an IB home tuition in Mumbai arrangement across subjects suits plenty of families. But Language and Literature is marked on how well a student analyses a text and shapes writing for a reader, and that is taught by someone who has marked those pieces before. Ask what text types they have marked at your child's year level.

sections.heading: How do we match an IB MYP language and literature tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: The useful first message contains a piece of writing, not a description of one. A parent looking for an IB MYP language and literature tutor in Mumbai should send the most recent marked response with the teacher's comments still on it, plus the task sheet if the school issues one. Within a few minutes a specialist can usually tell whether the writing is retelling the text, whether the structure is the problem, whether the response ignored the audience it was told to write for, or whether the ideas are sound and the sentences are letting them down. Those four need different tutors and different first sessions.

Matching then runs on three filters. The first is the text type the school is teaching: a unit on a novel, a unit on advertising and persuasion, and a unit on film or graphic text all look different in practice, and a tutor strong on literary analysis is not automatically strong on non-literary media. The second is marking experience against the criteria, because the whole problem on this page is a student doing something well that is not what is being assessed. The third is scheduling reality. A family in Khar West and a tutor in Mulund can hold a Saturday morning and will not hold a Tuesday evening for a full term, which is a matching failure rather than a tutor failure.

You then speak to each shortlisted tutor before anything is booked. One question separates the useful ones: ask what they would do with a response that retells the plot beautifully. The answer you want involves going back to a single paragraph and rewriting it to show how the writer produces an effect, not a lecture on literary devices. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will promise a specific grade for a Year 3 unit task. What a good first session does produce is one paragraph the student can compare against their own earlier version and see the difference without being told.

sections.heading: Language and literature among the eight MYP subject groups
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs from Year 1 to Year 5 and sorts learning into eight subject groups. Language and literature is the group covering a student's main language of instruction, which in most Mumbai international schools is English. It is distinct from language acquisition, the group for a language being learned, and parents mix the two up constantly. If your child is in an English language and literature class, the course assumes fluency and assesses what the student can do with it, which is a completely different proposition from learning the language.

Assessment sits on four criteria: analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Say those four out loud and the mystery of the mid-band report usually solves itself. A student can read a novel a week and never be asked to analyse; a student can write pages and never organise them for a reader; a student can have excellent ideas and produce text that ignores the audience the task named. An MYP subject groups tutor in Mumbai who marks this work looks at the four criteria as four separate jobs rather than one general quality called good English. Some parents type an entire phrase into Google, something close to "MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai", and this is what sits behind it.

In Year 5 the personal project runs alongside the subject groups, and language and literature quietly decides how it reads. The project report has to organise a process, address a reader and sustain a line of thought over length, which is the same set of skills the subject assesses all year. Students who have been taught to structure for a reader write a report that makes sense; students who have only been taught to write beautifully produce something nobody can follow. The exact strands and descriptors your school marks against are in the current subject guide, so ask the MYP coordinator for the version in force rather than working from an older summary.

sections.heading: Why a strong reader can still sit in the middle band
paragraphs: The most common profile an IB MYP language and literature tutor in Mumbai meets is a capable reader whose responses retell. The student explains what happens in the chapter, accurately and with feeling, and the marker writes "more analysis needed" for the fourth time. Retelling and analysing feel similar from the inside, which is why telling a student to analyse more rarely changes anything. The practical fix is mechanical. Take one sentence from the text and ask three questions: what choice did the writer make here, what is the effect of that choice on a reader, and how do you know. Do that twenty times across a term and the habit replaces the summary.

Structure is the second thing in the way, and it is the one students resent most. A response that an examiner can follow has a visible shape: a line of argument stated early, paragraphs that each do one job, and transitions that signal where the argument has got to. Most mid-band writing has the ideas in it but in the order they occurred to the writer. A tutor fixes this by working on the plan rather than the prose, often by making the student write their paragraph openings first and read them in sequence to see whether an argument is actually there. It takes ten minutes and it is more useful than an hour of editing.

Then there is audience and purpose, which MYP tasks state explicitly and students skim past. A task that asks for a speech to a school assembly, a column for a newspaper, a letter to a character or a review for a magazine is not asking for a general essay in a costume. The register, the sentence lengths, the assumed knowledge and the ending all change. The last piece is precision at sentence level: choosing the specific verb, cutting the sentence that repeats the last one, making a pronoun point somewhere unambiguous. This is the difference between a good sentence and a sentence that scores, and it is teachable in a way that vague advice about style is not.

sections.heading: Home tuition and tutors across the six zones of Mumbai
paragraphs: IB Gram matches across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and a weekly language and literature slot lives or dies on travel. In South Mumbai, families in Fort, Churchgate, Malabar Hill, Prabhadevi and Mahalaxmi are usually matched within the island, because a tutor coming down from the suburbs for a six o'clock session is making a promise the Peddar Road signals will break by October. The Churchgate to Mumbai Central run of the Western Line, the Harbour Line out of CSMT, Metro Line 3 towards Bandra Kurla Complex and the Coastal Road all help, and the Bandra Worli Sea Link makes a Worli to Bandra pairing genuinely workable in a way a Worli to Andheri pairing is not.

In the Western Suburbs the line is the organising fact. Khar West to Santacruz West, Juhu to Andheri West, Malad West to Kandivali and Borivali to Dahisar are all sound weekly pairings along the Western Express Highway, the Link Road and the Western Line, with Metro Lines 1, 2A and 7 covering tutors who travel without a car. In the Central Suburbs, Ghatkopar, Kurla and Vikhroli sit on the Central Line while Powai and Chandivali hang off JVLR with no station, so those matches are made by road from Andheri East or Kanjurmarg and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road carries the rest.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Bhandup to Mulund West along the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway making Wadala and Chembur unexpectedly close to the island. sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar behind every language and literature deadline
paragraphs: Mumbai international schools run roughly June to April, and language and literature produces more assessed pieces across that year than most subject groups, because every unit ends in something written. The first summative tasks land from late July, often a response to a short text while the class is still settling. October and November bring longer analytical writing, usually on the main set text of the term. February and March are heaviest, with final unit tasks, oral or presentation components at some schools, and in Year 5 the personal project report competing for the same fortnight.

Knowing your own school's shape matters more than knowing the general one. Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School at Goregaon East on JVLR both run the Primary Years Programme, MYP and Diploma Programme and build their MYP writing expectations towards Diploma Programme work. Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Chembur, Thakur International School in Kandivali East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai sit on IB or Cambridge International Education pathways with their own submission weeks. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools; they appear here because their calendars are what a weekly slot has to fit around.

The scheduling lesson is to start in a flat month. A family that begins in late June or in the first fortnight of January gives the tutor room to work on analysing and structure before anything counts for much. A family that calls in the week a response is due is asking for editing, which is the one service a tutor must not supply. A Year 4 student in Chembur who starts in June will have written five or six pieces with feedback before the heavy February stretch arrives; the same student starting in February gets two rushed sessions and a document somebody else shaped. The first version costs less and teaches something.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid for a reading and writing subject?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the first option worth pricing, and for this subject the argument is specific rather than sentimental. An IB home tutor in Mumbai sitting beside a student can put a printed page between them, mark it in pencil while the student watches, and ask the student to read their own paragraph aloud, which is the fastest diagnostic in the subject. Reading aloud exposes a clumsy sentence instantly and no student does it voluntarily on a screen. IB home tuition in Mumbai for language and literature usually runs as one weekly session built around a single piece of writing, rising to two in a heavy fortnight.

Online is a real alternative rather than a fallback, and for older MYP students it has genuine advantages. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can put the set text, a model response and the student's draft side by side, and leave comments next to the exact sentence they refer to, which the student can reread on Thursday. It also widens the pool, and the supply of tutors who have actually marked MYP language and literature responses is thinner than the supply of English tutors generally. For families in Panvel, Dahisar or Kasarvadavali that difference in pool size usually matters more than the difference in format.

Hybrid is where most families land after a term: one in-person session for the teaching and one short screen session midweek to check that a draft exists. Two honest cautions apply whichever way you go. The first is that a good deal of MYP writing is still done by hand in class under time pressure, so the student needs regular handwritten practice and not only typed drafts with a tutor's comments alongside. The second is that an IB private tutor Mumbai families hire for this subject should be marking less and questioning more. If the draft comes back covered in corrections the student did not make themselves, you are buying a tidier document rather than a better writer.
bullets: Home sessions allow reading aloud and pencil marking, the fastest diagnostics here
Online suits older MYP students and puts text, model and draft side by side

sections.heading: How tutors are verified before a first session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Verification runs the same way for every tutor listed. Identity is confirmed against government photo identification, qualifications are checked against the original documents, and teaching claims are tested in a subject interview rather than taken on trust. For this subject the interview is practical: the candidate is given an anonymised MYP response, asked to mark it against the four criteria, and asked to say what they would do in the next session with the student who wrote it. Candidates who talk about literary terminology and not about the student tend not to progress. Every IB MYP language and literature tutor in Mumbai listed with us has cleared that interview before a family ever sees the profile, and the same applies whether you book home tuition or online sessions. An IB tutor Mumbai parents find informally through a building group has usually had no equivalent check at all.

One part of the brief we take seriously concerns language itself. Mumbai students arrive speaking Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati, Tamil, Konkani, Urdu and several more at home, and many of them speak and write Indian English, which is a complete and legitimate variety of English with its own history and conventions. A tutor who treats that as something to correct out of a child is doing damage and is also wrong about the subject. Multilingual students notice how language works, because they switch register and code every day; that awareness is exactly what criterion A rewards once someone shows them how to use it. What a tutor teaches is how to write for the audience and purpose a particular task names, which is a skill, not a replacement of how a family speaks.

The checks you make yourself are short. Listen to ten minutes of the first session and count who is talking. After a fortnight, ask your child to explain what their last response was arguing, in one sentence, without the paper. Look at the draft and see whose sentences are in it. A tutor may question, model, mark and give written feedback. A tutor may never write, dictate or supply any part of assessed work, and the student signs an academic honesty declaration that has to be true. Be wary of anyone offering a guaranteed grade: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor who promises a specific grade is describing something they do not control.
bullets: Photo identification and original qualification documents checked before listing
Interview requires marking a real MYP response and planning the next session

sections.heading: What a tutor diagnoses in the first hour, and in what order
paragraphs: A first hour with an IB MYP language and literature tutor in Mumbai is a diagnosis, and the order matters because fixing the wrong thing wastes a term. The tutor starts with comprehension, briefly: does the student understand the text at the level the task requires. This is rarely the problem for the students families bring to us, and establishing that it is fine in five minutes saves everyone from an unnecessary programme of reading support. Then the tutor looks at the response itself and asks whether it analyses or recounts, which is visible in the verbs. "The writer shows" and "the writer repeats the phrase so that" are analysis; "then he goes to" and "after that she decides" are recounting, however elegantly written.

Third comes structure, tested by the paragraph-opening exercise: read only the first sentence of each paragraph in order and see whether an argument appears. If it does not, the student is not short of ideas, they are short of a plan, and the next four sessions are about planning rather than writing. Fourth is the task's stated audience and purpose, checked by asking the student who they were writing for. A surprising number cannot say, because nobody has ever told them it was a real instruction rather than decoration on the task sheet.

Fifth and last is language, and it is last deliberately. Sentence-level precision is the slowest thing to shift and the easiest to obsess over, and a student whose structure is unsound gains nothing from better vocabulary. When the tutor does reach it, the work is concrete: cut the sentence that repeats the previous one, replace the three-word phrase with the one exact verb, make the pronoun point at something, vary the sentence length on purpose rather than by accident. One paragraph rewritten properly teaches more than ten paragraphs corrected.

What comes out of that hour is a short written plan, and a parent should expect to see it. It names the one thing being worked on first, how it will be practised, and roughly what will have changed by the fourth session. The plan does not promise a grade. A student who learns to analyse in October is a different writer by March, and how that translates into marks depends on the school's tasks, the student's work between sessions and a dozen other things no tutor controls.
bullets: Check comprehension first and briefly; it is rarely the real problem
Test analysing versus recounting by looking at the verbs in the response
Read paragraph openings in sequence to see whether an argument exists
Ask the student who the task told them to write for
Work on sentence precision last, one rewritten paragraph at a time

sections.heading: What does progress look like after four weeks of home tuition?
paragraphs: At four weeks of weekly home tuition, look for changed behaviour and not a changed grade. A student who has had four sessions should be able to point at a sentence in a text and say what the writer did and what effect it has. They should be planning before writing, even badly. They should be able to tell you who their last piece was written for. In most Mumbai schools nothing summative will have been marked in that window, so a report card is not available as evidence, and judging the month by one is simply measuring the wrong thing too early.

At one term the marks begin to say something. The comparison worth making is between the teacher's comments on the first assessed response and the comments on the third. Movement usually appears in analysing and organising first, because those respond to a method a student can apply deliberately. Using language shifts more slowly, because sentence-level control is built over years rather than weeks, and a parent who expects it to move in a month will be disappointed by real progress happening elsewhere. If by the end of a term the teacher is writing different things, the arrangement is working.

Over a full year, be honest about the limits. A tutor has one or two hours a week and no control over whether a draft gets written on Sunday. Students develop at different rates, which says nothing about ability and nothing about any individual child. A Year 1 student and a Year 5 student are different situations entirely. Some of what presents as a writing problem is a reading-time problem, a sleep problem or six subject groups landing in the same fortnight. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and nobody who understands this subject would.

When it is not working, four weeks is enough to tell. The signs are consistent: the student cannot say what the last session was about, the drafts come back heavily corrected rather than rewritten by the student, or the sessions have become a reading club. Tell us what specifically is wrong and a replacement shortlist comes back in a few days, with the previous feedback and plan passed on so the new tutor does not start from nothing. Changing in week five costs a fortnight. Changing in March costs the year.
bullets: Four weeks: the student can name a writer's choice and its effect on a reader
Four weeks: planning happens before writing, and the audience can be stated
One term: compare teacher comments on the first and third assessed responses
Analysing and organising move before using language does

sections.heading: Booking a language and literature tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Getting started needs one message and three attachments: the last marked response with comments, the current task sheet, and the name of the text or unit the class is working on now. Add two sentences about what you have actually noticed, because parents see things reports do not. The writing takes four hours and still comes out thin. The feedback has said the same thing three times. The student loves the book and freezes at the task. A request for a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai families can hold weekly starts with that material and nothing more elaborate.

Next, settle the practical details once instead of weekly. Say your zone and locality, your preferred slot, and whether a weekday evening or a weekend morning is realistic given the corridor you live on. If your society requires visitor approval, register the tutor as a standing weekly entry rather than arranging it each time. Say where in the home the session will happen, since a table away from a television matters more for an hour of writing than for most subjects. If you want a hybrid arrangement rather than straight home classes, say so now, because it changes which tutors are shortlisted.

The first session has a shape you should expect. The tutor reads the marked work before arriving, spends most of the hour on one real piece of the student's own writing, and ends by sending you a short written plan: what the student already does well, the one thing being worked on first, and what the next four sessions will cover. You decide afterwards whether to continue, and if the answer is no you say so and a new shortlist comes back. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school, and we do not guarantee grades.

On fees, the honest answer is a list of factors rather than a number. Rates move with the year group and level, with how scarce the specialism is, with session length and weekly frequency, and with travel distance where the tutor is coming to you. A tutor crossing the Sea Link or driving the length of Ghodbunder Road is pricing road time as well as teaching time. Ask for the rate, the session length and the travel assumption together, in writing, before the first session rather than discovering them after it.
