No external exams, so reports and conferences are your only early signal

sections.heading: Oral, written and visual language: what a PYP English tutor actually teaches
paragraphs: PYP language is organised into three strands, and a good tutor names which one they are working on each week. Oral language covers listening and speaking. Written language covers reading and writing. Visual language covers viewing and presenting, which is the strand Mumbai parents are least aware of and the one that surprises them when the child has to stand up and present. Most children are uneven across the three, and a descriptor-based report often averages that unevenness away.

Take a How We Express Ourselves unit on the way stories carry culture. The class reads folk tales, including Marathi and Gujarati ones in translation, then writes its own retelling and performs it. A tutor who understands the unit works on four separate things in that fortnight: the narrative shape, so the retelling has a problem and a resolution rather than a list of events; paragraphing and dialogue punctuation, taught on the child's own draft rather than in an exercise; a vocabulary bank the child collects from the reading and is then expected to use; and the oral rehearsal, which for a shy Grade 3 child in Bandra is often the hardest part and the part nobody practises. A tutor who ignores the unit hands over a photocopied comprehension sheet, and the class teacher sees no change at all.

On the reading side the useful work is diagnostic before it is remedial. A tutor listens to the child read aloud, notes what kind of error repeats, and separates decoding problems from comprehension problems, because those two need opposite interventions. Then the questioning gets deliberate: retrieval questions the text answers directly, inference questions the text only implies, and evaluation questions about why the writer chose that word. Children in English-medium PYP classrooms across Mumbai are frequently strong at retrieval and weak at inference, and a parent cannot see the difference by listening to fluent reading at bedtime.

On the writing side the PYP portfolio is the evidence, so ask to see it. A tutor should be able to flip through a term of the child's own writing and point at what has not changed: still no planning, still one long sentence joined with and, still no paragraph break. Conventions get taught against that evidence. Spelling lists in isolation rarely transfer. Spelling patterns pulled out of the child's own drafts usually do, because the child already cares about that piece of writing.
bullets: Oral, written and visual language are reported separately and progress unevenly
Reading work starts diagnostic: decoding errors and comprehension gaps need opposite fixes
Retrieval, inference and evaluation questions, practised in that order, on real texts
Conventions taught on the child's own draft, not on a photocopied worksheet
Oral rehearsal before every presentation, including the final-year PYP exhibition

sections.heading: Which parts of Mumbai do PYP English home tutors cover?
paragraphs: All six Mumbai zones: South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane. The rule we match by is simple. A tutor who already lives or teaches in your zone will hold a weekday evening slot for a full term. One brought across the city will start rescheduling by the fifth week, whatever they promised in October.

In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock still beats you. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a few kilometres and can lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at 6pm, so we match inside the island: Cuffe Parade with Colaba, Walkeshwar with Babulnath, Worli with Lower Parel. The Western Line from Churchgate to Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line down to Dockyard, Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade towards BKC and the Coastal Road all help a tutor who is already south of Mahalaxmi. In the Western Suburbs everything runs along the line, so Khar West to Santacruz West works, Malad to Kandivali works, and Bandra to Andheri at 6.30pm does not. The Western Express Highway, Link Road, Metro Line 1 from Versova to Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 up to Dahisar carry most of our Juhu, Vile Parle, Goregaon and Borivali matches.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so Powai tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. The SCLR, the Santacruz to Chembur link road, is what makes a Kurla or Chembur tutor viable in Powai at all. In the Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund, the Eastern Freeway puts South Mumbai closer to Wadala and Chembur than the map suggests, and the Harbour Line carries the rest. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway: Vashi with Nerul, Belapur with Kharghar, Panvel on its own. The Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line have changed what is possible across the creek, but we still do not build a weekly 7pm lesson around either. Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes from the station off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak. The Bandra Worli Sea Link helps a Bandra tutor reach Worli, and very little else.

A search for IB tutors near me Mumbai returns people who will say yes to any postcode. Ask the question the other way round. An IB PYP English tutor in Mumbai who lives in Thane West and already teaches two children on Pokhran Road will give your Friday slot the same reliability she gives theirs. We would rather tell you we have nobody in Panvel this month than send someone whose commute will not survive the term.
bullets: South Mumbai matched inside the island: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Worli
Western Suburbs matched along the Western Line, not across the highway
Powai and Chandivali reached by road via JVLR and the SCLR
Navi Mumbai matched node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Panvel
Thane slots planned around Ghodbunder Road, not around a map distance

sections.heading: What the Mumbai school year does to a PYP reader and writer
paragraphs: Most Mumbai PYP schools open the academic year in late July or August and close it in May, with the long break through the hottest weeks. Check your own school's calendar, because they differ, but the pressure points are predictable and almost nobody plans for them. The first one is not an assessment at all. It is the monsoon.

From the end of June into September a 6pm home lesson in Mumbai is at the mercy of water on the Western Express Highway, a slow Central Line and a flooded subway at Milan. Families who book tutoring in July lose sessions in August and conclude that tutoring does not work. Agree a monsoon rule in the first week: the session moves online rather than cancelling. Then comes the Diwali break in October or November, which is the best catch-up window in the Mumbai year. A child who reads every day for those two weeks starts the second term visibly ahead, and a child who touches nothing comes back having lost fluency. Tutors are also free in that window at hours that are impossible in term time.

Families we work with have children at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School on JVLR in Goregaon East, both of which run the PYP, and at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, JBCN International School, Parel, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools, or with the IB itself. We name them because their calendars and their language expectations are what a tutor has to work around.

January and February bring the parent-teacher conference where language concerns usually surface for the first time, and for Grade 5 families the Middle Years Programme transition conversation lands in the same window. February to April is the final-year exhibition term, plus portfolios and end-of-year reports across every grade. If you want a tutor working on written output before the summer report, start in November, not in March. A tutor who begins six weeks before a report can produce a child who writes more. They cannot produce a term of evidence that was never collected.
bullets: Monsoon weeks from late June: agree an online fallback in advance
Diwali break is the best catch-up window in the Mumbai year
January conferences are where language concerns usually surface first
February to April: exhibition term, portfolios and end-of-year reports
Start in November if you want change visible in the summer report

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for PYP English in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default at PYP ages and it is what most families book. A seven-year-old does not manage a screen, a mouse and a pencil at the same time. An IB home tutor in Mumbai sitting at your table can put the child's actual reading folder, portfolio and library book in front of her, watch the pencil grip and the rereading, and stop the moment the child's attention goes. The tutor also sees the room the child works in, which often explains the writing problem faster than any diagnostic.

The honest cost of home classes is travel, and you pay it whether you see it or not. A tutor who crosses two zones for a 7pm lesson is giving up a second booking, which shows up in the rate and in how long the arrangement lasts. Home tuition also needs a fixed weekly slot, a cancellation rule and a clear arrangement at the gate. Decide all three in week one. An IB PYP English home tutor in Mumbai who has to argue with a security desk every Thursday will eventually suggest moving online, and you will not know why.

Online earns its place in three situations. The first is scarcity: a mother-tongue or English-as-an-additional-language specialist your zone simply does not have. The second is traffic, which is the Peddar Road and Ghodbunder Road problem, and the monsoon. The third is frequency, where two short online sessions a week beat one long home session for a child building a reading habit. An IB online tutor in Mumbai needs a different setup for a PYP child than for a Diploma Programme (DP) student: an adult nearby for the first five minutes, the book physically in the child's hands rather than on screen, and the writing task done on paper and photographed afterwards.

Hybrid is what most of our PYP language families settle into after a term. One home session a week for the reading, writing and talking that needs a person in the room, and one short online session for a vocabulary review or a plan check before a presentation. Some families run home tuition in the dry months and switch to online through August. A home tutor for PYP transdisciplinary learning Mumbai parents book in July should be asked, in July, how they want to handle the week the roads flood.
bullets: Home tuition suits PYP ages: physical books, visible handwriting, no screen
Travel across zones shows up in the rate and in reliability
Online solves scarcity, traffic and the monsoon, not attention span
Two short online sessions can beat one long home session weekly
Hybrid: home for writing and talking, online for review and planning

sections.heading: How is an IB PYP English tutor in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Before an IB PYP English tutor in Mumbai reaches your shortlist we verify identity and qualification documents, check the stated Primary Years Programme teaching or tutoring history against references, and ask the tutor to talk through how they would run a first session with a child of your grade. Anyone who cannot describe a programme of inquiry does not get sent out.

Verification on this platform means four concrete things. We see government identity proof. We see degree and teaching qualification documents, and confirm the subject and level claimed rather than the level implied. We take references for the PYP work specifically, because secondary experience does not transfer downwards: a strong Diploma Programme English teacher is often a poor Grade 2 reading tutor, and the reverse is true too. And we ask for a worked answer to a real case, usually a child who reads fluently and writes almost nothing, then listen for whether the plan starts with the child's portfolio or with a workbook.

What we do not claim is that a document check predicts how your child will respond to a stranger in the house. Do your own checking in the first two sessions. Ask the tutor which unit of inquiry the class is in, and whether they have read the school's language policy. Ask for a written plan after session one. Sit within earshot of that session rather than in the room. Ask what they will stop doing if the approach is not working by week four. Be wary of anyone who promises a specific report descriptor, or who talks about outcomes at a primary age as though they were fixed.

Parents regularly ask us to name the best IB tutor in Mumbai for Grade 2 reading, and there is no such person in the abstract. There is a tutor who is right for a child who has lost confidence and wrong for a child who is simply bored, and those two sit in the same band with the same documents on file. The question that gets you a good match is narrower. Which of your tutors has taught a Grade 2 child who reads well and refuses to write, and what did she do in the first month?
bullets: Government identity proof seen and recorded before any match is sent
Degree and teaching qualifications confirmed for the level actually claimed
References taken for PYP work, not for secondary teaching experience
A worked first-session plan requested and read before approval
Ask your tutor which unit of inquiry the class is in

sections.heading: Reading comprehension, bilingual homes and the Grade 5 handover to MYP
paragraphs: The commonest reason a Mumbai parent looks for a PYP English tutor is a child who reads aloud beautifully and understands less than you think. Fluent decoding hides a comprehension gap for years, and in a classroom where discussion is quick and oral a child can follow the shape of a conversation without following the text. The diagnostic is easy to run at home. Ask your child why a character did something, not what they did. Retrieval answers come instantly. Inference answers come slowly or not at all. A child who can retell a chapter but cannot say what the author wanted you to feel is not a weak reader, she is an unpractised one, and that is where an IB PYP English tutor in Mumbai earns the weekly slot.

The writing problem is usually the opposite shape. PYP children write often and briefly, in bursts attached to a unit, and then around Grade 4 the expectation becomes sustained and organised. Children who were never taught to plan simply write longer versions of a Grade 2 paragraph. The work is unglamorous: a planning frame simple enough that the child uses it without being asked, oral rehearsal before the pencil moves, and a hard separation between revising, which changes what the writing says, and editing, which fixes spelling and punctuation. Children who conflate the two produce neat, empty paragraphs and cannot understand why the teacher is unmoved. A tutor should be able to show you two drafts of one piece and point at what changed between them.

Mumbai homes are rarely monolingual. Marathi, Gujarati, Hindi, Konkani, Tamil and Bengali are spoken at home while school runs in English, and parents often decide, wrongly, that the home language is the problem. The IB's position on mother-tongue language is the opposite: the home language is an asset and schools are expected to support it. What actually helps is a vocabulary bridge. A child who owns a concept in Gujarati does not need to relearn the concept, only to label it in English, and a tutor who speaks the home language can do that in a sentence where a monolingual tutor spends a session. Children arriving into PYP from a CBSE or ICSE school have a different gap again: solid grammar drill, weak independent writing, and no experience of being asked for an opinion about a text.

The final PYP year contains a handover nobody announces. Middle Years Programme (MYP) Language and Literature is criterion-assessed, expects longer analytical writing, and assumes a child can take notes, read across genres and present without a script. A child who leaves PYP reading only fiction and only in short bursts feels that change in the first MYP term, usually in October of Grade 6. The useful last-year work is a reading log with genres deliberately mixed, note-taking in the child's own words rather than copied phrases, and oral stamina built by presenting to an adult who asks follow-up questions. Visual language matters here too. Reading an infographic, a photograph or an advertisement is assessed later and taught lightly now.
bullets: Ask why a character acted, not what they did, to test inference
Planning frames and oral rehearsal before the pencil moves on paper
Revising changes meaning, editing fixes spelling, and children confuse them
Home-language vocabulary bridges beat banning Marathi or Gujarati at the table
Final PYP year: mixed-genre reading log, note-taking, presenting without a script

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one year of PYP English tutoring look like
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see habits, not results. The child picks up a book without being told, uses a planning sheet unprompted, or stops resisting at writing time. Those three are the honest early signals and they are visible to any parent who is paying attention. What you will not see at four weeks is a changed report, because PYP reporting runs on evidence collected across a whole term. If none of the three has shifted by week five or six, the match is wrong and we should be discussing a replacement rather than giving it more time.

At one term the class teacher starts to notice, and that signal matters more than anything we tell you. The comments change from needs support with written expression to writes at length with increasing control, the child volunteers for a presentation, the portfolio holds a piece the child is actually proud of. On the reading side a term is usually enough to move inference from guessing to reasoning, provided the child is reading at home between sessions. One session a week with nothing in between moves very little, and any tutor who tells you otherwise is selling.

Across a full year the realistic outcome is a child who goes into the next PYP year, or into MYP, without a language problem being the thing every adult discusses. That is worth more than it sounds. We do not guarantee grades or report descriptors, and no honest tutor will tell you otherwise. There are limits you should hear before you book. A tutor cannot diagnose a specific learning difficulty, and a child who still cannot decode reliably by Grade 3 needs a proper assessment from an educational psychologist or a speech and language professional, not more tuition. A tutor also cannot replace daily classroom teaching, or read at home on your behalf.

When it is not working, the sequence is short. Tell us in week four or five with one specific example rather than a general feeling. We put it to the tutor once, because many of these turn out to be a slot problem, a child who is exhausted at 7pm, or a pace mismatch, and all three are fixable in a conversation. If it is not fixable we send a replacement profile, and the new tutor gets the portfolio, the previous plan and a note on what did not land, so your child does not sit through the same baseline session twice in a month.
bullets: Four weeks: habits change, reports do not, and that is normal
Five or six weeks with no habit shift means a wrong match
One term: teacher comments change and inference becomes reasoning, with home reading
Persistent decoding trouble by Grade 3 needs assessment, not more tuition
Replacement tutors receive the portfolio, the plan and what did not work

sections.heading: Booking home classes for PYP English in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have five things on the table for the first session: the child's PYP portfolio or reading folder, the most recent report, the letter or email about the current unit of inquiry, whatever the class teacher said at the last conference, and the book the child is reading now. If you have the school's language policy, add it. A tutor who gets those five runs a diagnostic in one session instead of three, and you pay for one.

Pick the slot honestly. A Grade 2 child who gets home at 4.30 after a long bus run up the Western Express Highway is finished by 6.30, so an evening slot that suits your calendar may be useless for her. Earlier on a weekday, or a mid-morning weekend slot, often works better at these ages. Clear a table with a lamp and no television in the line of sight, and keep phones out of the room, including yours. Tell the security desk the tutor's name and the standing day so that the gate pass is not a weekly negotiation.

The first session is assessment and conversation, not teaching. Expect the tutor to listen to your child read aloud, ask the kind of questions that separate retrieval from inference, look at two pieces of recent writing, and talk to the child about what she actually likes reading. Expect no homework from session one. Within a couple of days you should have a short written plan: the two or three things the next four weeks will work on, what the tutor wants done between sessions, and what you should be able to see by week four. PYP transdisciplinary learning home classes Mumbai families book without that plan tend to drift into general English practice by the second month.

If you are still deciding between two tutors, ask each of them the same question. What would you do in the first twenty minutes with my child? The answers separate people quickly. One will describe a book, a conversation and a piece of the child's own writing. Another will describe a level test. Both are defensible, but you know your child, and you know which one will walk out of that room willing to do it again next week.
bullets: Bring the portfolio, the last report and the current unit letter
Pick a slot before the child is finished for the day
Table, lamp, no television in view, and every phone out of the room
Give the security desk the tutor's name and the standing weekly day
Expect a written four-week plan within two days of session one

faqs.question: Does a PYP child really need an English tutor when there are no exams?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the absence of exams is exactly why the question is hard to answer. PYP reporting is descriptor-based, so a language gap can sit quietly behind a phrase like developing as a communicator until Grade 4 or Grade 5, when written work gets longer and the gap becomes visible to everyone including the child. A tutor is worth booking when something specific is happening: a child who will not write, a child who reads fluently and cannot infer, a child who has joined PYP from another board, or a child heading into the Middle Years Programme next year. General topping-up with no named problem is usually a wasted weekday evening.

faqs.question: My child reads fluently but writes almost nothing. What would a tutor actually do?
faqs.answer: Start with the child's own drafts, not a workbook. The first job is working out whether the block is ideas, structure, or the physical act of writing, because all three look identical from outside. A tutor will usually have the child talk the piece through before writing it, give a planning frame simple enough to use unprompted, and separate revising from editing so the child is not fixing spelling while still deciding what to say. Progress at four weeks looks like a plan the child makes without being asked and a draft that has a middle. Longer, neater paragraphs come after that, not first.

faqs.question: We speak Gujarati and Marathi at home. Should we switch to English to help her English?
faqs.answer: No, and switching usually makes things worse. The Primary Years Programme treats the home language as an asset, and schools are expected to support mother-tongue development rather than suppress it. A child who understands a concept in Gujarati already owns that concept and only needs the English label for it, which is fast work for a tutor. Dropping the home language removes the richest vocabulary the child has, and it often costs confidence at the same time. What does help is a tutor who can bridge both languages in a sentence, plus reading aloud at home in whichever language the adult reads best.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a PYP English tutor?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a published price list. Board and level matter, because a PYP language tutor and a Diploma Programme Physics tutor are not in the same band. Subject scarcity matters: a mother-tongue or additional-language specialist in a zone with few of them is harder to book than a general primary tutor. Travel distance matters, because a tutor crossing from Khar West to Powai is giving up a second booking that evening. Session length and frequency matter, and so does whether you want home tuition or online. Ask any tutor to quote the full weekly cost including travel before you commit to a term.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Kharghar for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the tutor is already based in Navi Mumbai. We match Kharghar with Belapur and Nerul rather than pulling someone across the creek, because a tutor coming from the island city for a 7pm lesson along the Sion Panvel Highway or over the Atal Setu keeps it up for a few weeks and then starts rescheduling. Palm Beach Road makes node-to-node travel genuinely quick, which is why node matching works here. If there is nobody suitable in your node in a given month we will say so and offer online, rather than booking a commute that collapses in week five.

faqs.question: Our society gate needs a visitor pass every time. How does that work for a weekly home tutor?
faqs.answer: Set up a standing entry on day one and it stops being a problem. Give the security desk the tutor's name, the day and the time, and ask whether your society issues a recurring pass for service visitors, which most of the larger complexes in Powai, Thane and Navi Mumbai do. Without it the tutor spends ten minutes at the desk every week and the lesson shrinks to fit. If your building requires a resident to approve each entry through an app, tell the tutor which app it is and who in the family will be reachable at that hour.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, but not in the room. At PYP ages a parent in the doorway changes how the child answers questions, and the tutor loses the honest version of what the child can do alone. The arrangement that works is to stay within earshot for the first two or three sessions, then step back to the last five minutes, which is when the tutor should tell you what happened. Ask for that handover every week. It is more informative than a monthly report, and it is where you catch a drifting arrangement early enough to fix it.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for a seven-year-old?
faqs.answer: It works for some things and not others. Vocabulary review, reading aloud, a plan check before a presentation and short frequent sessions all transfer to a screen. Extended writing, handwriting and a child who needs physical redirection do not. A PYP child also needs an adult to start the call and then leave, which is more work for you than a home session. Online makes most sense when the specialist you need is not in your zone, during the monsoon weeks, or when Ghodbunder Road or Peddar Road at 6pm makes a reliable weekly home slot impossible. Most of our PYP families end up hybrid.

faqs.question: Four weeks in and I see no change. What should I do now?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week four with one specific example rather than waiting for the term to end. Then check what you are measuring, because at four weeks the honest signals are habits: does the child pick up a book unprompted, use a planning sheet, stop resisting writing time. If none of those has moved, the match is probably wrong, and we will put it to the tutor once since a surprising share of these turn out to be a slot problem, a child who is exhausted at 7pm, or a pace mismatch. If that conversation does not fix it, you get a replacement profile and the new tutor inherits the plan.

faqs.question: The tutor is competent but my child does not like her. Can we change?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should say so early rather than hoping it settles down. At primary ages the relationship is most of the method. A child who dreads the session will not read between sessions, and reading between sessions is where the progress actually lives. Ask for the change in the first few weeks. We send a replacement profile, pass on the portfolio, the previous plan and a note on what did not land, and ask the new tutor to skip a full baseline so your child is not assessed twice in a month. You do not owe the first tutor an explanation.

faqs.question: My child joined an IB PYP school in Juhu from CBSE mid-year. Where does a tutor start?
faqs.answer: With what the new school is asking for, which is almost never what the old one drilled. Children arriving from CBSE or ICSE usually have solid grammar and spelling and no experience of being asked for an opinion about a text, choosing their own reading, or presenting an inquiry to a class. An IB PYP English tutor in Mumbai will typically spend the first fortnight on exactly that: inference questions, short opinion writing with reasons attached, and the vocabulary of the unit of inquiry the class is already halfway through. The grammar does not need redoing. What needs building is independence, and a child who has never chosen a book needs help choosing one.

ib-pyp-english-tutor.closingCta: Send us the grade, the school and the two evenings that work. We come back with two or three verified profiles, each with what they have taught and the slots they can actually hold, and you speak to the one you like before anything is booked. The first session happens at your home, or online if you prefer, and you get a written four-week plan after it. If the match is wrong, tell us and we replace the tutor.

sections.heading: How we shortlist an IB PYP exhibition home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: The query that arrives is almost never "teach my child the PYP". It is usually a parent in Khar West or Chembur writing in the week the school mentor has asked for a second draft of the lines of inquiry, and the child has a folder of printouts about sea turtles and no argument holding them together. So the first thing we ask for is not a budget. It is the grade, the school, the date of the presentation, and the single part of the exhibition that has stopped moving: the central idea, the research, the action, the display, or the oral presentation.

The second thing we ask for is your address and your usable weekday window. Those two answers shape the shortlist more than anything academic. A family on Pokhran Road in Thane and a family in Cuffe Parade are asking for the same help, and they will be matched from completely different pools, because a tutor who has to cross the city at 6pm will start cancelling by the third week. We match along a corridor rather than across it: Wadala to Chembur on the Eastern Freeway, Khar to Santacruz on the Western Line, Vashi to Nerul on Palm Beach Road.

Then you get two or three profiles instead of twenty. Each one says what the tutor has taught, how long they have worked with the final primary year, whether they have supported an exhibition before or only taught subject lessons, and where they actually live. You speak to each tutor before anyone is scheduled. The first session at your home is diagnostic: the tutor reads the child's process journal and the school's exhibition brief, asks the child to explain the central idea out loud with nobody prompting, and writes down what is genuinely missing rather than what a template says should be missing.

We do not send whoever is nearest and hope it holds. We do not accept a request to produce the project, and no tutor on the platform will build the display board for a child. PYP transdisciplinary learning home classes Mumbai families book for the exhibition are supervision of a child's own inquiry, which is slower and far less tidy than doing it for them, and it is the only version the school will accept when it asks who helped.
bullets: 1. Send the grade, the school, the presentation date and the stuck part.
2. Tell us your address, your building's visitor rules and your usable evening window.
3. We shortlist two or three tutors who already travel your corridor.
4. You speak to each tutor yourself before any session is scheduled.
5. The first home session is diagnostic, not a lesson from a plan.
6. If the fit is wrong we change the tutor and keep your slot.

sections.heading: Where the exhibition sits in the Primary Years Programme, and what Mumbai schools do differently
paragraphs: The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the primary school and closes with the exhibition, a collaborative student-led inquiry in the final PYP year. Which year that is depends on the school: some Mumbai schools call it Grade 5 and others, using a different year nomenclature, call it Year 6. Ask your school's PYP coordinator which year group and which term, and ask for the written exhibition brief, because the structure, the submission points and the mentor arrangements are set by the school and not by a single national pattern.

The exhibition is internally organised and internally assessed. There is no external examination paper behind it, which is exactly why it unsettles parents who have older children in the Diploma Programme (DP) and are used to a published timetable. What the exhibition asks for is a transdisciplinary theme, a central idea written as a concept rather than a fact, lines of inquiry that each do a different job, sustained research the child can account for, an action that follows from the finding, a process journal kept as the work happens, and a presentation to the school community. A home tutor's remit sits around all of that, never inside it.

Families at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School in Goregaon East take the PYP through to the exhibition on the way to the Middle Years Programme (MYP), while families heading towards Dhirubhai Ambani International School or the American School of Bombay in BKC meet the IB later in a child's schooling. A parent whose first child is in DP2 already knows the rhythm. A first-time PYP parent is being told to stand back from a project with a deadline for the first time, which is usually when the search starts. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page.

Parents type long search strings at this point, including PYP transdisciplinary learning IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor Mumbai, and arrive looking for someone who understands both halves of that phrase. The two halves matter. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who has only taught Diploma Programme (DP) Physics is the wrong fit for a ten-year-old's inquiry, however strong the subject knowledge is, because the skill being taught here is not content. It is how to hold a question open for eight weeks without either abandoning it or handing it to an adult.

sections.heading: The parts of the exhibition a home tutor can actually help with
paragraphs: The exhibition is transdisciplinary by design, so the help a child needs is rarely subject help. Take a Grade 5 child at a Bandra school working under the theme of sharing the planet, who has chosen the mangroves off Carter Road. Her central idea reads as a fact about mangrove cover. Her three lines of inquiry read as three topics: types of mangroves, why mangroves are cut, animals that live in mangroves. A PYP transdisciplinary learning tutor in Mumbai spends the first two sessions turning that into one idea with a concept inside it, something about responsibility and consequence, after which the three lines of inquiry each have a different job instead of doing the same job three times.

The second block of work is research skill, and it is where most of the home sessions go. A ten-year-old needs to learn the difference between a source and a search result, how to write down where something came from at the moment of finding it rather than the night before submission, and how to decide whether a page is telling them something or selling them something. Interviews are the part Mumbai children can genuinely do well: a society gardener, a neighbour who works in environmental consultancy, a fisherman at Versova. A tutor teaches how to write six questions, how to ask permission, and how to record an answer without transcribing it word for word.

The learner profile is the third block, and it is misread constantly. The exhibition asks the child to show the IB learner profile attributes in the work, not to list them on the board. Being reflective means a journal entry written the same evening about a dead end, not a paragraph composed later claiming growth. Being an inquirer means a line of inquiry that changed because the evidence did not support it. A tutor who sees the journal every week can point at the real instances, which is also what makes the child's presentation answerable when a visiting parent asks an unscripted question.

The last block is the presentation and the display, and it is mostly editing. A home tutor for PYP transdisciplinary learning Mumbai parents bring in during the final fortnight is a rehearsal coach and a cutter of text: a board with four hundred words on it is a board nobody reads, and a child reading aloud from her own board has not understood it yet. Structure first, decoration last, and at least two full rehearsals in front of someone who is allowed to ask an awkward question.

sections.heading: Which parts of Mumbai an exhibition home tutor reaches, and when
paragraphs: Finding an IB PYP exhibition home tutor in Mumbai is a travel problem before it is an academic one. Mumbai, Maharashtra is a long thin city with roughly one usable road axis per corridor, so the honest answer to how far a tutor will come is set by the evening peak and not by the kilometre count. Parents search "IB tutors near me Mumbai" expecting proximity to settle it. Proximity along the line settles far more than proximity on the map does.

In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clocks are slow. Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Fort, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road and Worli sit within a few kilometres of each other, but the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals can absorb forty minutes of an evening, so tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. The Western Line into Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line to Dockyard, Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade towards BKC and the Coastal Road all help a tutor who lives in the right half of the island. In the Western Suburbs the geometry is north to south: Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar strung along the Western Line, the Western Express Highway and Link Road, with Metro Line 1 from Versova through Andheri to Ghatkopar, Metro Line 2A and Metro Line 7 running the Dahisar to Andheri stretch. Matching along the line, Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali, works. Matching across it does not.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Kurla, Ghatkopar and Vidyavihar on the rail and Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai is the exception worth planning for: it is physically central and has no station of its own, so a tutor arrives by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar and a monsoon evening on JVLR can double that trip. The Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) is the one crossing that makes a Western to Central match occasionally viable. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Wadala through Govandi, Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, on the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Monorail between Chembur and Wadala. The Eastern Freeway puts South Mumbai within reach of Chembur far faster than the map suggests, which is why a Wadala tutor can genuinely hold a Colaba slot.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so match node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, served by the Harbour Line, the Trans-Harbour Line to Thane and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 from Belapur to Pendhar. The Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link does the same on the western side, but pulling a tutor across either twice a week for one weekday lesson rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Vartak Nagar and up Ghodbunder Road, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes from the station off-peak and close to an hour in the evening. Thane tutors cover Thane; Mulund tutors sometimes cross over.

sections.heading: When does exhibition work peak in the Mumbai school year?
paragraphs: Exhibition work peaks in the final weeks before the public presentation, which most Mumbai IB schools schedule towards the close of their academic year. Two calendars are in use in the city: an April to March year and an August to June year. Ask your PYP coordinator which term the exhibition falls in, because every other plan in the household has to bend around that date.

Working backwards from the presentation, the pressure points are predictable. The long break, whether that is Diwali or the Christmas and New Year weeks, swallows research time that parents assumed would be used, and children come back having forgotten what their own lines of inquiry were for. The monsoon from June onwards makes weekday evening travel unreliable across the whole city, which is when home slots start slipping and hybrid arrangements earn their keep. February and March are the worst weeks in households with an older child in the Diploma Programme (DP), because Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines and final examinations land then and the family's attention is already spoken for.

The school's own expectations shape the work more than the IB documentation does. Families at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School in Goregaon East work to one set of submission points, families at JBCN International School in Parel, Borivali or Chembur to another, and families at Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West or D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul to their own. Some schools expect the process journal to be submitted and read. Some run a mid-point conference with the mentor. Some set a hard cut-off for the action component. A tutor who asks for the school's brief in the first session is reading the right document.

There is a second Mumbai calendar nobody writes down: the school bus. A child who leaves a Thane society at 7am and gets home from Goregaon at 4.30pm is not available for serious thinking at 5pm, and is tired by 8pm. The workable window for the final PYP year in most Mumbai households is narrow, and it is the real constraint on which tutors can be matched to you. Weekend mornings are where the heavier sessions belong, which is also when the building's visitor rules and the roads are both easier.

sections.heading: Home, online or hybrid for PYP exhibition support in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the lead option, and for the exhibition it is not a preference but a practical fit. IB PYP exhibition home tutoring in Mumbai puts an adult in the room where the chart paper, the printouts, the model and the laptop all are, which is where the project physically lives. A ten-year-old can be redirected in that room by a glance. The same child on a video call at 7pm will drift within fifteen minutes, and the parent ends up operating the device, muting, unmuting and holding pages up to the camera instead of getting on with their own evening.

Home tuition has costs you should see clearly. The tutor's travel is part of what you pay for in time if not in money, so a home slot is less flexible: moving a Wednesday 6.30pm visit is not a two-minute change for someone who plans their evening around the Western Express Highway. Your pool of tutors is smaller, because it is limited to people who can reach your building reliably. And heavy rain, a waterlogged junction or a political closure will occasionally cost you a session that an online slot would have survived.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai is the right call in three situations: the specialist you want is on the far side of the creek or the Atal Setu, the monsoon has made a weekday evening trip unreliable for a fortnight, or you want a short mid-week check-in between home visits rather than a second full session. Online is genuinely good for interrogating a central idea, reading a journal entry together, checking a research plan and tightening a slide. It is weak for the physical half of the work and almost useless for rehearsing in front of an audience.

Hybrid is where most Mumbai families settle, and it is worth setting up deliberately rather than drifting into. One home visit a week carries the main work and the materials. One short online check-in, placed the evening before the mentor meeting, keeps the thinking continuous and catches the week's drift before the school does. In the last fortnight the balance usually flips the other way: two home visits for rehearsal and board editing, because a presentation cannot be practised properly through a screen.

sections.heading: How is an IB PYP exhibition home tutor in Mumbai checked before they reach your door?
paragraphs: Every IB PYP exhibition home tutor in Mumbai on the platform is checked on four things before a profile is shown to a parent: government photo identity, the qualification claimed, actual teaching experience with the final primary year rather than with secondary classes, and contactable references from families or schools they have worked with. A short conversation about practice sits on top of that, because a transcript does not tell you whether someone can let a child be wrong for a week.

The questions we ask in that conversation are the ones you should ask too. Describe an inquiry you scaffolded without producing any of it. What would you do if a child's central idea turned out to be unworkable in week five? How do you handle a parent who wants you to tidy up the display board? What is your reading of the school's process journal expectation? A tutor who answers those with specifics has done this. A tutor who answers with reassurance has not.

There is a short list of things to check yourself, on the doorstep and after. Ask for photo identity at the first visit and expect the tutor to sign your society's visitor register without complaint. Keep sessions in a shared room rather than a bedroom, with an adult in the flat. Ask the tutor to leave a short written note after each visit saying what moved and what the child should do next, and compare that over a month. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents have found informally may be excellent, but without any of those habits you have no way of telling early.

One signal matters more than the rest at this age. A tutor who promises a specific result at the exhibition is telling you they intend to do the work themselves, which the school will notice and which teaches the child the opposite of what the exhibition is for. A tutor who says the first two weeks will look slow, because the central idea has to be rewritten before anything else can start, is describing the actual job. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here, and the tutors are matched to the family rather than placed by a school.

sections.heading: What a tutor at your dining table can do that a screen cannot
paragraphs: The exhibition is a project with objects in it, and that is the whole argument for an IB PYP exhibition home tutor in Mumbai rather than a video call. Printed sources get sorted on the floor into piles that become the lines of inquiry. Sticky notes get moved around until a sequence appears. The model built for the action component sits half finished on the table and gets criticised in person, which is not the same as being described over a camera. A tutor can pick up the board, hold it at arm's length and say the title is the only thing a visitor will read.

Rehearsal is the second thing that only works in the room. A child presenting to a laptop is performing to nobody. A child presenting in her own living room to a grandparent, a younger sibling and the family's helper has an audience that fidgets, looks away and asks a question she did not expect, which is exactly what the exhibition day will feel like. The tutor's job during that rehearsal is to sit at the back and write down the three moments the child lost the room, then work on those rather than on the slides.

The third thing a home visit gives you is diagnosis you cannot get any other way. A tutor who walks in sees the child working on a bed with a television on in the next room, or two siblings sharing one desk and one plug point, or a folder of printouts nobody has sorted since October. Those are the real causes of a stalled exhibition far more often than ability is, and none of them are visible on a call. The fix is usually physical: a cleared table for the duration, a box for the project so it stops migrating, a wall for the plan.

The handover is the fourth thing, and parents underrate it. The useful five minutes of a home session happen standing in the kitchen afterwards, when the tutor says the central idea was rewritten today and the child needs to find one person to interview before Thursday. That conversation does not happen when a call ends, because the call just ends. Set against all of this is the honest cost: an hour or more of the tutor's evening goes on the Eastern Express Highway or Ghodbunder Road to be in your flat, which narrows your options and makes the slot harder to move. For the final PYP year, with a child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, most Mumbai families decide that trade is worth making.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks of home tuition?
paragraphs: After four weekly sessions a child should be able to state her central idea in one sentence without being prompted, name her lines of inquiry and explain what each one is for, and talk about two or three sources in her own words including where they came from. The process journal should have entries the child made herself, including at least one about something that did not work. That is the four-week test, and it is deliberately about the child's talk rather than about pages produced.

By the end of a term the markers are different. A line of inquiry has been revised at least once because the evidence did not support it, which is a good sign and not a setback. The action has actually happened rather than being planned. A draft display exists and has already been cut down once. The child has rehearsed the talk end to end in front of a person. The mentor's feedback has been read and acted on rather than filed. If all of that is true, the last fortnight is editing and rehearsal instead of panic.

The honest limits are worth stating before you book anything. A home tutor cannot change the school mentor's view of the work, and should not try. A tutor cannot make a child care about a topic she was pushed into choosing, which is why the central idea is worth fighting over in week one. A tutor cannot repair in three weeks a project that drifted for three months, although two sessions a week in that fortnight will usually produce something the child can stand behind. And IB Gram does not guarantee grades or outcomes, because the work is the child's and the assessment belongs to the school.

When nothing has moved after a month, the cause is usually one of three things and only one of them is the tutor. A central idea the child never owned will stall whoever is sitting next to her. A session slot too late in the evening, after a long bus ride home from Juhu or Goregaon, will produce an hour of compliance and no thinking. A tutor teaching subject content instead of inquiry skills will leave the child better informed and no closer to an exhibition. Say which one it looks like and we will change the slot, the approach or the tutor accordingly.

sections.heading: Getting started: what to prepare before the first home session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have five things ready and the first session will be worth paying for. The school's written exhibition brief with its dates. The process journal in whatever state it is in, untidied. The central idea exactly as the child has written it, not as you would write it. The mentor's last piece of feedback. And the child's own list of what she still wants to find out, written by her, however short. A tutor who reads those five things in the first thirty minutes can tell you what the real problem is.

Prepare the room as well as the paperwork. A cleared table with a plug point and a chair on the other side of it, out of the line of sight of a television, with the project materials in one box rather than spread across three rooms. Tell us your building's visitor process when you send the query, because a tower that will not admit visitors after 8pm or requires the resident to approve entry on an app changes which tutors can realistically hold your slot. Register the tutor as a recurring visitor before the first evening rather than at the gate.

The first session itself follows a fixed shape. The tutor reads the brief and the journal while the child is in the room. The child explains her inquiry out loud and the tutor asks questions rather than correcting. Together they test whether the central idea is conceptual, and whether the lines of inquiry do different work. Then the tutor writes a plan for the next fortnight: what the child does, what you do not do, and what the tutor will bring next week. You get that plan in writing, and the kitchen handover at the end tells you the one thing to watch for.

IB PYP exhibition home tuition in Mumbai works best as a standing weekly slot booked from the term the exhibition starts, not as emergency cover in the last three weeks. Start when the brief comes home. The tutors who understand the final PYP year are the same ones Mumbai families book early, and their evening slots fill first in exactly the term you need them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Kharghar or Thane for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already lives in that node. A tutor based in Nerul or Belapur reaches Kharghar along Palm Beach Road comfortably for a 6.30pm start, and a tutor near Thane station reaches Majiwada quickly but Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road much less quickly in the evening peak. What does not hold for a full term is a tutor crossing the creek or the Atal Setu twice a week for one lesson. If the specialist you want is on the far side of the city, take one home visit at the weekend and a short online check-in midweek instead of forcing a commute that will quietly collapse by week three.

faqs.question: What does the society gate and visitor process look like for a weekly home tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor as a recurring visitor before the first session rather than at the gate on the evening itself. Most Mumbai societies will take a name, a phone number, an identity type and a standing day and time from the flat owner, and some ask for the tutor's photograph for the visitor app. Tell us your building's rule when you send the query, because a tower that refuses entry after 8pm or requires the resident to approve every entry changes which slot is workable. Tutors carry photo identity and expect to sign the register every week without being asked twice.

faqs.question: How are IB tuition fees in Mumbai worked out for exhibition support at home?
faqs.answer: Fees are set by the tutor and depend on five things: the board and level, how scarce the specialism is, the session length, how far the tutor travels to your home, and how many sessions a week you book. IB home tuition in Mumbai for the final PYP year usually sits below Diploma Programme work because the content load is lighter, but exhibition support in the fortnight before a presentation is scarce and priced accordingly. We will not quote a figure on this page, and a tutor who quotes before seeing the child's journal and the school's brief is guessing at the work involved.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor even allowed to help with the PYP exhibition?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary the school sets: the exhibition is student-led, so a tutor may teach skills and ask questions but may not produce content. A tutor can show your child how to test whether a line of inquiry is conceptual, how to record a source as she finds it, how to plan an interview and how to rehearse a presentation. A tutor does not write the central idea, does not type the process journal and does not lay out the display board. The test is simple: if the school asks who helped and with what, the answer should be comfortable to give in full.

faqs.question: The school has assigned an exhibition mentor already. Why add a home tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the two jobs are different. The school mentor steers the inquiry and signs off the work during school hours, usually across several children at once. An IB PYP exhibition home tutor in Mumbai works with one child in the room where the project physically lives, at the hour when she is tired and the deadline still feels abstract. The tutor does not replace or second-guess the mentor. The first session should open with the mentor's last written feedback, and everything done between sessions should aim at what the mentor actually asked for rather than at a parallel plan.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for exhibition support, or does the tutor need to be in the building?
faqs.answer: Online works for talk and fails for things. A video call is good for interrogating a central idea, reading a journal entry together, checking a research plan and tightening a slide. It is poor for the physical half of the exhibition: sorting printed sources on the floor, building the model for the action, laying out a board, and rehearsing in front of an audience that actually fidgets. Most Mumbai families settle on a home visit as the main session with a short online check-in before the mentor meeting, which keeps the thinking continuous without adding a second trip across the city.

faqs.question: We live in Bandra and the tutor we like lives in Mulund. Is that commute realistic for a term?
faqs.answer: Usually not for a weekday evening slot. Bandra to Mulund means the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road or the Eastern Express Highway at the worst hour, and the tutor will spend longer travelling than teaching, which ends in cancellations. Two things do work: a weekend home session when the roads are calmer, or a tutor matched along your own corridor with the Mulund specialist kept for online check-ins. We would rather tell you a match is geographically unrealistic than book it, because a cancelled session three weeks before the presentation costs more than a slightly different tutor would have.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be at home, but not in the room. Most Mumbai families have a parent, a grandparent or a helper present, which is right for a child of this age and sensible for the tutor as well. Sitting in on the whole session changes the child's behaviour: she starts performing for you instead of thinking aloud, and she stops saying the thing she is unsure about. Ask the tutor for a few minutes at the end to tell you what moved and what the child should do before the next visit, and leave the middle of the session alone.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor while keeping your slot. A mismatch at this age is rarely about subject knowledge; it is pace, patience, or an adult talking over a ten-year-old. We ask for specifics rather than a rating: what the child said afterwards, whether the tutor arrived on time, whether the work set between sessions was clear enough for her to start alone. The replacement begins with the previous tutor's notes and the child's journal, so you are not paying for the same diagnostic twice, and you are not locked into a package.

faqs.question: What if there is no visible progress after a month of home classes?
faqs.answer: Say so directly and expect a specific answer rather than reassurance. After four weekly sessions a child should state her central idea in one sentence unprompted, name her lines of inquiry and explain two or three sources in her own words. If none of that is true, the usual causes are a central idea she never owned, a slot too late in the evening after a long bus ride, or a tutor teaching subject content instead of inquiry skills. Each has a different fix, and two of the three do not involve changing the tutor at all.

faqs.question: Can you promise a better outcome at the exhibition?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not guarantee grades or outcomes, and anyone who has watched a PYP exhibition would not promise one, because the work belongs to the child and the assessment belongs to the school. What a good home tutor changes is the process: sources recorded as they are found, a journal written in the same week as the thinking, a rehearsal that happens more than once, and a child who can answer an unscripted question on the day. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed result for a primary project, because it signals they plan to do the work themselves.

faqs.question: When in the Mumbai school year should we start looking for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Start when the school hands out the exhibition brief, not when the presentation is three weeks away. The tutors who understand the final PYP year are the same ones booked by families at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School in Goregaon East, and their weekday evening slots fill first in exactly the term the exhibition falls in. Starting early also buys the slow work that matters most: choosing a central idea the child genuinely cares about, and letting one line of inquiry fail before it is rewritten.
