sections.heading: How does IB Gram find an IB PYP exhibition tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: You send one message with four things: which school your child attends, which year group she is in, roughly when the exhibition launches, and where in Mumbai you live. IB Gram reads that against the tutors already teaching in your part of the city and comes back with two or three names, each with real Primary Years Programme experience rather than a general primary-school background.

The filter that matters most is not a degree. It is whether the tutor has sat with a child through a full inquiry cycle and knows what a mentor teacher at an International Baccalaureate (IB) school will push back on. A graduate who taught Grade 5 Maths in a state-board school can drill arithmetic beautifully and still have no idea what a line of inquiry is, or why writing the child's central idea for her defeats the point of the exercise. So we ask candidates to describe an exhibition they supported, what the child's first topic was, and how it changed between November and March. The answer tells us more than any certificate does.

Geography is the second filter. An IB PYP exhibition tutor in Mumbai who lives in Mulund will take the booking in Powai and quietly resent it by the fourth week, because JVLR at seven in the evening is not a twenty-minute drive. We shortlist inside the travel corridor first and widen it only if your area genuinely has nobody with exhibition experience. If you are in Kharghar or Panvel, we look at Navi Mumbai tutors before we look at anyone on the island.

The last filter is the child herself. A ten-year-old who freezes when she has to present needs a different tutor from one whose problem is that she has six topics and no decision. We ask what the school mentor has already written, because that line in a diary or on a parent portal is usually the most accurate description of the problem you will get anywhere. Then you talk to the shortlist yourself before anything is confirmed and before any money moves.
bullets: 1. Send your school, year group, area and exhibition launch date.
2. We shortlist two or three tutors who have run exhibition cycles.
3. You speak to each tutor yourself before confirming anything.
4. First session runs at your home, or online if travel is unrealistic.
5. After two sessions you continue, switch tutor or stop.

sections.heading: Where the exhibition sits in the IB Primary Years Programme
paragraphs: The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is the International Baccalaureate (IB) curriculum framework for children aged roughly three to twelve, which in Mumbai schools maps onto nursery through Grade 5. It is organised around six transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subjects: Who we are, Where we are in place and time, How we express ourselves, How the world works, How we organise ourselves, and Sharing the planet. Each theme becomes a unit of inquiry the class works through for several weeks at a time.

The exhibition is the last of those units and the only one the child largely drives herself. It is the Year 6 exhibition in IB language, meaning the final PYP year, which is Grade 5 at most Mumbai schools. Instead of a teacher setting the central idea, the student picks a theme, builds her own central idea, writes her own lines of inquiry, researches, takes action and then presents to parents, staff and often to younger classes. The programme is designed so this is the point where she shows she can run an inquiry without being carried through it.

Two structural facts should change how you think about tutoring here. First, the exhibition is school-assessed and internal. There is no external IB paper, no mark sheet arriving from abroad, no number that follows the child into the Middle Years Programme (MYP). Second, it is the bridge into MYP, where the same habits reappear as service as action and, years later, as the personal project and eventually the Extended Essay (EE) in the Diploma Programme (DP). A child who learns to narrow a question and keep a research log in Grade 5 walks into MYP Year 1 with an advantage that is real and entirely unmeasured.

That is why a PYP transdisciplinary learning tutor in Mumbai is doing something different from a DP subject tutor. There is no syllabus to finish and no past paper to work through. The work is process: research skills, thinking skills, communication, self-management and the social skills a group project exposes within a fortnight. The learner profile attributes the school keeps on its corridor walls, inquirer, thinker, communicator, reflective, principled, risk-taker, are the actual assessment vocabulary your child's mentor will use when she writes feedback.
bullets: Six transdisciplinary themes replace separate subjects across the PYP years
The exhibition is the final PYP unit, student-driven rather than teacher-set
Assessed internally by the school, with no external IB mark
Key concepts: form, function, causation, change, connection, perspective, responsibility
Feeds directly into MYP habits of research, reflection and action

sections.heading: What does the PYP exhibition actually ask a ten-year-old to do?
paragraphs: It asks her to choose one of the six transdisciplinary themes, turn a personal interest into a single central idea worth investigating, write three or four lines of inquiry under it, gather her own evidence, take some form of action, present the whole thing publicly and then reflect honestly on what went wrong. Six jobs, one term, ten years old.

Take a child at a Chembur school who picks Sharing the planet because she is annoyed that the wet and dry waste bins in her building end up in the same truck. Her first attempt at a central idea is that waste is a big problem in Mumbai, which is a topic rather than a central idea, and her mentor will send it back. A tutor's job that week is to ask what exactly she thinks is broken. Three sessions later the central idea is closer to the proposition that systems only work when the people inside them understand why they exist, and now the lines of inquiry write themselves: how the building's waste system is supposed to work, who decides what happens to it after collection, and what actually changes behaviour on the fourteenth floor.

Primary research is where Mumbai children either shine or copy. The internet will hand her a national statistic about landfill; the housekeeping supervisor in her own building will tell her which floors mix their bins and why the collector refuses certain bags. A tutor who knows the exhibition pushes her towards the second kind of source: a scripted interview with the society secretary, a short survey of the families on her own floor, a photograph log kept over a fortnight, a visit to the sorting point with a parent. She learns to record where each claim came from, which is the habit the process journal exists to build in the first place.

The presentation is not a slide-deck competition, although it usually turns into one by February. Schools vary in what they ask for, so the structure, the length, the group size and the assessment language all come from your child's PYP coordinator and the current programme documentation, not from a tutor's memory of another school in another year. A good tutor asks for the school's own exhibition handbook in the first session and works to that document. What stays constant is the reflection: she has to be able to say what her thinking was in November and how it is different in March, in her own words, when an adult she has never met asks her a question in front of her parents.
bullets: Central idea first, lines of inquiry second, never the reverse
Primary research: interviews, surveys, site visits, photograph logs
A process journal recording where every single claim came from
An action step the child can actually carry out herself
A public presentation she can answer unscripted questions about
Written reflection comparing early thinking with her final position

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai we place PYP exhibition tutors
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is one city on a map and six separate scheduling problems in practice. An IB PYP exhibition tutor in Mumbai is matched to a corridor rather than to the whole metropolitan area, because a weekly slot that requires crossing the city at six in the evening collapses by the third week of the term. Home tuition in Mumbai is a timetabling problem before it is a teaching one, and pretending otherwise is how a term of exhibition support turns into four sessions and an apology.

In South Mumbai we place tutors within the island: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Breach Candy, Peddar Road, Tardeo, Worli and Lower Parel. Distances are tiny and the clock still beats you, because the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at half past six undo eight kilometres. The Western Line from Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line out of CSMT and Metro Line 3 towards BKC carry the tutors who do not drive, and the Coastal Road has changed what a Worli to Nariman Point run costs in minutes. In the Western Suburbs, which run from Bandra up through Khar, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Versova, Oshiwara, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar, we match along the line rather than across it. Khar to Santacruz is nothing. Juhu to Kandivali at seven on a Wednesday is an hour you will pay for in cancelled sessions. Metro Lines 2A and 7 between Dahisar and Gundavali, and Metro Line 1 from Versova through Andheri to Ghatkopar, have made some north-south pairings workable that the Western Express Highway never did.

The Central Suburbs hang off the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali sitting on JVLR between them. Powai has no station of its own, so a home tutor arrives by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) is the reason a Chembur tutor can take a Powai booking at all. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund, served by the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway makes Wadala and Chembur closer to Fort than the map suggests. A Vikhroli family and a Mulund family look adjacent on paper and belong to different matching pools in the evening peak.

Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road, the Sion-Panvel Highway and the Navi Mumbai Metro between Belapur and Pendhar. The Atal Setu has pulled Panvel much closer to South Mumbai for a weekend session, though we still match a Kharghar family with a Navi Mumbai tutor for a standing weekday slot. Thane spreads from the station eastward along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: twenty minutes off-peak, close to an hour at half past six. Thane tutors cover Thane, and a Mulund tutor crosses over only when the slot is early. The Trans-Harbour Line between Thane and Vashi is the one cross-creek route that reliably holds up.
bullets: South Mumbai matched inside the island, Colaba through to Worli
Western Suburbs matched along the line, Bandra to Dahisar
Powai and Chandivali reached by road via JVLR, not rail
Navi Mumbai matched node to node along Palm Beach Road
Thane scheduling set by Ghodbunder Road rather than distance

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar sets the exhibition timeline
paragraphs: Most IB schools in Mumbai run an August to May or June year, and a few follow an April to March calendar instead, so the first question about exhibition timing is which of the two your school uses. On an August start, the exhibition is usually introduced after the Diwali break, developed across December and January, and presented somewhere between February and April. On an April start it lands earlier in the cycle. Neither pattern is universal and schools move the presentation evening, so take your dates from the PYP coordinator rather than from this page.

Families we work with send children to Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School at Goregaon East off the JVLR, both of which run the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma Programme, and to the IB and Cambridge International Education schools spread across the city: the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Singapore International School at Dahisar East, NES International School in Mulund West, Podar International School at Santacruz and Powai, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, D.Y. Patil International School at Nerul and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane. Naming a school here is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page, and we do not guarantee grades.

The pressure points are predictable enough to plan a home tuition slot around. The fortnight after Diwali is when topics are chosen, and when a child who has not thought about it arrives at school with nothing while her friends arrive with three ideas. Late December is lost to the winter break, which is also the only long stretch where primary research is genuinely easy, because the building's staff, her grandparents and the neighbours are all available and school is not. January is the month groups fall apart. The three weeks before the presentation evening are when slide-making swallows the thinking, and that is the point where a tutor is most useful and most often hired far too late.

Two Mumbai-specific collisions are worth planning for. The monsoon from June to September kills outdoor primary research and makes evening travel unreliable, which matters on an April-start calendar where the exhibition term falls inside it. And in February and March the older siblings in the house are sitting Cambridge IGCSE and Diploma Programme examinations, so the dining table, the quiet room and the parents' attention are all contested at once. Families with a Grade 5 child and a DP2 child in the same flat should fix the exhibition slot before the exam timetable is published, not after it, because the second negotiation is much harder than the first.
bullets: Confirm whether your school runs an August or April academic year
Topic choice lands in the fortnight after the Diwali break
Winter break is the easiest window for interviews and surveys
Presentation evening usually falls between February and April
Older siblings' IGCSE and DP exams compete for the quiet room

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for exhibition support in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default for exhibition work, and that is practical rather than a preference. The child's evidence lives at home: the process journal, the printed survey sheets, the labelled photographs, the half-built model, the laptop with the slides on it. An IB PYP exhibition home tuition slot in Mumbai lets the tutor pick up the journal, read the last three entries and see what actually happened since the previous visit instead of being told what happened. Primary research is also local. If the inquiry concerns her own building's waste, water, security staff or lift usage, the research site is the address the tutor is already standing in.

Online works better than most parents expect for the thinking parts and worse for everything else. Narrowing a central idea, pressure-testing lines of inquiry, rehearsing the questions a visiting adult will ask, tightening a reflection: all of that is conversation, and a shared screen handles it. An IB online tutor in Mumbai also solves the scarcity problem. If you are in Panvel or Kasarvadavali and nobody within forty minutes has run an exhibition cycle, a tutor in Bandra over video is a better answer than a nearby tutor who has never seen one. What online does badly is a restless ten-year-old. Attention on a screen at the end of a school day is short, and a child who is avoiding the work finds it far easier to avoid online.

Hybrid is what most families end up with by February without having planned it. The weekly session is at home, and a second short online call lands midweek when a draft needs a look or the group has had a fight. We set this up deliberately: one home visit a little over an hour long, one twenty-minute online check-in, and a rule that the check-in is cancelled rather than stretched when there is nothing to show. Most PYP transdisciplinary learning home classes Mumbai parents book settle into this shape, because the work is episodic. Some weeks there is a great deal to do, and some weeks the child is waiting on a reply from somebody she interviewed.

The honest trade-offs are worth stating plainly. IB home tuition in Mumbai costs more than online because travel time is real, it is the first thing to break when the monsoon or an evening on the Western Express Highway interferes, and it is harder to reschedule at short notice. Online is cheaper, more reliable and less effective during the model-building, poster and material-handling weeks. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents hire for home visits should live within a corridor of you. Hiring someone who crosses the Thane creek or the Bandra-Worli Sea Link twice a week for a seven o'clock slot is a booking that quietly becomes an online booking by week five, and it is better to decide that honestly in October than in January.
bullets: Home visits let the tutor read the process journal, not hear about it
Online suits central idea work, rehearsal and reflection drafting
Hybrid: one home session weekly, one short midweek online check
Model-building and poster weeks need somebody in the room
Match within your corridor or the home slot becomes an online slot

sections.heading: How is an IB PYP exhibition home tutor checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram is checked on four things before a profile reaches a parent: government photo identity, the qualifications claimed, verifiable PYP or primary teaching experience, and at least one reference from a family or school that has used them. Unverified profiles are not shortlisted for anybody.

Experience verification is where exhibition requests fail quietly. Plenty of good tutors have taught primary Maths or English in Mumbai for years and have never been inside an exhibition cycle. So for this request we ask specifically: which school, which year, what the child's theme was, what the first draft central idea looked like and how the mentor reacted to it. Anyone who has done the work answers in concrete detail and usually complains about something along the way. Anyone who has not talks in general terms about inquiry-based learning and child-centred pedagogy. We route the second group to other work. An IB PYP exhibition tutor in Mumbai who cannot describe one real cycle should not be taking the booking at all.

Three checks are yours and no platform can do them for you. First, watch the first session: does the tutor ask your child questions, or supply the answers? The exhibition is assessed on her thinking, so the tutor who is fast and helpful is the dangerous one. Second, ask directly how much of the final work the tutor expects to touch, and listen for a clear line rather than a reassuring blur. Third, be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed outcome or promises the school will be impressed, because the exhibition carries no external mark to promise and a mentor's judgement is not for sale.

Practical verification matters too, particularly for home visits. Ask for the tutor's identity document the first time they come, give your society gate a name and a standing weekly slot so entry is registered once rather than renegotiated every week, and keep sessions in a room an adult passes through. An IB home tutor in Mumbai working with a ten-year-old should expect all three of those and should not be offended by any of them. If a tutor resents the gate register or wants the door closed, you have learned what you needed to know in week one rather than week six.
bullets: Photo identity and claimed qualifications checked before shortlisting
Exhibition experience probed with specifics, not phrases about inquiry
At least one reference from a family or school that used them
You watch session one for whether the tutor asks or tells
Standing gate entry and an open door on every home visit

sections.heading: The central idea problem: why most exhibitions stall in week two
paragraphs: Almost every exhibition that goes badly goes badly in the same place. The child picks a topic she likes, the topic is enormous, and nobody converts it into a central idea with an argument inside it. Plastic, space, animal cruelty and mental health are the four that arrive every single year. A topic answers the question of what this is about. A central idea has to say something that can be examined, supported and disagreed with by a reasonable adult.

The conversion is a conversation rather than a template, and it takes two or three sessions. The useful question is not what she wants to do but what she has noticed that annoys her. A child who says plastic usually means something far more specific: that the vendor outside her gate double-bags everything, or that her school canteen switched to paper straws and the bin still has plastic ones in it. From there, a central idea along the lines of people changing habits when the alternative is easier rather than when they are told is testable in her own building, in one term, by a ten-year-old. The test we use is simple: can you write three lines of inquiry under it that need three different kinds of evidence? If all three would be answered by the same search, the central idea is still a topic wearing a sentence.

Two traps follow. The first is secondary research swamping primary research. A child with a laptop can produce forty slides of statistics about the Pacific garbage patch and learn nothing, while the exhibition criteria reward evidence she gathered herself. IB PYP exhibition tutoring in Mumbai is largely the job of converting screen time into an interview script, a survey, a tally sheet or a photograph log. The second trap is the group. Most Mumbai schools run the exhibition in small teams, and teams fail along predictable lines: one child does everything, one does nothing, two want different central ideas and neither will move. A tutor cannot fix another family's child, but she can help yours write down her own contribution each week so the mentor sees evidence, and rehearse raising the problem with the mentor instead of at the dinner table.

The action component is where parents over-help most. A donation drive organised by the mother is not action. Action is whatever the child can do herself and report on: a bin label she designed and put up, a short talk to a Grade 2 class, a request she made to the society committee, a changed habit she tracked in her own flat for three weeks. It can be small and it must be hers. The same line applies to the presentation and the written work. Schools treat parent-authored exhibitions as an academic honesty problem, and mentors spot them immediately, usually because the child cannot answer a question about her own slide. A tutor who understands this spends the final fortnight making the child explain her work out loud to a stranger, which is the only preparation that survives the actual evening.
bullets: A topic is not a central idea: it needs a claim that can be tested
Test it: three lines of inquiry needing three different kinds of evidence
Convert screen research into interviews, surveys and tally sheets
Groups fail predictably, so record your child's own weekly contribution
Action must be small, hers, and reportable in her own words
Rehearse by making her explain the work to an unfamiliar adult

sections.heading: What should progress look like across the exhibition term?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see a narrowed central idea, three or four written lines of inquiry and a process journal with entries the child wrote herself. That is the whole four-week target and it is enough. If the central idea is still a broad topic after four weeks of home classes, something is wrong with the match or the child is avoiding the work.

By mid-term the shape of it should be visible: evidence she gathered rather than downloaded, a clear record of where each piece came from, an action step chosen and started, and a draft presentation that is an argument rather than a tour of facts. The change you should notice at home is smaller and more telling than any of that. She starts referring to her central idea unprompted when something related comes up at dinner, and she starts complaining that a source is unreliable. Those two behaviours are the real evidence that the inquiry has become hers rather than the tutor's.

Across a full cycle, the gain that lasts is not the exhibition itself, which nobody outside the school will ever ask her about again. It is that she can narrow a question, keep a log, interview an adult without her mother in the room, and stand in front of people and answer something she was not expecting. Those are the skills MYP starts charging for in Year 1. The honest limits are worth saying out loud: the exhibition carries no external mark, a tutor cannot change a mentor's judgement, and we do not guarantee grades or outcomes at any stage of the programme. A child who will not do the work will not be rescued by an hour a week, and six sessions in February cannot replace a term of thinking.

When it is not working, say so in week two rather than week eight. The usual causes are a tutor who answers instead of asking, so the child is being carried; a timing clash where the slot lands after a long school day and sports practice; or a mismatch of temperament with a child who needs more patience than this particular tutor has. Tell us which of the three it looks like and we move the slot or move the tutor. Replacing a tutor mid-term is normal in exhibition work, and the second match is usually better, because by then everybody involved knows what the actual problem was.
bullets: Four weeks: narrowed central idea, written lines of inquiry, journal started
Mid-term: primary evidence gathered, sources logged, action step underway
Signs it is working: she argues with her own sources unprompted
No external mark exists, so no tutor can promise an outcome
Raise a mismatch in week two; a mid-term replacement is routine

sections.heading: Booking home classes for the PYP exhibition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Getting started takes one message and about ten minutes of preparation on your side. Have four things ready: the school's exhibition handbook or the letter the coordinator sent home, your child's process journal even if it runs to three lines, the theme she is currently leaning towards, and the two evenings a week that genuinely work once school, sports and traffic are accounted for. The fourth is the one families get wrong, and it is the one that decides whether the booking lasts a term.

The first session is diagnostic and should not feel like tuition. The tutor reads the handbook, asks your child to explain her topic without interrupting her, asks three or four questions she cannot answer yet, and from that works out whether the problem is scope, research, confidence or motivation. By the end of it you should have a written plan for the term: what gets done before the winter break, what the primary research will consist of, and roughly when rehearsals start. A home tutor for PYP transdisciplinary learning Mumbai parents book in November has time to do this properly. One booked in February is doing damage control and will say so.

Ask the tutor two questions at the end of session one. What is the single biggest risk to this exhibition, and what will you not do for her? The answers tell you whether you have hired a thinking partner or a slide-maker. What you want is a PYP transdisciplinary learning IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor Mumbai families keep for the whole term, not somebody who appears for a fortnight. Parents mostly arrive here after typing IB tutors near me Mumbai into a phone at nine at night, which returns agencies before it returns people, and the difference shows up in exactly that answer.

IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and level, how scarce the specialism is, how far the tutor travels to reach you, how long each session runs and whether you book weekly or twice weekly. Exhibition support sits at the specialist end, because the pool of tutors who have genuinely run a cycle with a child is small, and home visits in a corridor with bad evening traffic cost more than online sessions do. We will not print a figure on a page, because an honest number depends on all five of those variables. Ask on the first call and you will get a range for your own area rather than a national average.
bullets: Have the school's exhibition handbook ready for session one
Bring the process journal, however thin it currently is
Pick two evenings that survive school, sports and traffic
Session one is diagnostic: scope, research, confidence or motivation
Leave session one with a written term plan and a rehearsal date

faqs.question: What does an IB PYP exhibition tutor do that the school mentor does not?
faqs.answer: The mentor assesses; the tutor rehearses. Your child's mentor teacher at school guides a group of students, gives feedback at set checkpoints and ultimately judges the work, which means there is a limit to how much time any one child gets and a good reason the mentor will not simply hand over a better central idea. A tutor works with one child, weekly, on the parts the mentor flagged: narrowing the idea, building an interview script, restarting a journal that has gone silent, rehearsing answers. The tutor never writes the work. The school decides what good looks like, and the tutor helps your child get there.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Lower Parel for a weekday evening session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in South Mumbai it is usually straightforward because we match inside the island rather than bringing somebody down from the suburbs. A Lower Parel or Worli address is reachable from Parel, Dadar, Prabhadevi and Mahalaxmi without crossing a signal that eats half an hour, which is what makes a 6.30 or 7pm slot hold for a full term. Give your society gate the tutor's name and a standing weekly time so entry is registered once rather than negotiated every week. If your building insists on a fresh visitor pass per entry, tell us before matching, because some tutors will not accept a booking with a twenty-minute gate queue attached.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the exhibition should we start home tuition?
faqs.answer: Start when the school announces the exhibition, which for most Mumbai schools on an August calendar means the fortnight after Diwali. That gives roughly a term, which is what the work actually needs: two or three sessions to narrow the central idea, several weeks of primary research, an action step that has to happen in real life, then rehearsal. Families who call three weeks before the presentation evening get help with slides and delivery, which is the least valuable part of the whole exercise. If you are already late, say so, and we will prioritise the reflection and the question-handling, because those are what the mentor probes on the night.

faqs.question: Is the PYP exhibition graded, and does it affect her MYP place?
faqs.answer: No, there is no external International Baccalaureate mark for the exhibition, and it is assessed internally by your school. Most Mumbai schools report it descriptively, against the learner profile and the approaches to learning skills, rather than as a score, and it does not travel with her as a number into the Middle Years Programme. Because no external mark exists, no tutor can promise an outcome, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What the exhibition does affect is her report comments, her own confidence about standing up and presenting, and how ready she is for the research expectations that begin in MYP Year 1.

faqs.question: Her exhibition group is doing nothing and she is doing everything. Can a tutor help?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer is that a tutor fixes your child's position in the group rather than the group itself. Most Mumbai schools run the exhibition in small teams, and uneven effort is the most common complaint we hear in January. What a tutor can do is help her write a weekly record of what she personally researched, drafted and presented, so the mentor has evidence instead of a disputed account. The tutor can also rehearse the conversation she needs to have with her mentor, which most ten-year-olds will not start unprompted. What no tutor can do is make another family's child work.

faqs.question: Does online exhibition support work as well as a tutor at home?
faqs.answer: For the thinking it is nearly as good; for the making it is not. Narrowing the central idea, pressure-testing lines of inquiry, drafting the reflection and rehearsing unexpected questions are conversations, and a shared screen handles them well. Reading a process journal, sorting printed survey sheets, checking a model, fixing a poster and holding a distracted ten-year-old's attention at the end of a school day all go better with somebody in the room. If you are in Kharghar, Panvel or Kasarvadavali and no experienced exhibition tutor is within reach, online with the right tutor beats weekly home visits from the wrong one.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for exhibition support?
faqs.answer: Five things: the board and level, how scarce the specialism is, how far the tutor travels to you, the session length, and whether you book weekly or twice weekly. Exhibition work sits at the scarce end, because relatively few tutors in Mumbai have run a full cycle with a child, so it prices closer to Diploma Programme subject support than to general primary tuition. Home visits carry travel, which is why a Juhu to Kandivali booking costs more than a Khar to Santacruz one. Online is cheaper. We do not publish a price list, because any figure that ignored your area would mislead you.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar. Is a weekly evening slot realistic for us?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided we match you inside Navi Mumbai rather than across the creek. Kharghar is a short run from Belapur, Nerul, Seawoods and Panvel on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, so a 6.30pm slot with a Navi Mumbai tutor holds through a term. The Atal Setu has made a weekend session with a South Mumbai tutor genuinely possible, but a weekday evening booking that depends on crossing it will not survive the monsoon. If nobody in the nodes has exhibition experience, we will tell you that plainly and recommend online with a tutor who does.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace the tutor, with no argument and no requirement to justify it at length. In practice there are three causes, and knowing which one applies makes the second match better: the tutor answers instead of asking, so your child is being carried; the slot is wrong, landing after a long school day when nothing registers; or the temperaments simply do not fit. Say which it looks like. We shortlist again from the same corridor, and the replacement is briefed on what the first tutor got wrong. Mid-term changes are routine in exhibition work because the term is short.

faqs.question: Is it cheating if a tutor helps with the exhibition?
faqs.answer: It is cheating if the tutor produces the work, and it is not if the tutor teaches the child to produce it. Schools treat the exhibition as the child's own, and mentors identify parent-authored or tutor-authored projects easily, usually because the child cannot explain her own slide when asked a simple question. A legitimate tutor asks questions, teaches research method, corrects a journal habit, rehearses delivery and refuses to write the central idea. If your tutor is drafting her reflection or building her poster, stop the sessions. Ask any tutor in session one what they will not do for your child, and listen to how fast they answer.

faqs.question: What should we prepare at home before the first session?
faqs.answer: Four things: the school's exhibition handbook or coordinator's letter, the process journal in whatever state it is in, the theme she is leaning towards, and a quiet table that is not the family sofa. The table matters more than parents expect, because exhibition work means spreading out survey sheets, photographs and drafts for an hour. Decide in advance which parent is the point of contact, because exhibition tutoring generates more parent conversation than subject tuition does. If an older sibling is sitting Cambridge IGCSE or Diploma Programme exams in the same flat, say so, and we will pick a slot that does not collide with their study hours.

faqs.question: Four weeks in and nothing seems to have changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Check one specific thing before changing anything: has the central idea narrowed, and are there three or four written lines of inquiry under it? If yes, the progress is real even though it looks like nothing, because the visible output arrives later in the term. If the central idea is still the original broad topic after four weeks of IB PYP exhibition home classes in Mumbai, the match or the method is wrong, and that is the week to tell us. Also check who is talking during sessions. If the tutor explains and your child nods, change the tutor, because nodding does not develop her thinking.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: You tell us the grade, the school, your locality and the two evenings that are genuinely free. We shortlist tutors who already work in that part of Mumbai, who have taught children this age, and who are willing to run a short session rather than a long one. You speak to them before anything is booked, and the first visit happens with you in the next room.

Most of this starts with a search like IB tutors near me Mumbai parents run on a phone in the school pick-up queue. What we ask for first, though, is not a syllabus. It is a description of the evening. A parent in Chembur tells us her son is cheerful until about half past six and then cannot hold a pencil. A parent in Khar West says his daughter reads happily in bed and refuses anything that looks like homework. Those two children need completely different people in the room, and neither request is solved by matching on subject alone. So the intake question we care most about is this: what does the hour between the school bag landing and dinner actually look like in your house?

We also ask what you have already tried, because a great deal of what parents do at home works and gets abandoned too early. If you read aloud every night for a year and stopped once your child started reading independently, that is worth knowing. If you bought a workbook and it caused three weeks of arguments, that is worth knowing too, and a sensible tutor will not open by handing out more of the same. The shortlist we send is deliberately small. Three names you will actually ring beats twelve profiles you will never open. Most families who ask us for an IB home tutor in Mumbai at primary level are really asking for one calm, regular adult hour a week.

Once you choose someone, the practical details get fixed before the first visit: the day, the start time, the society gate process, and whether the session ends with a short conversation with you. For an IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai working with a six or seven-year-old, that last point matters more than it does with an older student, because most of what changes happens between sessions, in your house, not in the forty minutes the tutor is present.

sections.heading: What the Primary Years Programme actually asks of a Mumbai home
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from the early years to roughly Grade 5, after which most Mumbai schools move children into the Middle Years Programme (MYP). For a parent, the practical consequence is that there is no syllabus booklet to work through at home and no chapter numbers to stay ahead of.

That absence unsettles people. Parents who grew up with a textbook and a Saturday test go looking for the equivalent, cannot find it, and buy something instead: a grade-level workbook, an app with a streak counter, a second set of sums before dinner. Almost all of it substitutes for a thing the school has not asked for. The honest answer to the question of what you should be doing at home in these years is less structured work than feels responsible, and more reading, talking and ordinary household life than feels like enough.

There is one transition worth planning for rather than worrying about. Somewhere in the last couple of primary years, written work gets longer and more independent, and children who have done a lot of reading and talking tend to find that shift less jarring than children who have done a lot of worksheets. That is not an argument for drilling paragraphs in Grade 3. It is an argument for protecting reading time now, because reading is the thing that carries forward into everything else.

If you do bring someone in at this stage, be clear with yourself about why. Because other families in the tower have one is a weak reason. Because my child has stopped reading for pleasure and I want somebody who is not me to sit with her is a strong one, and so is because we have just moved from a different board in Thane and the way work is set here is unfamiliar. A PYP transdisciplinary learning tutor in Mumbai is not a syllabus coach; the job is closer to a reading companion with a plan. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, board or organisation named on this page, so nobody here has a commercial reason to tell you your child needs more hours than she does.
bullets: No chapter list to stay ahead of, which unsettles most parents initially
Written work lengthens late in the programme, so protect reading time now
A bought workbook usually substitutes for structure the school never requested
A specific reason for hiring beats copying what the neighbours did

sections.heading: Reading together long after your child can read alone
paragraphs: If you do only one thing at home during the primary years, read together, and keep doing it for years after your child can read alone. Reading aloud to a competent reader is not babying her. It lets her meet sentences, vocabulary and ideas well above what she can decode unaided, and it keeps books attached to your voice and the end of the day rather than to assessment.

Take turns. You read a page, she reads a page, and on the nights she is flat you read all of it and nobody comments on that. Stop at the interesting bit and ask what she thinks happens next, then let her be wrong without correcting her, because a prediction is a guess and a wrong guess is still thinking. Ask which character she would not want to sit next to on a bus. Let her pick books that are far too easy for her. A child re-reading the same comic for the fourth time is building fluency, not wasting an evening, and the quickest way to kill a reading habit is to audit it.

Number does not need a worksheet at this age either, and in a Mumbai day there is a usable amount of it lying around already. Count the change at the shop downstairs and let her hand it over. Work out how many minutes until the school bus and then check whether you were right. Double a recipe out loud while she helps. Read the score in an over and work out what is needed off the last six balls. Compare the distance from your building to Bandra with the distance to Vashi on your phone map and ask which is further. Each of those takes a minute, costs nothing, and does something a page of twenty sums does not, which is attach number to a real question somebody actually wanted answered.

The language of school will come home in your child's own words, and the useful move is simply to let it. If she says the class is finding out how water reaches the building, you have a week of conversations available: where the tanker comes from, who drives it, what happens in May when the pressure drops, why the overhead tank is on the roof. You are not teaching a unit and you should not try to. You are being a person who is interested in what she is interested in, and that is the one part no tutor can take over for you.
bullets: Read aloud past independence, taking turns, with no comprehension questions attached
Let easy books and repeat reads count, because repetition builds fluency

sections.heading: Home tuition across six Mumbai zones, and what the commute costs the evening
paragraphs: We match within zones for this age group, and the reason is bedtime rather than geography. A tutor who arrives at 7.40pm because the Western Express Highway was solid is no use to a seven-year-old, however good she is on paper. Across Mumbai the rule is identical in all six zones: short travel, early slot, same day every week.

In South Mumbai, Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar and Worli sit close together on the map and far apart in the evening. The Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals can absorb forty minutes at peak, so we match inside the island rather than bringing somebody down from the suburbs, and while the Coastal Road helps a Worli tutor reach Nariman Point it does nothing for a crawl through Kemps Corner at six. In the Western Suburbs, families in Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar are strung along the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7, so a tutor who lives on the line reaches you quickly and one crossing from the east does not. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link is fast; the approach road to it at half past six is not.

The Central Suburbs follow the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai has no station of its own, so a tutor reaches Hiranandani Gardens by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the JVLR queue is the single factor that decides whether a 6pm slot survives past October. Kurla, Ghatkopar and Mulund sit on the line and are easier. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Wadala are served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road, and the Eastern Freeway makes a Chembur tutor reachable from Wadala and the island far faster than the map suggests. Metro Line 1 between Versova and Ghatkopar is the one east-west move that reliably beats the road.

Navi Mumbai is built in nodes and we treat it that way. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel sit a short drive apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, served by the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines, and a tutor matched node to node holds a weekly slot for a full term. The Atal Setu has changed what a Sunday trip looks like, but it has not made a weekday evening crossing from the island sensible for forty minutes with a seven-year-old. In Thane, Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali are one zone on paper and two in traffic: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at seven, which is why we push Thane families towards an earlier slot than they first propose. Mulund tutors sometimes cross over on the Eastern Express Highway; the reverse happens less.

Wherever you are, IB home tuition in Mumbai works best when the tutor's own evening is not itself a battle. Ask the question plainly on the first call: where do you live, and how will you get here on a Wednesday at six in August?

Western Suburbs matched along the line, Khar West to Santacruz, Malad to Kandivali

sections.heading: Why is a Mumbai PYP child so tired by six in the evening?
paragraphs: Because the school day for a primary child in Mumbai is rarely only the school day. Add a bus of forty minutes each way, a uniform change, lunch, and for many children an activity wedged in between, and a seven-year-old has been awake and behaving herself since half past six in the morning. Flatness at six in the evening is the ordinary arithmetic of that, not a sign of anything.

The commute is the part parents consistently underestimate, because they are not the ones on the bus. A child at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu who lives up in Malad, or one at Oberoi International School on JVLR in Goregaon East who comes across from Andheri, can spend over an hour a day sitting in a vehicle before anything else happens. Children at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in Bandra Kurla Complex travel in from across the Western Suburbs and over the Sea Link. At Singapore International School in Dahisar East, at NES International School in Mulund West, or at D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, the catchment is wide in a different direction. No school is doing anything wrong here. The city is large, the roads are slow, and the cost of that lands on the child rather than on the timetable.

The school year in Mumbai mostly runs from June to the following April, with a break around Diwali and a long summer from late April. For primary, the pressure points are not examinations. They are the weeks when something is being presented or shared: a unit celebration, a class assembly, a sports day, a performance before the winter break, and in the final primary year a longer preparation stretch in the second half of the year. Those are precisely the weeks to cut everything optional at home, tuition included if you have it running.

What all of that means for a parent is straightforward and slightly uncomfortable. The evening is not spare capacity waiting to be used. If your child is flat at six, the useful intervention is food, a shower and a book, not thirty minutes of practice squeezed in before dinner. A tired child practising badly learns the thing badly and learns, more durably, that evenings at home are unpleasant. If one line from this page survives, make it that one.
bullets: Bus time both ways can exceed an hour across wide Mumbai catchments

sections.heading: Should a PYP child have home classes, online sessions, or neither?
paragraphs: For most primary-age children the honest first answer is neither, and the second answer is home. A tutor in the room can read a seven-year-old's face, slow down, switch to a game and stop early. An online session cannot do that nearly as well at this age, and after a full school day the screen itself is working against you.

A home session for a primary child should look nothing like the one an older sibling has. Short, somewhere between thirty and fifty minutes depending on the child. Mostly talk, reading, drawing, a game with cards or dice, and a small amount of writing at the end if it fits. The parent nearby rather than hovering, usually in the next room with the door open. No marking, no score, and no written report that reads like a performance review. The PYP transdisciplinary learning home classes Mumbai parents book should leave a child cheerful at the door; if she dreads Tuesday, the format is wrong even when the tutor is excellent.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai genuinely helps in a handful of situations. If you have moved out to Kharghar or Kasarvadavali and the person you trust lives in Bandra, online keeps a relationship that would otherwise end. If a session is lost to a fever or a flooded road in July, a twenty-minute online catch-up beats nothing. For a child who already spends part of the day on a screen, though, a weekly screen session is a hard sell, and most primary children drift inside fifteen minutes unless the tutor is unusually good at holding attention through a camera.

Hybrid is the realistic middle in this city. The standing weekly visit happens at home and the one-off makeup goes online when the monsoon or the Ghodbunder Road queue makes a visit impossible. The trade-off runs in both directions and we would rather say it plainly: home costs more in travel and is harder to reschedule at short notice, while online is easier to book and weaker at noticing a six-year-old has quietly stopped following. An IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai is the default we recommend at this age, and we say so even in the cases where online would be simpler for everyone involved, including us.

sections.heading: What a parent should check before an IB PYP home tutor arrives
paragraphs: IB Gram checks identity against government photo identification, confirms the degree or teaching qualification claimed, asks for and contacts references from previous families or schools, and records which boards and which age groups the tutor has actually taught. We do not accept IB experience as a self-description. Teaching a primary child is a separate skill from teaching a Diploma Programme (DP) subject, and somebody excellent at one can be poor at the other.

Then there is the part only you can do, and at this age it matters more than at any other. Watch the first session, or at the very least the first ten minutes of it. Does the tutor come down to your child's level or talk over her head to you? Does she wait after asking a question, or fill the silence herself because the pause is awkward? Does she laugh when your child says something strange? Does she open by finding out what the child likes, or by opening a book? None of that appears on a qualification, and all of it decides whether the arrangement lasts a term.

Ask these out loud before you commit. What ages have you taught in the last year? What will the first session look like? How long will you stay? What will you do on a day he does not want to work? How will you tell me how it went? A tutor who answers that last one with a promise of a weekly report with marks has misread the request. For a seven-year-old you want two sentences at the door, not a dashboard.

There is a household side to this too. Fix the society gate protocol early, get a standing visitor entry logged so the guard is not ringing you every week, and keep a clear rule that an adult is present in the flat. In most Mumbai buildings a regular tutor gets a standing gate pass once you have registered her once, and it is worth doing in week one rather than week four. If you are weighing up names and wondering how to pick an IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for more than one term, the answer is almost never the credential. It is whether the child looks forward to Tuesday.
bullets: Photo identification, qualification and references checked before any shortlist reaches you
Primary teaching experience verified separately from Diploma Programme subject experience
Watch the first ten minutes and notice who the tutor addresses
Ask what happens on a day your child refuses to work
Register the society gate pass in week one, not week four

sections.heading: How do you help at home without running a second school day?
paragraphs: By replacing instruction with attention. The most useful things a parent does in the primary years are reading together, talking about what happened, and leaving the child alone once she is done. The second school day begins the moment you start setting work, marking it, and insisting it is finished before dinner.

Start with what you ask at the door. What did you learn today gets nothing from almost every child in Mumbai and everywhere else, because it is a test question and children can hear a test question coming. Specific and slightly odd works far better. What did you wonder about today? What did somebody build or make? Who did you sit with at lunch and what did they have? Did anything go wrong? What was the loudest thing that happened? Ask one, not five, and ask it while you are both doing something else: in the car, waiting for the lift, chopping onions. Children talk sideways. They very rarely talk across a table while being looked at.

Then the harder discipline, which is letting errors stand. If your child writes that thay went to the beech and you correct both spellings, you have taught two spellings and taught, more lastingly, that writing is a thing adults fix. If instead you read it, laugh at the beach, ask what happened next and say nothing at all about thay, you have kept a writer in the house. At this age the asset most worth protecting is willingness. Pick one thing to mention, or none. A small error allowed to pass is very often the better teaching decision, and almost every parent finds that physically difficult to do for the first month.

When a child resists, price the fight before you win it. A nightly battle over twenty minutes of work buys you twenty minutes and spends the child's willingness to sit down with you at all, which is the asset every other thing on this page runs on. If the resistance is new, it is usually tiredness, something that happened at school, or work pitched at the wrong place, and asking plainly gets you further than pressing. Do you want to do this now, or after dinner, or not at all tonight is a real question, and you have to be genuinely willing to accept the third answer. Offering a choice you will not honour costs you more than never offering it.

There is an honest boundary where a parent should stop and go to the class teacher instead. When you cannot work out what is actually hard. When something that used to be easy has stopped being easy. When your child starts saying unkind things about herself. When you notice that you are the one getting upset in the evening. The teacher sees your child among thirty others every day and holds information you simply do not have from the sofa. Email her, describe what is happening at home in plain sentences, and ask what she would like you to do. That conversation costs nothing, happens quickly, and often settles the question of whether anyone needs hiring at all. A home tutor for PYP transdisciplinary learning Mumbai parents engage after that conversation tends to be a far better aimed appointment than one booked out of worry on a Sunday night.
bullets: Ask what she wondered or made, never what she learned today
Ask sideways, in the car or at the lift, not across a table
Correct one thing or nothing, and protect willingness above accuracy
Offer the option of not tonight, and be willing to honour it
Email the class teacher before hiring anybody, and ask what she sees

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one year of IB home tuition in Mumbai look like
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at results at all. You should be looking at whether your child is comfortable with the person, whether she mentions them unprompted between visits, and whether the house is calmer or tenser than it was in week one. That is the entire four-week test for a primary child, and if it fails, change the tutor or stop.

By the end of a term, roughly three months, the things worth noticing are small and behavioural rather than academic. She picks up a book without being asked to. She has an opinion about a story and argues it at dinner. She tries a sum out loud instead of waiting for you to confirm it first. She writes more than one sentence without stopping to ask whether it is right. None of that appears as a number anywhere, and in the primary years there is no number for it to appear on. If you want a crude measure, keep one piece of her writing from June and look at it again in December.

The honest limits are worth stating. A tutor cannot make a child enjoy reading in a house where nobody reads. A tutor cannot compensate for a bedtime that is too late, and sleep does more for a primary child's day than any session anybody can sell you. A tutor cannot repair a mismatch between a child and a school, although a good one is often the first adult willing to say out loud that it might be one. And IB Gram does not guarantee grades or outcomes of any kind, which is an unusually easy promise for us to decline at this stage, because in the primary years there are no grades to guarantee in the first place.

Across a year, what changes is frequently the parent as much as the child. Families who come to us asking for extra Maths practice quite often finish the year with a weekly reading session, a shorter evening and the report that the arguments have stopped. That is a real result even though nobody measured it. Parents searching for the best IB tutor in Mumbai are usually hoping for somebody who will produce a visible change, and the change that matters most at this age is largely invisible and happens in your own flat, between the visits, on the nights nobody is being taught anything.
bullets: Four weeks measures comfort and household temperature, not academic results
One term shows small shifts, like picking up a book unprompted
Keep a June piece of writing and compare it in December

sections.heading: Getting started with PYP home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Before you contact anybody, do two things. Email the class teacher and ask what she is seeing in the classroom. Then for one week, note on your phone the time your child actually stops being able to think in the evening. Those two pieces of information shape the match more than anything else you could send us.

When you do get in touch, tell us the grade, the school, the locality and pin code, the two or three evenings that are genuinely free, and what you would like to be different in three months. If you have a specific worry, say it in plain words; vague requests produce vague matches and a wasted fortnight. Tell us if there is a sibling in the flat, because a tutor who can hold two children at different stages in the same room is a different and narrower search.

The first session is deliberately low stakes. The tutor will spend a good part of it finding out what your child likes, what she reads, what the class is working on, and what she thinks she is good at. There may be very little written work produced and that is intentional rather than a slow start. You should be in the flat, nearby and reachable, and not sitting in the room watching, which changes how a seven-year-old behaves within about a minute. At the end you get two or three sentences at the door, not a report.

After that, give it a month before you judge it, and then judge it honestly. If it is not working, say so and we will change the tutor; nobody here will try to talk you into one more month to see. And if what you actually need turns out to be no tutor at all and twenty minutes of reading on the sofa, we would far rather you did that instead. The point of an IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai at this age is to make the house calmer, not busier.
bullets: Email the class teacher first and write down what she reports
Track for a week when your child stops being able to think
Send grade, school, pin code and two genuinely free evenings

faqs.question: Does a PYP child actually need a home tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Often not, and you should be wary of anyone who says otherwise before meeting your child. Many primary children do perfectly well on reading at home, conversation and enough sleep, and one of the most common useful outcomes of a first call with us is a parent deciding to wait a term. A tutor earns a place when something specific is going on: a change of board or country mid-year, a child who has stopped reading for pleasure, a language of instruction that is not spoken at home, or a parent and child who cannot work together without the evening ending badly. Those are real reasons. Everyone in the building has one is not.

faqs.question: What does a session with a primary-age child actually look like?
faqs.answer: Mostly talk, reading, play and a little writing, in that order. A good session for a seven-year-old runs thirty to fifty minutes and does not resemble a class. The tutor might read half a chapter with your child taking turns, play a dice game that happens to be addition, ask what the class is finding out about this week and chase it for ten minutes, then write three sentences about it together. An IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai who sits a primary child in front of a worksheet for forty minutes is delivering what a printed workbook already does, and that is the version least likely to change anything.

faqs.question: The tutor has to reach our building in Powai on a weekday evening. Is that realistic?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the slot is early and the tutor lives on the right side of the road. Powai has no railway station of its own, so tutors reach Hiranandani Gardens and Chandivali by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and JVLR at seven is the deciding factor. A 5.30pm or 6pm start usually holds through the year; an 8pm start looks workable in June and collapses in the monsoon. We match Powai families with tutors already working across the Central Suburbs rather than with someone who would be crossing the city for one short session.

faqs.question: Do I have to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Yes, an adult should be in the flat, and for this age we strongly prefer it to be you for the first few weeks. Not in the room, though. A seven-year-old performs for a watching parent and stops thinking. The arrangement that works is the door left open, you within earshot in the kitchen or the next room, and two minutes of conversation at the end. If work genuinely makes that impossible, a grandparent or a long-standing member of the household being present is acceptable, but somebody responsible is at home, every time, without exception.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on at primary level?
faqs.answer: Level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, in roughly that order. IB tuition fees in Mumbai usually sit lower for primary than for Diploma Programme subjects, because the pool of people who can teach a seven-year-old well is larger than the pool who can teach Higher Level (HL) Physics. Travel matters more than parents expect: a tutor crossing Ghodbunder Road or coming over the Atal Setu is pricing an hour of her own evening into the visit. Shorter sessions cost less than long ones, and at this age shorter is also better teaching, so for once the incentives point the same way.

faqs.question: My child melts down over homework every evening. Should I push through it?
faqs.answer: No. A nightly fight over primary homework costs far more than the homework is worth, and what you lose is her willingness to work with you at all. Change the variables first: do it straight after a snack rather than after a screen, do ten minutes rather than thirty, sit at the table doing your own work alongside her rather than supervising. If it still goes badly after a fortnight, email the class teacher and describe exactly what is happening at home. Teachers would overwhelmingly rather know than receive work that was extracted by argument the night before.

faqs.question: We are in Kharghar and the tutor we liked lives in Bandra. Online or find someone local?
faqs.answer: Find someone local for the weekly session. Kharghar to Bandra is a long evening crossing even with the Atal Setu, and a tutor making it for forty minutes with a primary child will quietly give up by the third month. Navi Mumbai has a real pool across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, and node-to-node matching along Palm Beach Road holds for a full term. If you are attached to the Bandra tutor specifically, a fortnightly online session with her alongside a local weekly visit is a workable hybrid, but do not build the whole arrangement on a commute nobody can sustain.

faqs.question: How long before we see something change?
faqs.answer: Expect a change in mood before a change in work, and expect the first to take about a month. In the opening four weeks the only questions are whether your child is comfortable with the person and whether the evening is calmer than it was. Across a term you may notice smaller things: a book picked up without prompting, a sum attempted out loud, a longer piece of writing produced without checking first. There is no mark to watch in the primary years and no number we can point at, and we do not guarantee grades or outcomes at any stage of any programme.

faqs.question: The tutor seems competent but my child is not warming to her. What now?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we will change the tutor, usually inside a week or two. At primary level fit is not a nice extra; it is most of the service, and a technically strong tutor a child does not like will produce nothing worth paying for. You do not need to justify the request or wait for something to go wrong first. What helps us is specificity: she talks to me instead of to him, he goes quiet the moment she arrives, he enjoyed the first two sessions and has gone off it since. We use that to choose the next person rather than sending a near-identical profile.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child after school instead of what did you learn?
faqs.answer: Ask something specific and slightly odd, and ask only one thing. What did you wonder about today? What was the loudest thing that happened? Who did you sit with at lunch? Did anything go wrong, and who fixed it? What did you learn is a test question, and children answer test questions with nothing. Timing matters as much as wording: ask while walking to the lift, during the drive, or while you are both doing something with your hands. Mumbai school runs are long, and the car is frequently the best conversation available all day.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of rain or traffic?
faqs.answer: It gets rescheduled, and in a Mumbai July that has to be agreed before it happens rather than argued about afterwards. Fix the rule in the first week: who calls whom, by what time, and whether the makeup goes online or moves to the weekend. Waterlogging on the Eastern Express Highway or a halted Western Line service is nobody's fault, and a tutor who sets out from Mulund and turns back at Bhandup should not forfeit the slot. Families who settle this in week one have noticeably fewer arguments through the monsoon than those who improvise it each time.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB PYP maths home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: The message that arrives is almost never "find a tutor". It is usually a full sentence with the real problem buried in the second half: my daughter is in PYP 3 at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, she cries at her maths homework, and I need somebody at the house on Tuesdays and Fridays after five because I get back from Lower Parel at half past six. Both halves matter equally. The first half tells us which tutor can teach the International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP) at that age. The second half tells us which of those tutors can physically be standing at your gate at five past five, week after week, for a whole term.

So the matching runs travel first. A tutor in Mulund who is genuinely good with eight-year-olds is still the wrong tutor for a family in Khar West on a Wednesday evening, because that tutor will spend longer on the Eastern Express Highway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road than in your living room. We keep a tutor's working radius narrow on purpose. Along the Western Line that means Bandra to Santacruz, or Malad to Kandivali, rather than Churchgate to Borivali. In the Central Suburbs it means Powai and Chandivali served from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, because Powai has no station of its own and everything there arrives by road off JVLR. In Navi Mumbai it means node to node, Vashi to Nerul or Belapur to Kharghar, not across the creek for a weekday lesson.

Only then do we look at who has actually taught primary maths inside an IB school rather than coached a Grade 10 board batch. PYP maths teaching is a separate craft. The tutor has to be comfortable sitting with a child who has not yet decided whether she is good at maths, and who will take her cue from the adult's face when she gets a subtraction wrong. A Mathematics tutor in Mumbai who has spent ten years on Diploma Programme (DP) calculus is not automatically that person, and we do not pretend otherwise.
The sequence below is the whole process. Nothing is hidden behind it and there is no sales call in the middle of it.

sections.heading: Where PYP sits, and what comes after it
paragraphs: The Primary Years Programme covers the early and primary school years, up to the point where a child moves into the Middle Years Programme (MYP). In Mumbai the schools that run it as a full authorised programme are a short list rather than a long one: Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School at Goregaon East (JVLR) are the two most parents are choosing between, with JBCN International School, Parel and Singapore International School at Dahisar East drawing families from the island city and the far north respectively. Several other schools run a primary curriculum that is IB-influenced without being authorised PYP, which is worth checking on the school's own page before you assume the two are the same thing.

What makes this stage structurally different from everything above it is that there is no external examination anywhere in it. No papers, no grade boundaries, no May or November session. Progress is reported through the school's own assessment of conceptual understanding and through units of inquiry, which means a parent gets a report that talks about transdisciplinary skills and a child who cannot reliably work out change from a hundred rupees. That gap between the report language and the kitchen-table reality is the single most common reason a Mumbai parent starts looking for an IB home tutor in Mumbai at this age.

A Mathematics IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor Mumbai parents hire is therefore not preparing anybody for anything. The job is to build the number sense, the place value and the willingness to try that the MYP will assume is already there. The pressure is real but it is deferred: the child who leaves PYP shaky on fractions and negative numbers meets them again in MYP 1 at speed, with a new school timetable and a locker and five other subjects, and the gap widens quietly for two years.

An IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for two or three years at this stage usually starts as a short intervention and turns into a standing appointment, because the parent discovers the useful part is not remediation but the weekly habit of a child explaining her thinking out loud to an adult who is not her mother.

sections.heading: What a PYP maths tutor builds now that the Diploma will cash in later
paragraphs: Parents who have an older child already in the Diploma Programme ask about the far end of the road almost immediately, and the honest answer is that it is a long way off but the direction is real. At DP a student chooses between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, and then between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) within that choice. The Analysis and Approaches route leans on algebraic fluency, proof and calculus. The Applications and Interpretation route leans on modelling, data and technology use. Every DP student in either route also produces a mathematical exploration as the Internal Assessment (IA), a piece of independent written mathematics on a topic of their own choosing. Check the current subject guide or your school's coordinator for how any of this is structured and weighted in the year your child actually sits it, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle and a figure that was true last year may not be true next.

None of that is a PYP tutor's business to teach. What it does tell you is which habits are worth money later. The AA and AI route choice at sixteen is usually decided by how comfortable a student is manipulating symbols without a context to lean on, and that comfort is laid down years earlier by children who were allowed to see that a number can be taken apart and put back together. The HL versus SL decision is largely a question of stamina with unfamiliar problems. The exploration rewards a student who can hold a question in her head for three weeks without being told the method. These are dispositions, not topics, and they are built at seven, not seventeen.

So the concrete work in a PYP maths session looks small and slow. A tutor spends twenty minutes on why the nine in ninety and the nine in nine hundred are not the same nine, using the physical arrangement of counters on the table rather than a rule. Another session is spent entirely on a child being allowed to get a problem wrong, say out loud why she thought it was right, and find the error herself. A third works on reading a word problem twice before touching a pencil, which is a skill that is still earning marks for students in DP 2.
Our siblings pages cover the full PYP maths scope and sequence strand by strand, and the DP route teaching in detail. This page stays on what the home visit itself is for.

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar shapes a weekly home slot
paragraphs: PYP has no examination season, which fools parents into thinking the year is flat. It is not. The pressure points are set by the school's own reporting cycle and by the rest of the household. The first few weeks after the June start are when a new teacher's expectations land and when a child who coasted last year is suddenly visibly behind. The stretch before the first reporting cycle and the parent-teacher conferences is when most families call us, because that is when the report language arrives and the gap becomes undeniable. The Diwali break resets everything and the fortnight after it is the worst time to start something new. March and April carry the tail end of the year and the transition conversations about moving up a year group or into MYP.

The household calendar matters just as much. A family in Chembur with one child in PYP 4 and one in DP 2 will discover in October that the older child's Internal Assessment drafts and the younger child's maths slot are competing for the same adult attention and the same quiet room. Families near Dhirubhai Ambani International School at BKC and the American School of Bombay deal with a different squeeze, because BKC traffic in the evening peak decides whether a tutor arrives at six or at half past. In Thane, families at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School plan around the Ghodbunder Road commute rather than the school bell. In Navi Mumbai, families at D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul usually want a slot that fits between the school bus drop and dinner, which in practice means a tutor who already lives in the node.

Our practical advice on scheduling is boring and it works. Pick a slot that is slightly later than you think you need, because the thing that kills a weekly arrangement is not the tutor's commitment but a twenty-minute delay happening every single week until everybody is irritated. Avoid the half hour immediately after the school bus arrives, when a seven-year-old is hungry and useless. Keep the slot on the same two days every week so it becomes furniture rather than a negotiation.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Ecole Mondiale World School, Oberoi International School, Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay or any other school named on this page.
