sections.heading: What the TOK essay rewards, and what it quietly punishes
paragraphs: The TOK essay is marked on one global judgement: whether the student has produced a clear, coherent and critical exploration of the title they chose. Everything that earns credit follows from that. The essay rewards arguments about how knowledge is made and defended inside specific Areas of Knowledge, examples precise enough that a reader could check them, genuine consideration of a perspective the student does not hold, and some honest statement of what follows if the argument is right. Ask your school for the current TOK subject guide and read the assessment instrument in it yourself; it is shorter than you expect.

What the essay punishes is topic writing. A title about the role of evidence becomes an essay about climate change, with three paragraphs of science and no claim about how scientific knowledge gets accepted. The student has written something informative and scored almost nothing, because the question was never about climate. The second common loss is breadth: five Areas of Knowledge mentioned in passing, none of them examined. Two areas handled properly beat a tour of the lot, and a good tutor will cut an area out of a plan on the first evening rather than the fourth.

Examples are where home tuition earns its keep. Students arrive with examples they have read about and cannot defend, usually a famous experiment or a historical turn they know one sentence of. A tutor's job is to press: what exactly was claimed, who accepted it, on what grounds, and what would have changed their mind. Half of those examples fall apart under two minutes of questioning, which is far better happening in your living room in November than in an examiner's hands in March.

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar sets the TOK essay clock
paragraphs: Most IB schools in Mumbai open their academic year in the middle of the monsoon and sit the May examination session, which pushes the TOK essay into a predictable squeeze. DP2 begins while the rain is still closing roads at Sion, Hindmata, Milan Subway and the Andheri subway, the school runs its titles session in the first weeks, and then the internal deadlines begin to stack. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, and Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai all describe the same pattern from different postcodes.

October and November are the real pressure points. The TOK essay's first full draft, an Internal Assessment (IA) or two, and the Extended Essay all tend to land either side of the Diwali break, and the break itself is the trap: a fortnight at home reads like free time and is usually spent on travel and family. A DP2 student at B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade or Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo who goes into Diwali with a plan and two paragraphs comes out of it in reasonable shape. One who goes in with a title and nothing else loses the only unbroken fortnight of the year.

Ask the DP coordinator or the examinations officer for this session's internal dates in writing, and ignore any date you have heard from another parent. Schools set their own interim deadlines well ahead of the IB's upload window so that supervisors have time to authenticate work, and those interim dates differ between NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Parel and Oberoi International School on JVLR. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page; we name them because their calendars are what your child's weeks look like.

sections.heading: Is a home tutor or an online tutor better for TOK essay work?
paragraphs: For TOK essay work an IB home tutor in Mumbai is usually the stronger first choice, because the session is a conversation over a printed draft and the student has to be the one talking. IB TOK essay help in Mumbai delivered in a dining room has one unglamorous advantage: nobody can hide behind a muted microphone. The tutor reads a paragraph, asks what it is claiming, and waits. Sitting across a table makes that silence productive. Home tuition also fixes attendance, which is the whole game in a drafting cycle; a tutor who is physically in your flat at seven on a Wednesday gets a session even on evenings when your child would have cancelled.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai is the right answer in three situations, and parents should not be talked out of it. If your child needs a TOK specialist strong in an Area of Knowledge that is scarce near you, online opens the whole city instead of one corridor. If the family is in Kasarvadavali or Panvel, where an evening road trip can eat ninety minutes each way, online converts travel time into session time. And in the final fortnight, short online reviews of a redrafted section work better than a weekly ninety-minute visit, because feedback needs to arrive the day after the rewrite rather than six days later.

Hybrid is what most TOK families settle into without planning it. Fortnightly home classes for the slow structural work, with screen-shared reviews in between for the paragraph-level rewrites. The honest trade-offs: online demands that your child can type and talk at once and that your connection holds through a downpour, while home visits are hostage to traffic and to a study space that is actually quiet. Decide which risk your household handles better, then say so when you speak to the shortlist rather than discovering it in week four.

TOK experience is the one most platforms skip: having taught DP Physics is not evidence of being able to coach a TOK essay, and we ask for the sessions a tutor has actually supervised or examined and what the students were writing about.

We also check how a tutor talks about academic honesty, because that is the risk a TOK essay carries. A tutor who offers to tighten your child's prose directly, send over a model essay, or supply paragraphs to adapt is not a tutor you want near an externally assessed piece of work that a supervisor has to authenticate. Anyone matched through IB Gram coaches questions, structure and feedback on your child's own drafts, and does not write, co-write or supply content. Your own checks matter as much as ours, and they take one phone call. Ask which prescribed titles the tutor has worked on and what the students did badly. Ask how they would handle a draft that is interesting and off-title. Ask what they will send you after each session. sections.heading: Choosing a prescribed title your child can actually argue
paragraphs: Title choice decides most of the outcome, and it is made in a week when nobody is paying attention. The titles the IB publishes for a session are deliberately awkward: each one contains a claim about knowledge, usually with a word in it doing quiet work, and the essay has to engage that word rather than walk past it. Students pick the title that sounds most like something they already believe, which is the worst possible reason. The right test is supply: for which title can this student produce two Areas of Knowledge and four examples they can defend under questioning tonight, without a browser open?

Then comes the scope trap. A title that invites discussion of knowledge in general tempts a student into covering everything at a centimetre's depth. The tutor's intervention is a single ruthless plan: this claim, these two areas, this example and this counter-example, these implications. A plan that fits on one side of paper is the signal that the thinking has actually happened. If the plan needs two pages, the essay will be a survey, and surveys read as informed and score as thin. Cutting a second plan down is normal; a student who refuses to cut has usually not understood the title yet.

The drafting rhythm matters as much as the plan. Supervisor interactions are recorded on the planning and progress form your school keeps, and that record is part of the work, not paperwork around it: ask the coordinator what the current requirement is for your child's session and what the form must show. The useful pattern is draft, supervisor meeting, redraft against the published criterion, tutor session on the argument, redraft again. A tutor sits between those meetings and never replaces them. IB TOK essay help in Mumbai that pulls a student away from their own supervisor is actively harmful, because the supervisor is the person who authenticates the final piece.

sections.heading: What four weeks of IB TOK essay help in Mumbai should change
paragraphs: At four weeks, the honest measure is not a grade. It is whether your child can say out loud, in two sentences, what their essay argues and which claim about knowledge it is testing. If they can, the structural work is done and the rest is writing. If they still answer with a topic, something has gone wrong in the match or the title choice, and that is worth raising immediately rather than waiting for a report. A first full draft that is genuinely on-title, even if clumsy, is a good four-week result. A polished draft that answers a slightly different question is not.

At one term you should see a finished essay that has been through at least two real redrafts, each one triggered by a specific weakness rather than general tidying. You should also see the habit transferring: students who have been properly coached through TOK start asking harder questions about evidence in their other subjects, which shows up in IA introductions and in history essays. Over a full examination cycle, the gain parents report most often is time, because a child who is not stuck on the core has their weekends back for subject revision.

The honest limits need saying. Home tuition cannot manufacture reading that was never done, and TOK rewards a student who has noticed things. It cannot fix a title chosen badly in month one without starting again, which late in the year may not be possible. It cannot stand in for the supervisor relationship. And a tutor who meets your child weekly for a term still has fewer hours with them than one week of school. IB Gram does not guarantee grades; what good TOK coaching reliably produces is a student who knows what their own argument is.

faqs.question: Will the tutor write any part of my child's TOK essay?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor matched through IB Gram coaches the process and never writes, co-writes or supplies text. The TOK essay is externally assessed and authenticated by your child's supervisor at school, so work that is not the student's own puts the whole diploma at risk through an academic misconduct finding. What a tutor does instead is ask what each paragraph claims, press on whether an example holds up, point out where the title has been abandoned, and give structured feedback on your child's own drafts. If anyone offers to tighten the prose for you, that is the moment to walk away from them.

faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided the tutor is matched from within South Mumbai rather than brought down from the suburbs. A seven o'clock slot in Worli works well for a tutor living between Mahalaxmi and Prabhadevi, and the Coastal Road has made the run from Nariman Point manageable. What does not hold for a full term is pulling someone across from Andheri or Ghatkopar in the evening peak. faqs.question: How many sessions does a TOK essay usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than parents expect, but spread over longer. TOK essay coaching works as a short series of sessions placed at the structural decision points rather than a weekly subject tuition rhythm: one on title choice, one on the plan, one on the first draft, then one after each substantive redraft. A student starting early often needs only a handful across a term. A student arriving two weeks before an internal deadline needs more sessions packed closer together, and gets less from them, because thinking does not compress well. We will tell you which pattern your timeline allows.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for TOK essay work?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a fixed price list. The board and level, since DP core coaching draws on a smaller pool than IGCSE subject work. The scarcity of the specialism, because a tutor strong in the arts or in mathematics as an Area of Knowledge is harder to find than a generalist. Travel distance, since an hour each way on Ghodbunder Road is real time. Session length, as a ninety-minute drafting session is not two short ones. And urgency, because a compressed schedule in the final fortnight costs more to staff. You will see the rate before anything is booked.

faqs.question: My daughter has her prescribed title and is stuck on the opening paragraph. Where does a tutor start?
faqs.answer: Not with the paragraph. A tutor starts by asking her to say what the title is claiming and what she thinks about it, in her own words, with nothing written down. Students stuck on an opening are almost always stuck on the argument, and writing is the symptom. Once she can state a position in two sentences and name the two Areas of Knowledge she will use, the opening writes itself in fifteen minutes. If she cannot, the session goes to examples instead, because an argument she cannot illustrate is not yet an argument she can defend.

faqs.question: Does online TOK help work as well as home tuition?
faqs.answer: For feedback on a redrafted section, online is often better, because the comments arrive the day after the rewrite instead of at the next weekly visit. For the structural conversations, title choice, the plan, the first full read, home classes are stronger, since a student cannot retreat into a muted microphone when the tutor asks what a paragraph is doing. Most TOK families end up hybrid without deciding to: fortnightly home tuition for the heavy thinking and short screen-shared reviews in between. Pick by which risk you handle better, traffic or connectivity.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar and both parents work late. Can sessions run after seven with nobody home?
faqs.answer: That is a decision for you, and we will tell you what most families here do. In Navi Mumbai nodes like Kharghar, Belapur and Nerul, tutors are matched within the node so a half past seven start is realistic rather than aspirational. Many parents keep sessions in a living room with a helper present and the door open, which is sensible practice for any home tuition arrangement. Others shift to online for the weekday slot and keep a weekend home visit for the longer work. Say which you prefer during the introduction call.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week two rather than week six. The usual signal is not rudeness but drift: sessions that feel pleasant and produce no decisions, or a tutor doing most of the talking. We ask you two questions, what was supposed to change and what actually changed, and then re-match from the remaining shortlist, usually with the same timetable slot so your child's week does not move. The new tutor gets the plan and the drafts rather than starting from nothing. Replacement is a normal part of matching and not a complaint we take badly.

faqs.question: Can the tutor speak to my child's TOK teacher at school?
faqs.answer: Only if the school invites it, and we do not push for it. The supervisor relationship belongs to the school, which authenticates the final essay, and a private tutor contacting a teacher directly can create exactly the impression you want to avoid. What works instead is the student carrying the information both ways: bringing the supervisor's written comments to the session, and taking a clear plan back to the next meeting. A tutor who wants to deal with the school over your child's head has misunderstood where they sit in this.

faqs.question: Is it too late to get help two weeks before the school deadline?
faqs.answer: No, but the work changes. With a fortnight left, nobody is rethinking the title. The sessions go to making the existing draft answer the question it is nearest to: cutting the paragraphs that discuss the topic rather than the knowledge claim, strengthening two examples instead of adding four, and making the implications explicit at the end. That is genuine improvement and it is honest work. Starting in the first month of DP2 is simply a different and better position, so if you have a DP1 student at home, this is the useful month to plan.

faqs.question: Do you promise a specific TOK grade if we book a full term?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest will. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because the essay is written and submitted by your child and assessed externally against a published criterion. What a term of structured coaching does reliably produce is a student who knows what their own argument is, has defended it under questioning, and has redrafted against the criterion rather than against a parent's taste. Be wary of any tutor who quotes a guaranteed grade for core coaching. The right question to ask instead is what their last TOK student actually struggled with.

sections.heading: Is the exhibition the same task as the TOK essay?
paragraphs: No, and treating them as one task is the most expensive mistake a DP1 family makes. The exhibition and the essay are two separate assessments inside Theory of Knowledge, which itself sits in the Diploma Programme (DP) core next to the Extended Essay (EE). The exhibition is internally assessed by the school and then externally moderated; the essay is written to a prescribed title and marked outside the school. They reward different work. The exhibition rewards precise accounting for particular things in the world. The essay rewards sustained argument. A tutor who runs one like the other will waste your term.

There is a prior question, and parents should settle it before buying any coaching: which course is your child actually entered for? Theory of Knowledge appears only in the DP. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student or a Cambridge IGCSE student has no exhibition and no prompts, and an enquiry about one usually turns out to concern the MYP personal project or a Grade 10 student preparing for DP1. Ask the DP coordinator in writing for the course, the year group and the component. Sibling experience and school prospectuses are both unreliable guides here.

Within the DP, the exhibition is normally a DP1 task, which changes its character. Your child is doing it in the year when nothing feels urgent, alongside first Internal Assessment (IA) planning and subject choices that are still settling. The register runs across all IB and IGCSE subjects and any tutor in Mumbai listed on it has been checked the same way, so exhibition coaching can be arranged alongside a subject tutor without two separate conversations about availability.

sections.heading: Objects, prompts and commentary: what is actually being assessed
paragraphs: Three parts make up the exhibition, and credit lives in how tightly they hold together. There is a chosen prompt, taken as published from the list in the subject guide. There are objects, which have to be specific things with a real place in the world rather than categories of thing. And there is a commentary, in which your child identifies each object, gives its particular real-world context, and justifies why it belongs in an exhibition on that prompt. Appropriate references are part of the task, not an afterthought. Check the current guide for the exact requirements of your child's session, because wording is revised on the IB's own cycle.

The single biggest loss is generic objects. A student writes about social media, or photography, or the periodic table. None of those is an object; each is a class of things, and a commentary about a class cannot supply a real-world context. The fix is almost mechanical: name the thing. Not photography but one specific photograph, taken by a named person on a known day. Not social media but one particular post, with its author, its date and what happened after it. A commentary that can answer when, where and whose is already most of the way to clearing the task.

The second loss is decoration. The objects are chosen because they look good together, and the links to the prompt are written afterwards to fit. Moderators see this constantly, and it reads as a poster rather than an exhibition. The test a good tutor applies early is reversal: if the prompt changed, would this object still be in? If yes, the link is probably weak. Home classes are useful here because objects can physically be on the table while the question is asked, which makes the honest answer harder to avoid.
bullets: A named specific thing, never a category: this photograph, not photography
Each object needs a real-world context with when, where and whose answered

sections.heading: Why does the exhibition sneak up on DP1 students in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Because it is set in the quietest term of the two-year course and collected in one of the busiest. Mumbai IB schools open the year in the monsoon and mostly enter students for the May session, so DP1 begins while roads at Sion, Milan Subway and the Andheri subway are still flooding. The exhibition is introduced early, often with a lesson on the prompts and then nothing for weeks, and a DP1 student with no examinations in sight files it mentally under later. Later turns out to be the fortnight when the first subject IAs are also due.

The calendars at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and Ascend International School in BKC, Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Thakur International School in Kandivali East and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane differ in their dates and agree in their shape. There is a prompt commitment point, an object review or a draft commentary checkpoint, and a submission date before the school's own internal moderation. If you only ask for one date, ask for the object review date, because that is the one your child can still act on.

The pressure points worth marking on a kitchen calendar are the weeks around the Diwali break and the run into the final term of DP1. Diwali is deceptive: it looks like a clear fortnight and it is mostly travel. A student at Oberoi International School on JVLR or JBCN International School in Chembur who walks into that break with objects chosen and photographed comes out of it needing only the commentary. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any school named here, and we name these schools only because their term dates are what your child's weeks actually look like.

sections.heading: Should object sessions be home classes or a video call?
paragraphs: Object selection is the one part of this task that genuinely goes better in person. Home classes let your child put six candidate things on a table, and let the tutor pick one up and ask who gave it to you, when, and what happened to it afterwards. That question is harder to dodge with the thing in your hand. IB TOK exhibition help in Mumbai in the first few weeks is therefore usually arranged as home tuition, with the parent shown the longlist at the end of the first session rather than a progress rating.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai becomes the better choice once the objects are fixed. Commentary work is screen work: the student shares a document, the tutor queries a justification line by line, and the rewrite happens between sessions. Online also solves two real Mumbai problems. It opens the specialist pool beyond your corridor when exhibition-experienced tutors near you are already booked, and it removes a ninety minute round trip on Ghodbunder Road or across the creek to Panvel, which converts travel into teaching time.

Most families end up hybrid, and we recommend planning for it rather than drifting into it. A home visit for the inventory and the object review, screen sessions for the commentary drafts, and one last in-person session before submission to check the images and references. The trade-offs are plain. In-person sessions lose to traffic and to a study space that is really the television room. Online sessions lose to a dropped connection in a downpour and to a student who can look busy while doing nothing. Pick the failure you can manage.

sections.heading: Checks we run, and the three questions you should ask
paragraphs: Each tutor clears three checks before a profile reaches you. Identity, through a government photo document matched to the profile name. Qualifications, verified rather than taken on trust, with the subject background read against what the tutor says they can coach. And component experience, which for this task means exhibition work specifically: internal assessment, internal standardisation or moderation. Teaching DP Economics for years is not evidence of knowing why a commentary loses credit on justification. Tutors are registered for all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 and no tutor Mumbai families meet skips that check.

We also test attitude to academic honesty, because this component invites a particular kind of cheating that does not look like cheating. Choosing the objects for the student, drafting a justification paragraph for them to adapt, or supplying a worked example of somebody else's exhibition all cross the line, and the school has to authenticate the work. Anybody matched through IB Gram coaches the questions and gives feedback on your child's own commentary. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor promising a specific mark on an internally assessed component has told you exactly what they are.

Your own three questions take five minutes on the introduction call and are worth more than any badge. First: which prompts have you worked on, and what did students get wrong? Second: if my daughter brings you an object you find weak, what do you say and when? Third: what will I receive after each session? Parents type best IB tutor in Mumbai into Google and get directories; the useful filter is whether somebody will tell a polite teenager that a favourite object has to go.

sections.heading: Choosing three objects that are yours and not a poster
paragraphs: Start from what your child already has, and only then look at the prompts. Reversing that order is the single most useful thing a tutor does in week one. An inventory session runs through the physical and digital things your child can account for: a school house badge, a train pass, a temple offering receipt, a screenshot of a group argument, a certificate, a grandparent's identity document, a photograph nobody else has. Most students produce more than they expect once somebody asks properly, and a longlist drawn from life nearly always beats a shortlist drawn from a web search.

The scope trap here is not breadth, it is distance. Students reach for objects of world importance, a famous painting or a historic treaty, because they feel weighty. Those objects are hard to supply a real-world context for in your own words, and a commentary about them tends to turn into description. An object the student can speak about with authority gives the justification somewhere to go. Weight is not the criterion; specificity and a defensible link to the prompt are. One borrowed object of obvious significance plus two personal ones is a workable mix.

Then redraft against what the task rewards rather than against polish. The useful loop for the commentary is: identify the object precisely, state its particular context, say why it belongs in an exhibition on this prompt, and check the link survives a change of prompt. Your child's teacher is the person who assesses this and the checkpoints they set are the real deadlines. A tutor sits between those checkpoints, prepares your child to use them, and never substitutes for them. Keep a source note the day each object is chosen, because reconstructing references in the last week is miserable and avoidable.
bullets: Inventory first, prompts second; life beats a web search for objects
Prefer objects your child can speak about with real authority

sections.heading: IB TOK exhibition help in Mumbai: what good looks like at four weeks
paragraphs: Four weeks in, the test is whether your child can hold up each object and say in one sentence why it is in the exhibition and not merely interesting. Not a paragraph, one sentence. If all three objects pass that, the commentary is a writing job and the thinking is finished. If an object produces hedging, it is the wrong object and the next session should replace it, which is normal in week four and painful in week ten. A longlist cut to a defensible three, with photographs taken and sources noted, is a good first month.

By the end of a term you should see a complete commentary that has been through two genuine redrafts, each prompted by a named weakness rather than a general tidy, plus images and references in the format the school asks for. Across a full year, the transferable gain parents notice is that the student has become harder to fool by their own work: they start asking whether an IA introduction actually justifies its method. That habit shows up in DP2 and is worth more than the component mark itself.

The limits are real and worth hearing before you commit. A tutor cannot give your child a history they do not have, and this task rewards students who have noticed their own lives. A tutor cannot repair a prompt chosen badly in month one once the school checkpoint has passed. And home tuition for one evening a week is a small fraction of the hours school already has. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What reliably improves is the quality of the justification, which is exactly what the moderator reads.
bullets: Week four: three objects, each defended in one unhedged sentence

Session one is an inventory and a diagnosis, not a lecture. faqs.question: Will a tutor choose my son's objects or write his commentary?
faqs.answer: No. Objects are chosen by your child and the commentary is written by your child, with the tutor asking the questions that make both defensible. The exhibition is internally assessed and your son's teacher has to authenticate it as his own work, so a tutor who supplies objects or drafts a justification paragraph is creating an academic misconduct risk that can reach the whole diploma. What a tutor legitimately does is run the inventory session, press on weak links, mark where a context is missing, and give feedback on drafts your son has written himself.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building in Borivali on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the match should be made inside the corridor for it to last. For Borivali we look at tutors living between Malad, Kandivali and Dahisar, who can reach you on Link Road or the Western Line without an hour of travel, rather than someone excellent in Chembur who will quietly start cancelling in September. Half past six and half past seven starts both work in practice. Tell us which of the two your household can hold every week, and whether the society needs a visitor pass arranged before the first visit.

faqs.question: What counts as a specific object, and what gets rejected as generic?
faqs.answer: Specific means one thing with a traceable history: this ticket, this letter, this particular photograph taken by a named person. Generic means a category, which is what loses credit: social media, newspapers, museums, textbooks. The quick test is whether your child can answer when, where and whose about the object without inventing anything. A screenshot of one identifiable post passes. The idea of online debate does not. Digital objects are perfectly acceptable as long as they are particular and your child can account for how they encountered them.

faqs.question: How is the exhibition different from the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: They share nothing but a year group. The Extended Essay is a long independent research piece with a supervisor and a research question, assessed externally. The exhibition is a short commentary on three particular objects and one published prompt, assessed inside the school and then moderated. The skills barely overlap: the Extended Essay rewards sustained research and the exhibition rewards precise accounting for things in the world. Do not hire one tutor on the assumption that they cover both, and do not let exhibition work slide because the essay feels bigger.

faqs.question: My daughter picked a prompt in July and has done nothing since. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is normal and it is fixable, provided the school's object review date has not passed. The standard rescue is an inventory session that works from her own life rather than from the prompt, followed by an honest check of whether the prompt she picked suits the objects she can actually account for. Sometimes the prompt changes, which is a decision to take early and with her teacher's knowledge. Starting in the final weeks is the version that genuinely hurts, because object photography and references take longer than anyone budgets for.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy or print anything for the exhibition?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. The task asks your child to account for objects, not to acquire impressive ones, and buying something for an exhibition usually destroys exactly the personal context that earns credit. What is worth doing is photographing the chosen objects properly and early, in decent light, and keeping a note of where each came from on the day it is chosen. Ask the school what image format and reference style it wants, since that is set locally and parents frequently discover it the night before submission.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for exhibition coaching?
faqs.answer: Board and level, the scarcity of the component specialism, travel distance, session length and how compressed your timeline is. DP core coaching comes from a smaller pool than IGCSE subject tuition, so it prices differently, and a tutor who has moderated exhibitions is scarcer again. Travel is real cost: Ghodbunder Road at seven in the evening is not the same trip as two stations along the Western Line. Short commentary reviews cost less than a long inventory session. You will see the rate for your match before anything is booked, and we do not publish a price list because it would be fiction.

faqs.question: Does online work for the object session, or should it be home tuition?
faqs.answer: Start at home if you can. The inventory session works best with things physically on a table, where a tutor can pick one up and ask who gave it to your child and what happened next. After the three objects are fixed, online is often the better mode for commentary drafts, because feedback can arrive the day after a rewrite instead of a week later. Many families run exactly that split, and it costs less in travel while keeping the one session that genuinely needs a room.

faqs.question: We are in Mulund West and the tutor lives in Ghatkopar: who does the travel?
faqs.answer: The tutor travels to you for home tuition, and the rate reflects the trip. Mulund West and Ghatkopar are a short Central Line run apart, which is a pairing that holds for a full term in both directions. What we avoid is matching across the city, since a tutor crossing from the Western Suburbs to Mulund in the evening peak will deliver three good months and then start rescheduling. If travel time is heavy at your end of the city, we usually suggest a hybrid pattern instead.

faqs.question: What if my son's objects are all from the internet?
faqs.answer: That is fine if each one is particular and he can account for encountering it. A specific video, a specific post, a specific archived page all qualify as objects. The problem is not digital provenance, it is vagueness: a commentary on the internet or on memes has no real-world context to state. A tutor will push him to name the author, the date, the platform and what followed, and to keep the link to the chosen prompt visible. Mixing one physical object from home into the set usually strengthens the whole exhibition.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not a good fit after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us early and we re-match from the same shortlist, generally keeping your existing weekly slot. The signal to watch for is not friction but comfort: sessions that are pleasant and end without a decision. We ask what was meant to change and what did change, then move. The replacement tutor is given the object longlist, the plan and any draft commentary, so your child is not explaining the whole task again from the start. Changing tutors once in a term is common and nobody treats it as a complaint.

faqs.question: Do you promise a higher exhibition mark if we book a full term?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and the exhibition is assessed by your child's own school and then moderated by the IB, so nobody outside that process controls the outcome. Be wary of any tutor offering a guaranteed grade on an internally assessed component. What a term of coaching reliably changes is the quality of the justification and the precision of the object contexts, which is the part a moderator reads most closely. Ask instead for the kinds of mistakes their last few students made.

sections.heading: How a two-year fees question becomes a shortlist of home tutors in Mumbai
paragraphs: Most families who ask about fees are asking about one term. The more useful question covers both years: when will this student actually need a home tutor, for how long each time, and when will they not need one at all. So the first conversation here is a calendar conversation. Which year is the student in, which examination session are they sitting, which three subjects sit at Higher Level (HL), and which internal assessment dates are already printed on the school planner. A parent in Chembur with a DP1 student in September is planning something quite different from a parent in Khar West whose DP2 child has just opened a mock paper in January.

What comes back is not a price list. It is a shortlist of verified tutors who teach that subject at that level, filtered by where the family lives, because travel decides whether a slot survives a full term. A Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL request from Worli is matched inside the island; the same request from Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road is matched inside Thane. Matching across the city for a weekday evening lesson looks workable in week one and collapses by week six, and a collapsed slot is the most wasteful thing a family can keep paying for.

The part most families skip is the review date. Before the first session, write down when the arrangement gets looked at again: the end of the first term, the week after mock results, the fortnight after the final internal assessment goes in. A plan with review dates in it produces decisions. A plan without them produces drift, and drift is how a household ends up paying through March for sessions that stopped doing anything useful in November.

sections.heading: When does the Diploma Programme actually need the money?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) needs the most tutoring support at five predictable points: the settling-in term of DP1, the internal assessment (IA) cluster late in DP1, the Extended Essay (EE) drafting months, the fortnight after the DP2 mocks, and the final run to the papers. The months in between are quieter than almost any family expects.

The programmes below the Diploma behave differently, which is why a household moving up from one to the other gets caught out. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) in Years 4 and 5 is continuous: criterion-marked tasks arrive all year, so support tends to be steady and light rather than spiky, and a family gets used to a flat monthly shape. An IGCSE student under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel has one hard decision point, Core or Extended in Mathematics and Coordinated against separate sciences, and then a long flat stretch until the final series. The Diploma Programme is the opposite shape. It is flat for months, then most of the load lands inside a handful of weeks.

The Core is where the unbudgeted spending usually appears. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) carries an exhibition in DP1 and an essay in DP2, both of which need a reader and an argument partner more than a teacher. The EE needs a supervisor at school and, very often, somebody outside school to push back on the research question before four thousand words go in the wrong direction. A two-year plan has to cover all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai parents may end up needing, including the Core, not only the one subject that triggered the first phone call.

sections.heading: Which subjects turn into extra sessions, and when?
paragraphs: Three groups do it most often, and each one does it at a different month. Mathematics at Higher Level does it in the DP1 Diwali term. The experimental sciences do it in the internal assessment window. The essay subjects do it during the Extended Essay months. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL is the single most common reason a Mumbai family adds a weekly home tutor in October, usually because a strong IGCSE Extended grade did not translate into the HL pace.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology are quiet until the IA, and then they are not quiet at all. A Chemistry student needs a workable research question, a method that produces data worth processing, and uncertainty treatment that will not lose marks at moderation. That is a few sessions of hard thinking, not a term of teaching, and booking a standing weekly slot in August for work that happens in February is how money leaves a plan without buying anything. Group 3 behaves the same way: Economics and Business Management internal assessments are short but commentary-dense, and a History HL investigation is a research exercise most sixteen-year-olds have never attempted.

Language A at HL and Visual Arts reward early, thin support rather than late, heavy support. A student who is reading and annotating correctly in DP1 rarely needs a tutor for Paper 1 in DP2, which is a real saving that only exists if the help came early. On the IGCSE side, 0580 Mathematics Extended, 0654 Coordinated Sciences and 0500 First Language English push students towards short targeted runs before each series rather than a standing year-round slot, and that is a different spending shape again from the Diploma one.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school year, month by month, and where the spend lands
paragraphs: The Mumbai IB calendar is tight at both ends of the DP2 year and loose in the middle, and that is the whole argument of this page. Schools including Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, the American School of Bombay, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School on JVLR run broadly the same shape: a June start, a first assessment block before the Diwali break, internal assessment deadlines clustered through the DP1 spring and the DP2 autumn, mocks in January or early February for the May session, and then the papers. Naming those schools is context only; families here attend them and their calendars set the pressure points.

January is the month the market moves. Mock results come back at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane inside roughly the same fortnight, and a large share of the city DP2 parents start calling in the same week. The searches that spike then are for IB tutors near me in Mumbai, and proximity becomes the only filter left once the good slots have gone. Parents looking for the best IB tutor in Mumbai in February usually end up meaning the strongest one who is still free on a Thursday. The consequence of waiting is availability, not a different rate: a tutor with two free evenings in October has none by the end of January.

Not every household is on the May cycle. A smaller DP2 cohort sits the November session, which moves the entire shape forward by six months and puts Extended Essay drafting into the Mumbai monsoon rather than the winter. IGCSE students at Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, NES International School in Mulund West or D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul work to the Cambridge series instead, with coursework deadlines that do not line up with the Diploma ones. In a household running one child in DP2 and one in Year 11, those two calendars collide in the same February.

Diwali break: the natural review point for any DP1 arrangement

sections.heading: Switching between home tuition and online across two years in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the default here and should be, especially in DP1. A home tutor sees the desk, the phone, the notebook and how the student actually works when nobody is watching, and that is most of the diagnosis in the first month. For an IB home tutor in Mumbai the real cost of that visit is travel time, and travel time is the first thing to fail in a two-year arrangement. A slot that needs a clear road to work will not survive two monsoons and two January crunches.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai earns its place in specific windows rather than as a wholesale replacement. In the three weeks before the papers, a twenty-minute screen share on one past-paper question beats a ninety-minute home session that gets cancelled because of rain. Through the monsoon, when a Ghodbunder Road or Western Express Highway run becomes unpredictable, online protects continuity in the weeks that matter most. For a thin-pool subject such as Further Mathematics HL or a less common Language B, online may be the only route to a genuine specialist, and a family in Panvel or Mulund West should weigh that honestly rather than settling for a nearby generalist.

Most two-year plans end up hybrid, and that is precisely where the shape of IB tuition fees in Mumbai gets set. Home sessions where physical presence changes the outcome: the settling-in term, the IA planning weeks, the fortnight before a mock. Online check-ins where it does not: a quiet February for a Standard Level subject, a marked past paper discussed for half an hour, a short weekly progress call while the Extended Essay is drafting. Thinning a slot rather than cancelling it is how a household keeps a good tutor through a quiet term without paying for a full session that nobody has work for.
bullets: Home tuition first in DP1: the diagnosis needs the desk and the notebook
Online for short frequent checks in the weeks before the papers
Monsoon weeks: online protects continuity on Ghodbunder Road and JVLR
Thin-pool subjects may only be reachable online from anywhere in Mumbai
Hybrid lets a quiet term thin out instead of stopping dead

sections.heading: Checking a tutor early, because a late swap in Mumbai is the expensive one
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform is checked on identity, on the qualification they claim, and on whether they have actually taught that subject at that level rather than one adjacent to it. A Physics graduate who has never marked against the current IA criteria is not a DP Physics tutor. References from previous families are taken up, and the first session is treated as a diagnostic the family judges, not a formality the tutor passes. None of that is a substitute for the parent doing their own checking in the first fortnight.

Ask directly about the range of all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai says they cover, because somebody who claims every one of them has specialised in none. Ask which syllabus version they are working from and when it last changed. Ask them to mark one past-paper answer in front of you and explain where the marks went, which tells you more in ten minutes than any transcript. Ask what the assessment criteria are actually called in that subject. Then ask the question families forget: are you available right through to the examination month, or only this term.

The timing argument matters more here than anywhere else on this page. A swap in September costs a few weeks of progress and nothing else, because the calendar is empty behind it. A swap in February costs the weeks, the evening slot, and whatever is left of the choice in a city where every DP2 parent is already looking. Re-matching is a normal part of this and happens without drama; re-matching late is what turns a manageable plan into an expensive one. Do the checking while it is cheap to act on what you find.
bullets: Identity, qualification and subject-level teaching history checked before any match
Ask which syllabus version and which assessment criteria they work from
Ask them to mark one past-paper answer out loud in front of you
Confirm availability through to the examination month, not just this term
A September swap costs weeks; a February swap costs the slot too

sections.heading: When are IB tuition fees in Mumbai heaviest across the two Diploma years?
paragraphs: IB tuition fees in Mumbai are heaviest at five points across the two Diploma years: the DP1 settling-in term, the internal assessment cluster late in DP1, the Extended Essay drafting months, the fortnight after the January mocks, and the final run to the papers. Between those points the load should fall. In most households it does not fall, and that is where the waste lives.

The DP1 settling-in term is the one families underuse. By late September it is usually clear whether a Higher Level choice was wrong, and a rescue in October is far shorter work than the same rescue in DP2. A student who cannot hold the Analysis and Approaches HL pace in DP1 needs a run of sessions on technique. The identical student in DP2 needs the technique, plus a year of content learned badly while the technique was wrong, plus exam practice, inside half the time. That is the whole case for starting early, and it has nothing to do with rates. The internal assessment cluster is the second spike and the most predictable one in the two years: several IAs land within a few weeks, and the help that works there is short and dense rather than a standing weekly home tuition slot held since August.

The Extended Essay months are the third, and the work is argumentative rather than instructional, which means fewer sessions of a different kind. The January mock aftermath is the fourth and the one that bites hardest, because the whole city moves in the same fortnight and the family that waited is choosing from what is left. The fifth is the final run, where the best use of a session is a marked past paper rather than new teaching. Between all of these sit the quiet months, and that is where most households quietly overspend: the standing weekly session continues through a term when nothing is due, the student arrives with nothing to work on, and the hour becomes supervised homework. Pausing deliberately, with a restart date written down and the tutor told why, keeps the relationship and stops the spend. Drifting does neither.

Two further things catch Mumbai families out. The first is sibling overlap: a DP2 child and a Year 11 IGCSE child reach their heaviest weeks in the same February, so a household that planned one child two years ahead and the other a term at a time suddenly runs two arrangements at both peaks. The second is the mid-year increase. If a second weekly session during the IA cluster is agreed in principle in June, it is a decision taken in February. If it was never discussed, it arrives as a surprise in the hardest fortnight of the two years, when refusing feels like letting the child down.
bullets: DP1 settling-in: a wrong Higher Level choice takes fewest sessions to fix in October
Internal assessment cluster: short and dense, not a year-round standing slot
Extended Essay months: argument and structure, not additional teaching
January: the whole of Mumbai looks at once and availability is at its worst
Quiet terms: pause with a restart date instead of drifting on
Sibling overlap puts two separate peaks inside the same February

sections.heading: Why a good arrangement should shrink, not grow
paragraphs: Judge the first four weeks on diagnosis, not on marks. By the fourth session a tutor should be able to tell you in one sentence what the student is actually getting wrong: not that Physics is weak, but that she loses marks in the uncertainty section of every data-analysis question. At one term, school assessment marks should have moved, or there should be a clear reason they have not, and that reason should be something you can check against the marked scripts. At one exam cycle, mock to paper, the real question is whether the gap closed and whether the student can now work a question without the session.

The aim of a good arrangement is to need less of it. A tutor doing the job properly keeps handing work back: fewer sessions on content and more on marked papers, then fortnightly rather than weekly, then on call through the IA weeks. An arrangement that looks exactly the same in April of DP2 as it did in September of DP1 is worth questioning out loud. It may be genuinely necessary, as it often is in a thin-pool HL subject or where a student is carrying a long-standing gap, but the family should know which of those it is, and should ask the tutor to say so plainly rather than assuming.

The limits are worth stating. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor arriving in February of DP2 cannot manufacture a year of missed classwork in eight weeks. Tuition does not fix attendance, a subject fit nobody is willing to change, or a student who has privately decided the subject is not for them. It also cannot replace the school, which is why IB Gram stays an independent platform with no affiliation to any school, board or examination body named here. What a well-timed arrangement does is make the heavy months survivable and keep the quiet months light.
bullets: Four weeks: a specific diagnosis you can repeat back to the tutor
One term: movement in school marks, or a checkable reason there is none
One exam cycle: can the student now work a question unaided
Session load should fall across two years rather than stay flat
No tutor can replace a year of missed classwork in eight weeks

sections.heading: Planning two years of home tuition in Mumbai instead of one term
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first conversation and the two-year plan mostly writes itself: the most recent report card, the school assessment calendar for the year, the subject and level list with the examination session marked on it, and two weekly slots that work for your household rather than one. Add the visitor rule for your building if you live in a gated society, because a slot the gate will not clear is not really a slot, and that is discovered in week three far too often.

The first home session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. Expect the tutor to work through a recent school assessment or a past paper with the student, stop at each place where marks were lost, and finish by telling both of you what the next four weeks will cover and what should be different at the end of them. A single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need does not exist in one person, so if a second subject looks likely in DP2, say that in June and the second match is planned rather than scrambled.

Then agree the shape before you need it: the review dates, what specifically triggers a second weekly session, what a pause looks like and how a restart works, and how a replacement happens if the match turns out wrong. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents keep across both Diploma years is almost always one who was chosen for availability right through to the exam month, and for a travel leg that still works in July rain, rather than for having the first free Tuesday in September.
bullets: Bring the report card and the school assessment calendar to the first call
Offer two possible weekly slots, not one, and name the gate rule
First session is diagnostic: a past paper worked through out loud
Agree review dates, pause terms and replacement before session one
Say in June if a second subject is likely to be needed in DP2

faqs.question: If we can only support one of the two Diploma years, which one should it be?
faqs.answer: DP1, in almost every case. A problem found in DP1 takes fewer sessions to fix than the same problem found in DP2, because the fix is technique rather than technique plus a year of content plus exam practice under time pressure. A wrong Higher Level choice spotted in October can often still be changed at school; the same realisation in the DP2 winter cannot be acted on at all. Families who save everything for the final run end up buying the most labour-intensive version of the help, under the worst availability, in the exact fortnight when every DP2 parent in Mumbai is calling.

faqs.question: Does starting in DP1 actually reduce the total number of sessions?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the arithmetic is about what each session has to carry rather than about rates. In DP1 a session fixes a method, a way of reading a question, a habit of showing working. In DP2 that same session has to fix the method and also repair content that was learned badly while the method was wrong, and do it before the mock. That is why IB tuition fees in Mumbai are better planned as a two-year shape than as a monthly commitment, and why the honest advice is to start at the first real sign, which for most DP1 students is the October assessment block.

faqs.question: Why is January the hardest month to find a tutor in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Because mock results come back across most Mumbai IB schools inside the same fortnight, and a large share of the city DP2 parents begin looking in the same week. The scarce resource then is the weekday evening slot, not the tutor. Somebody who had Tuesday and Thursday free in October has neither by the end of January, so the household that waited takes a later slot, a longer travel leg, or a second-choice match. If your child sits the May session, treat late October as your decision point and January as the month you should already be running.

faqs.question: Our DP1 son has turned out to be in the wrong Higher Level subject. What does that do to the plan?
faqs.answer: It pulls spending forward, which is the good outcome rather than the bad one. The first job is a short intense run with someone who knows that syllabus well enough to tell you honestly whether this is a pace problem, a gap carried over from IGCSE, or a genuine mismatch of interest and ability. That takes a few weeks, not a term. If it is a mismatch, the conversation belongs with the school while the change window is still open. If it is a gap, you close it in DP1 and the whole DP2 plan gets lighter. Do not wait for the mock to confirm it.

faqs.question: Can we pause home tuition during a quiet term and restart before the mocks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a deliberate pause is far better than an arrangement that drifts. Tell the tutor the date you intend to restart and the reason you are pausing, so the slot is either held or formally released instead of quietly lost to somebody else. What does not work is continuing through a term when nothing is due: the student arrives with no work and the session becomes supervised homework. A pause also creates a natural review point, because when you restart you renegotiate the load for the months ahead rather than inheriting whatever shape last term happened to have.

faqs.question: Both our children are in the IB at the same time. How do we plan for that?
faqs.answer: Put both calendars on one sheet, because they collide more than parents expect. A DP2 child sitting the May session and a Year 11 IGCSE child under Cambridge International Education reach their heaviest weeks inside the same February, and a DP1 internal assessment cluster can land there too. Mark the fixed deadlines from each school, then decide in advance which child gets the extra sessions in the overlap month and which one waits. Households that plan one child at a time discover the clash in February, when both slots are needed at once and neither is available anywhere nearby.

faqs.question: Do we need more sessions during the Extended Essay months?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but a different kind of session rather than simply more of the same. The Extended Essay needs somebody to argue with about the research question and the structure, not somebody to teach the subject again. That tends to be a short series of long conversations instead of a standing weekly slot, and it is worth most before the first draft exists, because a badly aimed research question wastes four thousand words of work. Families who book help after the first draft comes back marked are paying to rescue writing rather than to aim it. The school supervisor leads; outside help should sharpen.

faqs.question: How do we make sure a mid-year increase in sessions is a decision and not a surprise?
faqs.answer: Agree the triggers in writing before the first session happens. Name the specific points at which the load may rise: the internal assessment cluster, the month before the mock, the final run to the papers. Agree what notice each side gives, and that any increase is reviewed again at a fixed date rather than quietly carried all the way to the exam. Then it becomes a decision you already approved in June and simply confirmed in February. Without it, the increase arrives in the hardest fortnight of the two years, when saying no feels impossible, and that is not a decision at all.

faqs.question: A tutor would travel from Vashi to our building in Nerul for an evening slot. Will that hold for two years?
faqs.answer: It can hold, provided the leg is short and the slot is realistic rather than optimistic. Node-to-node travel inside Navi Mumbai, Vashi to Nerul or Belapur to Kharghar along Palm Beach Road, survives a long arrangement far better than somebody crossing the creek from the island city after work. What breaks a two-year slot is a long peak-hour commute, a timing that only works when traffic is light, and a building that clears visitors in a narrow window. Ask for the travel time the tutor expects at seven in the evening in July, not the off-peak figure.

faqs.question: Our society in Powai clears visitors only in a fixed evening window. How do we keep one slot across both years?
faqs.answer: Get the tutor registered as a recurring visitor rather than cleared session by session. Most Powai and Hiranandani Gardens societies will issue standing weekly entry once the same name arrives at the same time for a few weeks, and many will accept a short letter from the flat owner naming the day and the slot. Do this in DP1, while the arrangement is new and nobody is under pressure. Trying to sort out gate access during the January rush, with a new tutor and a mock two weeks away, is how families lose sessions they have already planned around.

faqs.question: Does the Mumbai monsoon change how we should plan home tuition across the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, mainly by making June to September unreliable for travel. A tutor coming along the Western Express Highway, up Ghodbunder Road, or across JVLR into Powai will lose sessions to water and traffic in those months, and a cancelled session in DP1 September is lost from the most useful term of the two years. The practical answer is a hybrid agreement written in at the start: the slot is a home session by default and converts to online when the road does not cooperate, with no renegotiation needed on the night and nothing wasted.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram fit an IB home tutor into the slot you actually have free?
paragraphs: It starts with your grid, not with the subject. Before anyone asks who teaches Chemistry Higher Level (HL) well, the matching team asks for the three or four windows in your week that are genuinely free: not the hours you wish were free, but the ones that survive football practice at the society court, the swimming batch, the drive back from school and dinner. A parent who books a 6pm slot that only works in theory loses that tutor by the third week, because the tutor turned down another family to hold that hour and will not hold it twice.

The sequence runs in this order. 1. You send the programme, the subjects and your real weekly windows, including the ones you would rather not use, such as 4.30pm or Saturday morning. 2. IB Gram filters for tutors who can physically reach your address inside the travel buffer that window allows, which rules out a Borivali tutor for a 5pm Chembur start however well the subject matches. 3. You receive a shortlist in which every tutor already carries a stated slot, so you are choosing between offers rather than opening a negotiation about time. 4. The first session runs in the slot you intend to keep, not on a convenient Sunday, because a Sunday trial tells you nothing about a Wednesday at seven.

Putting the hour inside the shortlist is the step that saves the most calendar weeks. A tutor who is free on Thursday at 8pm is a completely different proposition from the same tutor free on Thursday at 5.30pm, and in Mumbai the second one is usually the harder find. When the slot is stated up front you can see immediately whether the match is about teaching quality or about the clock, and you stop discovering in week two that the only hour the tutor had was the hour your child has basketball.

If none of your windows hold, the honest answer arrives early rather than after a month of cancellations. Sometimes that means moving a subject to Saturday, sometimes splitting one long weekly session into two shorter midweek ones, and sometimes accepting an online slot for the second subject so the home slot can go to the one that needs a person in the room. None of those are compromises if they are chosen deliberately in September instead of being forced on you in January.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE: how many hours each programme asks of a Mumbai week
paragraphs: How much of your week tuition needs depends far more on the programme than on the subject. In the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme (PYP), Years 1 to 5, useful sessions are short: thirty to forty-five minutes, twice a week, placed before 5.30pm while the child is still awake enough to concentrate. Pushing a nine-year-old into a 7.30pm hour because that is when the tutor is free produces attendance, not learning. Primary slots are also the easiest ones to fill, because they sit in the part of the evening that older students cannot use.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 6 to 10, is assessed against four criteria per subject and runs on a rolling cycle of unit tasks rather than one terminal exam, which means the demand is steady instead of spiky. One weekly hour per subject holds most of the year, with a second hour added in the fortnight before a criterion D task or an MYP 5 eAssessment. Because the pressure is predictable, MYP families can usually keep an early slot all year and only negotiate extra hours twice a term.

International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) students sitting Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel papers face the Core and Extended decision, and that decision changes the hours. A student moving from Core to Extended Mathematics is picking up content the class may already have covered, so the first six weeks genuinely need two sessions a week before settling back to one. Leaving that decision to December and then asking for double hours in February is the single most common reason a family cannot find a slot at all.

The Diploma Programme (DP), Years 11 and 12, is where the week runs out of room. Six subjects at Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), an Internal Assessment (IA) in each, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) all land inside two years, and most DP families end up wanting two or three tuition slots a week rather than one. That is the point at which all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai stop being a single booking and become a timetable you have to defend against everything else in the week.
bullets: PYP: two short sessions a week, placed before 5.30pm while attention holds
MYP: one steady hour per subject, doubled before a criterion task
IGCSE: a Core to Extended move needs two sessions for roughly six weeks
DP: two or three weekly slots once IA and EE work begins
Retake and November-session students need a different calendar entirely

sections.heading: Which subjects need a weekly rhythm and which need a long block?
paragraphs: Some subjects want frequency and some want length, and matching the wrong shape to the subject wastes the hour you fought to get. Mathematics, at Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at IGCSE Core or Extended, rewards short frequent contact: two forty-five minute sessions on a Tuesday and a Friday beat one ninety-minute session on a Saturday, because the gap between practice and correction is where errors harden. If you only have one slot for Maths, put it mid-week so the tutor sees the work set on Monday before it is submitted on Thursday.

Laboratory sciences work the other way. A Physics or Chemistry session that covers a practical, the data table and the uncertainty treatment for the Internal Assessment (IA) cannot be done in forty-five minutes, so those subjects want a single long block, usually at the weekend or on the one weekday the child gets home early. The same applies to Language A written tasks and to Economics paper responses: a fifteen-mark answer needs an hour of writing plus a quarter of an hour of reading it back, and you cannot split that across two evenings without losing the thread.

Back-to-back sessions in the same subject are the arrangement most families try and most families drop. Two consecutive hours of Chemistry on a Saturday looks efficient and reads well on a calendar, but the second hour is usually spent re-explaining the first because nothing has been practised in between. The exception is IA and EE work, where a long uninterrupted block genuinely helps, since the student is producing a document rather than absorbing content. Keep teaching spaced and keep writing blocked, and the same number of paid hours does noticeably more.

Subject choice itself deserves a session of its own early on. The decisions that matter are which three subjects go to HL, whether a student takes Mathematics Analysis and Approaches because a university might want it or Applications and Interpretation because they will actually cope, and at IGCSE whether Extended is realistic in every subject or only in four. These are the questions all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers should be able to walk you through before the timetable is locked, because changing an HL in Year 12 is a scheduling emergency, not an adjustment.
bullets: Mathematics: two short midweek sessions beat one long weekend session
Physics and Chemistry IA work: one long block, weekend or early weekday
Language A and Economics essays: an hour to write, fifteen minutes to review
Avoid back-to-back hours in one subject except for IA and EE drafting

sections.heading: School-end times and evening traffic in six Mumbai zones
paragraphs: A search for IB tuition near me in Mumbai returns a map, but distance is not what decides whether a match holds; what decides it is the time your child walks through the door. South Mumbai, in Mumbai, Maharashtra, is the one zone where a 4.30pm start is sometimes genuinely available. Senior sections at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort or B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade generally finish mid-afternoon, and a child living in Colaba, Churchgate, Walkeshwar or Malabar Hill is home within half an hour. The tutor's own route is the constraint: crossing from Worli or Lower Parel down to Malabar Hill is a short distance that behaves like a long one after 6pm, because the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals back up. Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and BKC, and the Coastal Road, have improved some of those evening runs and left others untouched.

In the Western Suburbs the school bus sets the clock, not the bell. A child in Malad, Kandivali East or Borivali attending Ecole Mondiale World School or Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu is on a bus that leaves not long after the school day ends and reaches home somewhere between late afternoon and early evening, which makes 5.30pm the first honest slot and 6pm the realistic one. Oberoi International School empties onto JVLR from Goregaon East. Matching along the Western Line, Khar West to Santacruz West, Dahisar East to Borivali, works well; matching across the Western Express Highway at 6pm does not. Metro Lines 2A and 7 from Dahisar to Gundavali, and Metro Line 1 from Versova through Andheri to Ghatkopar, have made some north-south tutor routes workable that were not before.

The Central Suburbs carry one structural quirk that shapes every booking: Powai has no station of its own. A tutor reaches Hiranandani Gardens or Chandivali by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the state of JVLR at a quarter past six decides whether the 6.30pm session starts on time. Children at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai are home early enough that Powai supports a 5pm start better than most of the city. In the Eastern Suburbs, families in Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund are served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Monorail from Chembur to Wadala; NES International School sits in Mulund West, and the Eastern Freeway makes a South Mumbai tutor reachable from Chembur in a way the map hides.

Navi Mumbai and Thane are the two zones where the commute, not the school day, picks the slot. A child in Kharghar or Panvel attending a school in BKC or Bandra leaves before most of the city is awake and returns in the early evening even with the Atal Setu, Palm Beach Road and the Sion to Panvel highway working in their favour, so 6pm is the earliest sane start and 7pm is normal. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Seawoods families whose children attend D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul have far more room, and the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines plus Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 from Belapur to Pendhar keep tutors moving node to node. In Thane, Ghodbunder Road settles everything: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, which is why Thane tutors cover Thane, with Majiwada, Pokhran Road and Hiranandani Estate in between.

Western Suburbs: the bus route from Juhu schools sets the earliest slot
