sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar month by month, and the fortnights that go taut
paragraphs: The academic year in Mumbai opens in June into the monsoon, which is the worst possible combination for a new tuition arrangement and the reason so many families start in July and spend August catching up. June and July are when the week is still soft: nothing is due, the tutor can be trialled, and you can afford to test a 5.30pm slot and discover it does not work. Families who use those two months to settle the timetable almost never have a scheduling crisis later; families who wait until a report card arrives are shopping for hours at the moment every other parent is doing the same.

From September the pressure becomes periodic rather than constant. Middle Years Programme (MYP) unit tasks cluster, International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) students meet their first serious mock, and Diploma Programme (DP) Year 1 students start Internal Assessment (IA) planning. October and November bring mocks across most schools, and the fortnight around them is the first point at which a family wants to double their hours. January and February are the hardest stretch of the whole year: IA deadlines, the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and the Extended Essay (EE) final submission land close together, and a DP Year 2 student in Chembur can have a Physics IA draft due in the same fortnight as her TOK essay.

Then comes the squeeze nobody plans for. In March and April, with the May session weeks away, every DP family in the same building wants extra hours, and they want them in the same fortnight, in the same evening window, from the same small group of subject specialists. The arithmetic does not work: a tutor who holds five evening slots cannot give four of them an extra session in the same two weeks. The families who get those hours are the ones who booked them in January while the calendar was still empty, usually as a standing weekend block rather than a weekday evening.

School calendars differ, and that matters when you are sharing a tutor's evening with another family. Schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul set their own assessment and holiday dates, so two children living in the same tower can hit their crunch fortnights three weeks apart, which is occasionally useful. IB Gram names schools only to describe this local context: it is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, board or examination body mentioned on this page.
bullets: June and July: the soft window for trialling a slot without deadline pressure
October and November: mocks, and the first request for doubled hours
January and February: IA, TOK essay and EE deadlines arrive together
March and April: the pre-exam fortnight where every family wants the same hour
Book exam-term extra sessions in January, not in March

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: what each one does to your clock
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the default here, and for a weekday evening it is usually the right one. A tutor in the room gets a child who cannot minimise the window, a desk that has been cleared because someone is coming, and a parent who can hear whether the hour is working. What home tuition costs you is a travel buffer at both ends. A sixty-minute session in Khar West occupies perhaps ninety to a hundred minutes of the tutor's evening, which is exactly why the number of slots any one home tutor can hold is small, and why the popular hours disappear first. Families looking for IB home tuition in Mumbai are competing for a genuinely limited supply of early-evening road time.

Online removes the buffer, and that single fact changes which hours exist. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can teach at 9.15pm to a child in Panvel and at 7pm to a child in Bandra on the same night, and can hold a 7.30am Saturday slot that no travelling tutor would ever offer. Online is also what keeps a term intact through the monsoon, through a cancelled school bus, and through the week your building's lift is under repair. The honest trade-off is attention: an online session with a tired fourteen-year-old on a phone is a worse hour than a home session with the same child, and younger students in the Primary Years Programme (PYP) generally need someone in the room.

Hybrid is what most DP families settle into by the second term, and it is a scheduling decision rather than a preference. The pattern that works is a home session on the main teaching day, where new content and worked problems happen face to face, plus a short online check later in the week for a past-paper review or an IA draft read. That second contact costs the tutor fifteen minutes of setup instead of an hour of driving, which is why it is available at hours the home slot is not, and why it is the realistic way to add contact time in an exam fortnight.

Choose by hour, not by ideology. If your only free window is 4.30pm to 5.30pm and your child's school is nearby, book home. If your only window is after 8.30pm, or your child is in Kharghar and gets back at six, start online and move to home tuition if a daylight slot opens. An IB private tutor in Mumbai who tells you one mode is always better than the other has not looked at your week, and the decision should be revisited in January when the deadlines change shape.
bullets: Home tuition: best attention, but costs the tutor a travel buffer each way
Online: opens late-evening and early-weekend hours a travelling tutor cannot offer
Hybrid: home session for teaching, short online session for review
Monsoon weeks are the clearest case for keeping an online fallback agreed

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks about a Mumbai tutor, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Verification covers two different things, and families often only ask about the first. IB Gram checks identity, the qualification claimed, and familiarity with the actual syllabus a student is sitting, which means a tutor offering Chemistry HL should be able to talk about the current assessment structure and the IA criteria rather than about chemistry in general. Subject depth is checked against the specification, not against a resume. Where a tutor has taught Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel papers, that is recorded separately from International Baccalaureate experience, because they are not interchangeable.

The second thing, and the one that decides whether this arrangement survives to February, is reliability in a slot. Ask the questions that are about the clock. Where does the tutor come from, and what is their previous session? A tutor finishing in Lower Parel at 6pm and claiming a 6.30pm start in Juhu is telling you about a good week, not a normal one. How many evening slots are they already holding, and on which days? What is their monsoon plan? A tutor who has thought about what happens when Andheri subway floods has done this for a while.

Then check the things only you can see, over the first three or four weeks. Did they arrive within ten minutes of the agreed time every week, or did the drift start in week two? Did they send the reschedule request a day ahead or an hour ahead? Did the hour end when it was supposed to, and did the child have work to do before the next session? Anyone searching IB tuition near me in Mumbai is implicitly buying punctuality along with teaching, and punctuality is the easier of the two to assess from your own living room.

Keep the commercial arrangement month to month at the start, agree in writing who covers a session missed by each side, and know how a replacement happens before you need one. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page, and it does not guarantee grades. What can be arranged is a verified subject specialist in a slot you chose, with a stated process for changing either the tutor or the hour without losing the term.

sections.heading: What does IB tuition near me in Mumbai actually get you between 4pm and 9pm?
paragraphs: On a Mumbai weekday there is exactly one usable window, and it runs from roughly 4pm to 9pm. Before 4pm the child is in school or in a bus. After 9pm you are paying for a tired hour. Inside those five hours sit homework, a sport, dinner, a sibling's class and the tutor, and because the window is identical for every family in the city, the scarcity is not of tutors but of hours. This is the part of IB tuition near me in Mumbai that no search result shows you: the tutor you want may well be available, just not at seven.

Seven and eight are the contested hours, and for a plain reason. They are late enough that a child from a Juhu school living in Malad, or from BKC living in Kharghar, is home and fed, and early enough that nobody is falling asleep. A travelling home tutor can realistically teach two, perhaps three home sessions in an evening, and both of the hours everyone wants fall inside that stretch. Taking 4.30pm instead buys you a reliable tutor and a child who is still alert, and costs you the snack, the decompression and sometimes the sport; it works well for students whose school is close to home, and badly for anyone with a long bus.

The 9pm session deserves a blunt assessment. After a full school day, a commute down the Western Express Highway or across the creek, and a plate of food, most students can revise, practise familiar problems or be walked through a paper they have already attempted. Very few can absorb new content. If 9pm is the only hour you have, use it for past papers and corrections and move the teaching of anything new to the weekend. Weekends buy length and calm: a ninety-minute Saturday block is worth more than two tired weekday halves, which is why IB tutors near me in Mumbai are asked for Saturdays before anything else. The cost is real too, because that block displaces the match, the family lunch and the Creativity, Activity, Service commitment that has to happen sometime.

Two practical points close this out. The monsoon slot that survives is the early one: a 5pm session happens on a day when a 8.30pm session does not, because by evening the roads around Andheri, Sion and Dadar have stopped cooperating, so families who are serious about July and August either hold a daylight slot or agree an online fallback in advance. And a fair cancellation understanding is symmetrical: notice by a stated hour the previous day costs nobody anything, a same-day cancellation by the family is charged because the tutor cannot refill that hour, a same-day cancellation by the tutor is made up within the same week, and there is a sane limit on how many times either side can do it before the slot is reassigned. Written down in week one, that paragraph prevents almost every argument families have in March.
bullets: The only weekday window is roughly 4pm to 9pm, for the whole city at once
7pm and 8pm are contested because they suit the longest commutes
4.30pm buys reliability and alertness, and costs the sport and the snack
Use a 9pm hour for revision and past papers, never for new content

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks, judge the arrangement rather than the marks. Four sessions is one topic, and no honest tutor claims a grade movement from that. What should exist by then is a diagnosis you can repeat back: which two or three specific things are costing the marks, whether the problem is content, exam technique or submitting late, and a short list of what the student is doing differently. You should also know by week four whether the slot itself is stable, because a tutor who has already moved the hour twice will move it again in January when their own week fills.

At one term, you are looking for evidence in the student's own work. Rough notes that are organised, a Maths script where the method is written out instead of only the answer, an IA draft that exists rather than being promised, past-paper attempts with the marks the student gave themselves next to the marks the tutor gave. Marks often move at the first assessment after a term of steady work, and sometimes they move at the second; a term of genuine effort that produces an unchanged grade but a visible improvement in how work is produced is not a failed term.

At one exam cycle, the comparison worth making is against the student's own trajectory, not against a classmate or a target. Hours delivered is part of that: a family that kept thirty-odd weekly sessions through the year has bought something different from a family that managed a dozen around holidays, cancellations and the monsoon, and it is unfair to both student and tutor to compare the two outcomes. Count the sessions that actually happened before concluding that tuition did not work.

The honest limits are worth stating plainly. A tutor cannot add hours to a week that is already full, cannot replace a teacher a student is not listening to, and cannot compress six subjects of DP content into the eight weeks before the May session. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and nobody who has taught in Mumbai for a few years will offer you one. What a good match does is make the hour you have actually count, keep the deadline calendar visible, and stop the February pile-up from becoming a crisis.
bullets: Week four: expect a specific diagnosis and a stable slot, not a grade jump
One term: organised notes, written methods, a real IA draft, self-marked papers
One exam cycle: compare against the student's own trajectory and sessions delivered
Count cancelled sessions before deciding the arrangement did not work

sections.heading: Booking your first home tuition slot in Mumbai
paragraphs: Come to the first conversation with a week, not a wish. Write out your child's seven days as they actually are: school end, bus arrival, sport, any existing class, dinner, bedtime. Mark the three or four hours that are genuinely free and mark which of them you would prefer. That single sheet does more for the match than any description of the child's weaknesses, because the hour is the constraint that cannot be negotiated away, and a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai still only has one 7pm per evening.

Then gather four things: the current school timetable, the last report or assessment feedback, the list of subjects with HL, SL, Core or Extended marked, and any deadline dates the school has already published for IA, EE or TOK work. The deadline list is the one families forget and the one that shapes the booking most, because it tells the tutor which fortnights will need a second session and therefore whether a weekend block should be reserved now.

The first session is a working session, not a sales call. Expect a short diagnostic on recent work, a look at one past-paper question so the tutor can see how the student attacks it rather than whether they know the answer, agreement on what will be done before the next session, and confirmation of the standing slot with the notice rules spelled out. If the chemistry between tutor and student is wrong, say so after the first or second session; that is what the month-to-month arrangement is for, and changing early costs nothing.

Across South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central and Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane, the request that gets matched fastest is the specific one: programme, subjects, address, and two or three hours you can defend against everything else in the week. Vague timing is the reason good matches fall through in October, and precise timing is why some families keep the same tutor from Year 10 to the Diploma Programme.

Bring the timetable, the last report, the HL and SL list, and deadline dates

faqs.question: What time can an IB home tutor realistically start on a Mumbai weekday?
faqs.answer: Between 5.30pm and 6.30pm for most families, and 4.30pm only if the school is close to home. The chain is school end, then bus or car, then food, and in the Western Suburbs a child bussed back from Juhu to Malad or Kandivali East is rarely settled before late afternoon. South Mumbai and Powai support earlier starts because distances are short. Navi Mumbai and Thane families whose children attend island-city or BKC schools usually find 6pm is the earliest honest start, with 7pm more common once Ghodbunder Road or the creek crossing is in the picture.

faqs.question: Why are the 7pm and 8pm slots the hardest to get in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Because they are the only two hours that suit almost every family in the city at once. By 7pm a child with a long commute is home and fed; by 9pm most students are too tired to take in new content. A travelling tutor can hold two or perhaps three home sessions in one evening, and both of the hours everyone wants fall in that narrow stretch. The scarcity is in the hours, not in the tutors, which is why a tutor who seems unavailable is often perfectly available at 5.30pm or on a Saturday morning.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our building on a weekday evening, and how does the gate pass work?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the slot allows the travel time, and the gate is handled once rather than weekly. Most Mumbai societies will issue a standing visitor entry for a regular tutor if the flat owner registers the name, the day and the hour with the office, which matters because a tutor held at the gate for ten minutes every week loses a sixth of a sixty-minute session. Register the tutor in the first week, tell the guard it is a weekly slot, and keep an alternative contact number with the gate for the evenings the resident is not at home.

faqs.question: What happens when Ghodbunder Road or Peddar Road traffic makes the tutor late?
faqs.answer: The fair arrangement is that the tutor teaches the full hour or makes up the lost minutes, not that the session simply ends on time. Evening delays on Ghodbunder Road in Thane and at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in South Mumbai are predictable rather than exceptional, so they should be priced into the slot from the start by leaving a buffer or choosing a tutor who travels a shorter route. Persistent lateness is a matching problem: it usually means the tutor's previous session is too far away, and the answer is a different hour or a different tutor.

faqs.question: Is a 9pm session worth it after a full school day and a long commute?
faqs.answer: It is worth it for revision and worthless for new teaching. A student who has done a school day, a commute down the Western Express Highway or across the Atal Setu, and dinner can still work through a past paper, correct a marked script or practise problems of a type they already know. Asking the same student to meet a new topic at 9.15pm wastes the hour and the money. If 9pm is the only slot available, use it deliberately for practice and corrections, and move first teaching of anything new to a weekend block.

faqs.question: Are weekend sessions a better deal than weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: They are longer and calmer, and they cost you something else in the week. A ninety-minute Saturday morning block is the best environment for Internal Assessment drafting, laboratory write-ups and essay work, because nobody is watching the clock and the student is not already tired. The trade-off is that weekend hours collide with sport, family time and Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, and that most Mumbai families want them, so they go early in June and July. The usual compromise is one weekday evening for teaching plus one weekend block during IA and exam terms.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with the board, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs, and no honest page quotes you a figure. A Higher Level subject costs more than Standard Level, a scarce combination such as Higher Level Physics or Economics with an Internal Assessment deadline costs more than a widely taught one, and a tutor crossing a zone in evening traffic prices in that time. Session length and frequency matter too. Online sessions usually sit below home tuition precisely because no travel is involved.

faqs.question: What does a fair cancellation and rescheduling understanding look like?
faqs.answer: Symmetrical, written down before the first session, and with a limit on both sides. A workable version: notice by a stated hour on the previous day costs nobody anything; a same-day cancellation by the family is charged, because the tutor cannot refill that hour at short notice; a session the tutor cancels is made up within the same week at a time you agree; and after a set number of cancellations by either side the slot is reassigned. Agreeing this in week one removes almost every dispute that otherwise surfaces in the exam term.

faqs.question: Two sessions were lost to monsoon flooding. Does online tuition really work as a substitute?
faqs.answer: Yes for continuity, with honest limits on attention. Online genuinely saves a term through July and August, when the roads around Andheri, Sion and Dadar can close an evening slot entirely, and it saves the hour on the days a school bus does not run. It works best for past-paper review, corrections and IA draft discussion, and least well for a tired younger student on a phone. Switch the camera on, use a shared document or tablet for working, and keep the slot time identical so the week does not rearrange itself around the weather.

faqs.question: Every DP family in our building wants extra hours in the same fortnight. How does that get handled?
faqs.answer: By booking in January, because by March the arithmetic has already failed. A tutor holding a handful of weekly evening slots cannot give most of those families a second session in the same two weeks before the May session, so the hours go to whoever reserved them while the calendar was empty. The workable options are a standing weekend block reserved a term ahead, an online session at an hour no travelling tutor could offer, or a small group arrangement among neighbours sitting the same subject. Last-minute requests mostly get a different tutor, not a different hour.

faqs.question: The tutor teaches well but the slot is not working. How does a replacement happen?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram which part is failing, because the fix is different for each. If the teaching is right and only the hour is wrong, the first attempt is to move that tutor's slot or convert one session to online, which solves it often enough to try first. If the tutor cannot offer any hour you can use, a replacement is matched against your stated windows rather than against the previous tutor's profile, and the handover covers what has been covered and what is outstanding. Keep the arrangement month to month so a change is a scheduling decision, not a negotiation.

faqs.question: There is no visible progress after a month of weekly sessions. What should we look at first?
faqs.answer: Count the sessions that actually happened, then look at what changed in the work. Four weeks is often three sessions once a cancellation and a school trip are counted, which is one topic and not a fair test. Ask the tutor for the specific diagnosis and the two or three things being worked on, then look for written method in Maths scripts, an organised note file, and a self-marked past paper. If none of that exists after a genuine four sessions, the problem is the match or the hour, and it is reasonable to change one of them.

IB Gram comes back with a shortlist in which every tutor already carries a stated slot, so you choose between real offers instead of negotiating times. The first session runs in that slot, with the notice rules agreed, and the arrangement stays month to month until the hour has proved it holds.

sections.heading: How does a request for IB tuition in Mumbai turn into a shortlist?
paragraphs: A request for IB tuition in Mumbai turns into a shortlist inside a day, and the question we ask that most enquiries do not expect is about the five days when nobody is teaching. You send the board, the year group, the subjects and your pin code. We come back with tutors who teach that syllabus at that level, who can reach your building on the evenings you are actually free, and who will set written work for the gap.

The reason we ask about the gap first is that it changes the match. A Diploma Programme (DP) 2 student in Khar West with four free evenings and a tutor who sets one marked task a week is a different problem from a DP1 student in Kharghar who leaves home at six-fifteen for school in Colaba and gets back after five. The second student does not need a tutor who assigns more; she needs one who assigns less, specifies it exactly, and marks it. Match her with someone who ends every session with a page reference and a vague instruction to revise, and the arrangement will look fine for a fortnight before it quietly stops producing anything at all.

So the intake conversation covers three things that are not academic: when the school bus actually returns, what is already booked each week, and where the child works. Football twice a week, Bharatanatyam on Thursday, an Olympiad class on Sunday morning and swimming at the club are not obstacles to be removed, they are the shape of the week a task has to fit inside. A bedroom desk with a door is a different proposition from the dining table between a television and a kitchen. Tutors are told both before the first session, because a task that needs ninety uninterrupted minutes on a Wednesday will not be done in a household where Wednesday is match day.

None of this is a promise about results. IB Gram is an independent platform, and we do not guarantee grades. What the process controls is whether the home tuition arrangement produces work specific enough to be checked, which is the part almost every enquiry leaves to chance.

sections.heading: Which programme is your child in, and what does that change about the week between sessions?
paragraphs: The programme decides what between-session work can even be. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) it is a short daily habit an adult supervises. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) it is a piece of writing shaped by a published criterion. In the Diploma Programme (DP) it is a timed paper question or one named section of an Internal Assessment (IA) draft. In the Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE years it is past-paper work marked against a scheme.

Take an MYP4 Individuals and Societies student at a school in Powai. "Read chapter six" produces nothing a tutor can mark. "Write the first 250 words of your investigation using the source table, then highlight every sentence where you are describing instead of analysing" produces a page, a decision and an argument. The second instruction teaches the criterion as a side effect, because the student has to judge which of her own sentences are description before she can highlight them. The MYP criteria are published documents; a between-session task that quotes one of them does two jobs for the price of one.

In the DP the useful unit is the timed question, not the chapter. A Higher Level (HL) subject does not need longer tasks than a Standard Level (SL) one; it needs tasks that go a layer deeper and still finish in twenty-five minutes. A DP2 student taking HL Chemistry and SL Economics has two IAs, a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and an Extended Essay (EE) in motion at the same time, and the only instruction that survives that load names a single deliverable: the Economics evaluation paragraph, or the uncertainty column in the Chemistry draft. Anything broader gets postponed to a week that never arrives.

The Core and Extended decision at IGCSE matters here more than parents expect. A student entered for Core who spends her week on Extended-only questions is filling time with work that will never appear on her paper, and a student quietly capable of Extended who drills Core questions is doing the same thing in reverse. Subject choice across both boards, and the HL or SL and Core or Extended level inside it, should be settled before anyone sets a term of work, because the level is what tells the tutor which past papers and which variants are worth the student's evenings.
bullets: PYP: one short supervised habit, same time daily, written down somewhere
MYP: a paragraph written against a named criterion, then highlighted by the student
IGCSE: past-paper questions from the correct tier, marked against the scheme
DP SL: one timed question plus the marking, not a whole exercise set
DP HL: same twenty-five minutes, one layer deeper, single named deliverable

sections.heading: Subject by subject: what a strong between-session task actually says
paragraphs: The difference between a weak task and a strong one is almost never quantity. It is whether the instruction names an output. "Revise moles" is weak. "Do Q3 and Q4 of the 2018 Paper 2, show every unit conversion, and write one line under each saying which step you were unsure of" is strong, because when the tutor sits down there is either a page or there is not. No judgement is needed, no argument about effort is possible, and the session starts from evidence rather than from a negotiation about how much was done.

Mathematics shows the distinction most clearly. A DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches SL student in Chembur who can already integrate by substitution gains nothing from twenty more substitution questions. That is practice as time-filling: it feels like work, it produces a full page, and it moves nothing. Fluency practice looks different. Three questions she can nearly do, on a timer, then marked against the published scheme with every lost mark circled, is twenty minutes that changes her next paper. The test for any Maths task is blunt: could she already do it before she started? If yes, it was exercise, not learning.

In the sciences the task should be a named section, never the whole IA. "Work on your Physics IA" produces a reopened document and nothing else. "Write the Method so another student could repeat it without asking you a single question, and fill the uncertainty column for the first three trials" produces something a tutor can mark in four minutes and hand straight back. A Chemistry IA draft and a TOK essay landing in the same fortnight is ordinary in DP2, and the only way through it is one named section at a time, in writing, with a date attached to each.

English Language and Literature Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen text, so the honest task between sessions is a plan and one body paragraph, not a finished essay nobody will read closely. Economics rewards a fifteen-mark evaluation paragraph practised against the command term. History rewards one source comparison written out. Some subjects are harder to staff across Mumbai, among them HL Economics, Computer Science and Further Mathematics, and scarcity changes which evenings are available far more than it changes what the task should say.

Attach a date and a time limit, not just a chapter number

sections.heading: What eats the week between sessions in each of the six Mumbai zones
paragraphs: Across Mumbai, Maharashtra the thing that destroys between-session work is rarely laziness. It is the commute. A child who spends three hours a day in a car or on a train has already spent her best hours sitting still, and whatever is left after dinner is what a tutor is really competing for. A search for IB tutors near me in Mumbai returns a map of names; what decides the outcome is which evenings survive the journey, and that is geography rather than effort.

In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock is not: a tutor moving from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, even with the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 easing part of it. Families in Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar and Fort usually end up with a late slot, so tasks here have to be short and precise. In the Western Suburbs the Western Line and the Western Express Highway run the schedule, and matching along the line, Khar West to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali East, works far better than matching across it. Bandra, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon East, Borivali and Dahisar East now sit on Metro Lines 1, 2A and 7, which has made mid-week slots more realistic than they used to be.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so tutors reach Powai by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar and the return leg sets the end of the slot. Kurla and Mulund are easier to serve. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Wadala are joined by the Harbour Line, the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) and the Eastern Freeway, which makes IB home classes in Mumbai's eastern belt workable even for tutors living on the island, and the Monorail covers the short Chembur to Wadala hop.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway. Node-to-node matching holds for a full term where dragging a tutor across the creek does not, even with the Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line shortening the map. Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the timetable: twenty minutes to Kasarvadavali off-peak, close to an hour at seven in the evening. A Thane student's between-session window is wider than her session window, which is the exact opposite of South Mumbai.

Western Suburbs: match along the Western Line, not across the highway
Central Suburbs: Powai has no station, so the return leg ends the slot
Eastern Suburbs: the Eastern Freeway makes island tutors viable in Chembur
Navi Mumbai: node-to-node along Palm Beach Road holds for a full term

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar decides what between-session work is possible
paragraphs: Mumbai's IB and IGCSE schools run a year that peaks three times, and between-session work has to shrink and grow with it. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Oberoi International School on JVLR and Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort are living with different internal deadlines on the same city calendar.

August and September bring the first summative round and the Ganpati week, which removes a weekend and usually a weekday with it. October and November are when DP1 internal exams and MYP summatives arrive together, and this is where a vague instruction does the most damage: a student with four subjects assessing in the same fortnight needs her tutor to set less, not more. One named task per subject, written down, is the only thing that survives that month. Ask for more and you will get nothing, because the student will triage you out before she triages the school out.

January to March is the heaviest stretch for DP2. Mocks, final IA deadlines, the EE submission and the TOK essay all sit inside it, and the task between sessions has to become one thing at a time. Students at B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul run different internal timetables, so the single most useful document to hand a new tutor is the school's own assessment calendar rather than a general study plan.

The monsoon is the other calendar. From June to September a Tuesday evening can vanish to waterlogging at Hindmata, Sion, the Milan Subway or the Andheri Subway, and when the Western or Central Line halts, home tuition stops with it. The honest response is to set work that does not depend on the session happening: a task with its own deadline, submitted as a photograph, so a washed-out evening costs one session and not one week. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools or with any board; naming them is simply how Mumbai parents describe which calendar they are living with.
bullets: August to September: Ganpati week removes a weekend and often a weekday
October to November: four subjects assessing at once, so set one task each
January to March: DP2 mocks, IA deadlines, EE and TOK in one stretch
June to September: monsoon cancellations, so deadlines sit before the session
Hand the tutor the school's assessment calendar, not a generic study plan

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which one survives a Mumbai week?
paragraphs: Home tuition wins on the one thing this page is about: a tutor at your dining table can see the notebook. IB home tuition in Mumbai means the week's work is physically present, open on the table, half-finished or absent, and nobody has to take a teenager's word for what happened on Wednesday. That single fact is why it stays the lead option even though it is the slowest to arrange.

The cost is travel. An IB private tutor in Mumbai gives up sixty to ninety minutes a day to the road, which limits how many evenings she can offer and makes a cancelled slot expensive on both sides. A wet evening on Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway can remove the session outright, and if the week's work was only ever going to be checked inside that session, the week goes with it. Home tuition therefore needs a submission deadline that sits earlier than the session, not a promise to bring the book along.

IB online tuition in Mumbai solves the travel problem and creates a verification one. A screen share is genuinely good for marking a document, pasting a stuck list, or working through a past paper side by side, and for a Kharghar student whose school is in Colaba it may be the only realistic weekday option. But a tutor on a video call cannot see whether the notebook exists. Online holds together for between-session accountability only when the output is a file or a photograph sent before the call rather than described during it.

The arrangement that lasts is hybrid, and specifically a lopsided one: a weekly session at home where the teaching happens, plus a twenty-minute online check-in mid-week whose only purpose is to look at the work. It is short, it costs almost nothing in travel, and it moves the deadline from Saturday to Wednesday, which is precisely where most between-session work fails. Families in Thane, Navi Mumbai and the far Western Suburbs get the most from it. Families in South Mumbai with a tutor ten minutes away often do not need it at all.
bullets: Home: the notebook is visible, so nothing rests on self-reporting
Home: sixty to ninety minutes of tutor travel limits available evenings
Online: excellent for marking a submitted file, blind to an unopened one
Online rule: work goes in before the call, not shown during it
Hybrid: one home session plus a twenty-minute mid-week work check

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks, and what you should check in the first fortnight
paragraphs: IB Gram checks identity, qualification and syllabus-specific teaching experience before a tutor reaches your shortlist, and syllabus-specific means the paper, the variant and the level, not the subject in general. Someone who has taught Cambridge IGCSE Physics is not automatically right for DP Physics HL Paper 3. We also ask for a teaching sample and for references from families who used that tutor for a full term, because discipline about work between sessions shows up across a term and almost never inside a demo class.

What you check is different, and it takes two minutes a week. Was the work attempted? Is there something written to show me? Did you ask the tutor anything? Three yeses mean the arrangement is alive even if marks have not moved yet. One yes means it is not, whatever the session felt like from the next room. You are not marking the work and you are not teaching it, and the moment you start doing either you have replaced the tutor with yourself while still paying for both.

The clearest warning sign is a session that opens with "did you do it?" and the answer is no. Once, that is a bad week. Three times running and the tutor is spending your sessions doing the work that was supposed to arrive already done, which is the most expensive possible way to get it done. Ask for the task log at that point: what was set, on which date, and what came back. If the tasks were vague, the tutor's instructions need to change. If they were specific and ignored, the problem sits upstream of the tutor and a replacement will inherit it unchanged.

Parents hunting for the best IB tutor in Mumbai are usually one step away from the right question. The tutor who moves your child's marks is the one whose instructions get followed, and that depends on fit, timing and specificity as much as on subject mastery. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school or board named on this page, and we do not guarantee grades. What we can do is replace a tutor who is not setting checkable work, and tell you plainly when the issue is not the tutor.
bullets: We check identity, qualification and experience with the exact paper and level
References come from families who ran a full term, not a demo
You check three things weekly: attempted, written down, questions asked
Ask for the task log before asking for a new tutor
Do not mark the work yourself; that quietly replaces the tutor

sections.heading: The 167 hours: why what happens between sessions decides whether IB home tuition in Mumbai works
paragraphs: Two hours of home tuition is about one per cent of a week. The other 167 hours are where a subject is either learned or not, and tuition is not the input; it is the correction mechanism for the input. This is the part of IB tuition in Mumbai that nobody advertises, because it hands the work back to the student. A good tutor compresses a week of attempted confusion into two hours of repair. Where there is no week of attempted work, there is nothing to repair, and the session degrades into a lecture the student will have forgotten by Monday evening.

Two habits do most of the lifting, and neither needs a technical name. The first is coming back to a topic after you have begun to forget it. A DP1 student in Vikhroli who finishes a Chemistry topic on Sunday and does not touch it again until the mock has learned it once. The same student who spends ten minutes on it the following Wednesday, and ten more the Sunday after, has learned it three times for less total effort and will still have it in March. The second habit is closing the book. Writing out what you remember on blank paper is uncomfortable and slow, and it is far more useful than re-reading notes that make perfect sense while you are looking at them. Highlighting is the most dependable way to feel productive while changing nothing.

The single most valuable object a student can carry into a session is a list of what she did not understand, written while she did not understand it. One line each: the question number, and what specifically stopped her. "I don't get calculus" is not a line. "Q7b, I could not tell whether to use the chain rule or the product rule" is, and it converts two hours of general review into targeted repair. The list has to be written on the spot rather than reconstructed on Saturday morning, because by Saturday the confusion has smoothed over and the student arrives blank, saying it was fine, and the tutor has to spend the first thirty minutes finding the problem the student already found on Tuesday.

Which leads to the sentence most tuition pages avoid. A student who does nothing between sessions will not improve, and no tutor can fix that from the outside. A tutor can make the task smaller, clearer, dated and harder to avoid; she cannot do it on the student's behalf. Fees reflect her side of the arrangement and nothing more: board and level, how scarce the subject is, how far she travels and how long the session runs. Buying a longer session to compensate for an empty week is the commonest response and the least effective one. We do not guarantee grades, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching.
bullets: The session is about one per cent of the week; the rest decides the result
Return to a topic days later, not in the hours before a test
Close the book and write what you remember on blank paper
One line per stuck point, written while you are actually stuck
Photograph the working so the tutor marks what you wrote, not what you recall
A longer session cannot substitute for an unworked week

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at marks. You should be looking at artefacts. Is there a notebook with dated, attempted work in it? Has the stuck list become more specific, moving from "I don't understand graphs" to "I lose the sign when the gradient is negative"? Is the work being done without being chased three times? Those three things genuinely change inside four weeks. Marks usually do not, and a tutor who promises otherwise at the four-week mark is guessing in front of you.

At one term, internal assessment marks either move or they do not, and both outcomes tell you something provided the between-session record exists. Work attempted and marks moving means carry on. Work attempted and marks flat is the genuinely useful case: it means the diagnosis is wrong rather than the effort, and the tutor should be changing what is practised instead of how much. Work not attempted and marks flat is not a tuition problem at all, and more sessions will not touch it. Without a record of what was set and what came back, you cannot tell these three cases apart, which is the real argument for keeping one.

Across a full exam cycle the honest statement is that there are no guarantees. Boards set grade boundaries after the fact, a May session can go badly for reasons no tutor controls, and a student who worked steadily can still miss a 7. What a term of checkable work does buy you is a result you can explain: you will know which topics were practised, which were quietly avoided, and where the marks went. A parent who can explain a result can act on it next time, which a predicted grade never allowed.

If nothing has shifted after a month, work through it in order. Read the task log first. If the tasks were vague, the fix is the instruction and not the person. If they were specific and undone, ask why, and the answer is usually the timetable rather than the attitude: a Thane student with football twice a week and a school run down the Eastern Express Highway may simply not own the ninety-minute block her tutor assumed. Split the work into two twenty-minute blocks before changing anything else, and give that a fortnight.
bullets: Four weeks: dated attempted work, a sharper stuck list, less chasing
One term: marks move, or the diagnosis was wrong, or nothing was done
Exam cycle: there are no guarantees, but the result becomes explainable
No change after a month: read the task log before changing tutor
Try two twenty-minute blocks before assuming an attitude problem

sections.heading: Starting home tuition in Mumbai: what should you have ready before the first session?
paragraphs: Five things, and they take one evening to gather. The subject guide or syllabus code for every subject, so nobody practises the wrong tier. The last two pieces of marked school work, with the teacher's comments left on them. The school's assessment calendar for the term. One notebook kept only for tutor work, so the record lives in a single place. And the real weekly timetable, including the commitments that are not up for negotiation.

The first session is diagnostic and should look like it. The tutor works through a recent piece of school work, finds where it actually broke rather than where the marks were lost, and spends the last ten minutes writing the first task down: what, how long, by when, and what gets sent. One home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is not a realistic ask, and nobody should pretend it is; IB Gram matches subject by subject for all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes anywhere in Mumbai, which is why the intake asks for each subject separately.

Fix the slot rather than arranging it weekly. A standing Tuesday and Friday is worth more than two movable sessions, because a between-session deadline needs a fixed point to count back from. Clear a surface with a door if you have one, and if you do not, pick the quietest two hours of the day over the most convenient ones. For the first session have an adult at home, not to supervise the teaching but to hear what task was set, because that is the one piece of information the whole household needs to hold on to.

After you send the request you will hear back with a shortlist rather than one name, because fit on evenings matters as much as fit on subject. You choose, you meet, and if the first task is not written down before the tutor leaves that first session, say so immediately: it is the easiest thing in the world to fix in week one and close to impossible in month three. Sessions run across South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane.
bullets: Bring syllabus codes, two marked pieces of school work, and the school calendar
Keep one notebook only for tutor work, so the record stays in one place
Share the real timetable, including football, music and Sunday classes
Fix a standing slot so the between-session deadline has an anchor
Insist the first task is written down before the tutor leaves

faqs.question: What exactly should my child be doing between IB tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: One named task per subject, with an output the tutor will mark. Concretely: two or three past-paper questions done on a timer, the working photographed, then marked against the published scheme with every lost mark circled; or one named section of an IA draft; or a single paragraph written against a criterion. The instruction should fit on one line and should be impossible to half-do invisibly. "Revise the topic" fails that test on both counts. If your child cannot tell you in one sentence what she is supposed to produce before the next session, the task was not set properly and that is the tutor's problem to correct.

faqs.question: The tutor did not set any work this week. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Yes, unless it was deliberate and explained to you. The week between sessions is where the learning actually happens, so a session that ends without a specific task has given away most of its value. There are legitimate exceptions: a school exam block, the fortnight before a DP2 IA deadline when the school has already loaded the student, or a deliberate rest after mocks. Ask which one it is. If the answer is that your child is already doing enough, ask to see what came back the previous week instead; the task log settles the question much faster than a conversation about effort does.

faqs.question: How do I check the work without turning into a second teacher?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions once a week and then stop. Was the work attempted? Is there something written to show me? Did you ask the tutor anything? You are checking that the loop is running, not whether the Physics is correct. Start marking the work and you will end up teaching it, and your child will begin treating your opinion as the real assessment. Keep the judgement with the tutor and the record with yourself. A parent who can answer those three questions every week will spot a failing arrangement roughly a month before the report card does.

faqs.question: Our tutor travels to our building in Thane on a weekday evening. What happens when the monsoon shuts the roads?
faqs.answer: The session moves online and the deadline does not move with it. Ghodbunder Road and the Eastern Express Highway can add an hour in heavy rain, and when the Central Line halts, home tuition stops with it. The arrangement that survives this is one where the week's work was due on Wednesday night as a photograph, so a washed-out Friday costs a session rather than a week. Most tutors will switch to a video call on an hour's notice. Agree that rule in week one rather than during the first downpour, and agree what happens when it is the student who cannot get home.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: For the first session yes, after that rarely. The first session is where the diagnosis happens and the first task is set, and someone in the household should hear that task directly rather than relayed by a teenager. After that, a home tutor arriving at a standing time needs predictable access more than supervision. An adult in the room matters mainly for younger PYP and MYP students whose daily habit needs an eye on it. For a DP student a parent sitting in usually makes the session worse. What you do need is a cleared surface that is not shared with dinner.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, in roughly that order. HL DP subjects sit above MYP ones, scarce subjects such as HL Economics, Computer Science or Further Mathematics sit above widely taught ones, and a tutor crossing twice a week from Andheri to Nerul prices that road into the slot. IB Gram does not publish a rate card, because the honest answer varies across all five factors and a single figure would be a guess. One thing worth knowing for this page: buying a longer session to make up for an unworked week is the least efficient money in tuition.

faqs.question: My son's school is in South Mumbai and we live in Kharghar. He has no time. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Shrink the task and move it off the commute. A student leaving Kharghar before seven and getting back after five has one usable block a day, not three, so his work between sessions has to be twenty minutes that count rather than ninety that do not. Two short retrieval stints beat one long sitting. The Atal Setu and Harbour Line journey itself is fine for reading and useless for written work, so do not plan around it. Tell the tutor the real timings: a task designed for a child with four free evenings gets abandoned in week two by a child with one.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work if the whole point is checking the work?
faqs.answer: It works when the output is submitted before the call rather than described during it. On a video call a tutor can mark a photographed page, annotate a document and work through a paper live, all of which is effective teaching. What a tutor cannot do through a screen is see whether a notebook exists at all. So the rule for online is stricter, not looser: the work goes in by a stated time the night before, and the session opens with it already on screen. Arrangements that skip that step drift into conversation, and conversation is the most comfortable way to lose a term.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Look at the task log before you look for a new tutor. Three outcomes are possible and each needs a different fix. Tasks vague: the tutor has to start naming outputs and dates. Tasks specific and done but marks flat: the diagnosis is wrong, so what is being practised must change, which is a conversation rather than a reason to leave. Tasks specific and undone: the obstacle is the timetable or the willingness, and a new tutor inherits it untouched. A month is long enough to judge the artefacts and far too short to judge grades.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. How does a replacement happen?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram what specifically is not working and we shortlist again, usually within a few days. Useful reasons are concrete: no written task after three sessions, the level is wrong for the paper being sat, the slot keeps moving, or the student has stopped asking questions. We will ask to see the task log, because it separates a teaching problem from a scheduling one. Handover matters more than speed here: the incoming tutor should receive the stuck list and the last marked work, so the first session continues the diagnosis instead of starting it again from nothing.

faqs.question: How long should work between sessions take each day?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents expect, spread over more days than they expect. For a PYP or MYP student, ten to twenty minutes on most days beats an hour on Sunday. For a DP student carrying six subjects, two IAs, the TOK essay and the EE, the realistic unit is one timed question per subject per week plus the marking, which totals well under an hour a day. The number that matters is not minutes anyway; it is how many days had something written on them. Four short days and three empty ones outperforms one long day, every single time.

ib-tuition.closingCta: Send the board, the year group, the subjects and your pin code, and say which evenings are genuinely free. You will get a shortlist of tutors who teach that syllabus and can reach your building. The first session ends with one written task, a date and an output your tutor will mark. After the second session you will see both the task and the marking, and you can decide from evidence rather than impression.

sections.heading: How does a Mumbai request for home tuition turn into a shortlist?
paragraphs: Send five things: the subject, the level, the school, your area and the two or three evenings that are genuinely free. The shortlist is built on your week before it is built on the subject, because a tutor your family cannot reach at the hour you have open is not a tutor you will still have in October. You should expect a small set of profiles, each carrying an honest travel estimate from the tutor's own area to yours, not a long list sorted by credentials.

The free-evening question comes first for a reason. A student in the first year of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme who lives in Chembur, has football on Thursday, a Model United Nations commitment every second Saturday and school until half past three is not short of tuition options; she is short of evenings. Once a parent names Monday and Wednesday as free, the match is half decided, because only tutors who can be in Chembur by seven without a two-hour crawl up the Eastern Express Highway are real candidates.

Your own hours start here, not at the first session. Two or three profile reads, one short call per shortlisted tutor, a message thread to fix the slot, and a conversation with your child about why this is happening at all. That is most of an evening for a parent in Mumbai who is already running a working week, which is why the shortlist stays small. Three considered profiles cost you less time than eleven plausible ones, and the longer list rarely changes the decision.

Requests get sent back at this stage too. A parent in Borivali asking for a Higher Level (HL) Physics specialist at home on a Friday at nine at night will hear that the slot is unrealistic before anyone is matched to it, because an arrangement that needs a tutor to cross the Western Express Highway late on a Friday collapses quietly by the second month, and the family pays for that collapse in lost weeks.
bullets: 1. Send subject, level, school, area and the evenings that are genuinely free.
2. We shortlist on travel and timetable first, then on subject and component depth.
3. You hold one short call per shortlisted tutor, fifteen minutes is enough.
4. The first session is diagnostic and ends with a named list of gaps.
5. A four-week review sets frequency and asks what can already be dropped.

sections.heading: What each programme actually costs a Mumbai family in hours
paragraphs: Programme decides the shape of the time, not just the content. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child needs short, frequent contact, two half-hour sits rather than one long session, and almost no work between them; the real cost there is the parent's supervision, not the student's calendar. Middle Years Programme (MYP) Years 4 and 5 sit in the middle, with enough formal assessment to need structure and enough slack in the week to absorb a slot without displacing anything that matters.

IGCSE under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel is the first point where the week genuinely tightens. Grade 9 and 10 students carry coursework, practical work and past-paper practice, and a Grade 10 student in Khar West with mocks in January is in the first year of her life where a Saturday is a resource rather than a given. Families usually start with one or two subjects at this stage, which is survivable. The ones who get into trouble add a fourth in November, because each subject individually looked reasonable.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is a different order of magnitude: six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level (SL), with the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service running underneath all of it. A DP1 student already spends most of her discretionary hours on school work. Every tuition hour added in DP1 comes out of something else, and in DP2 that something is usually sleep, which is the worst available place to take it from.

So the programme question is really a question about ceilings. One subject with an IB home tutor in Mumbai fits almost any DP week. Two fit if the household protects one clear evening and defends it. Three is the point where the arrangement starts consuming the thing it was meant to protect, and a counsellor who has watched this happen will say so rather than take the booking and let February settle the argument.
bullets: Primary Years Programme: short frequent sits, parent supervision is the real cost
Middle Years Programme Years 4 and 5: structure needed, slack still available
IGCSE Grades 9 and 10: coursework and past papers start eating Saturdays
Diploma Programme Year 1: one or two subjects fit, three rarely do
Diploma Programme Year 2: every added hour comes out of sleep first

sections.heading: The hours hidden inside HL, SL, Core and Extended choices
paragraphs: Subject choice sets the workload for two years, and the internal assessments are where the hours actually go. Physics at Higher Level carries an Internal Assessment (IA) needing a question, a method, real data and an uncertainty analysis; students routinely spend three or four weekends on it and no tutor can compress that into a session. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level punishes a weak Grade 10 algebra base for two full years, which is why the honest answer to a DP1 parent is often that the first six sessions will be remedial rather than forward-looking.

At IGCSE the Core and Extended decision has the same structure. A student pushed into Extended Mathematics in Grade 10 because her school expects it before Analysis and Approaches is taking on a term of catch-up on top of a normal year, and that term has to come out of her week somewhere. Sciences add practical papers, and Business Studies and Economics add case-study technique that cannot be hurried. All IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers behave this way: the examinable content is finite, the skill underneath it is not.

Language choices quietly cost the most reading time. English A Language and Literature needs works read closely enough to write a comparative essay under time pressure, and Hindi B or French B at Higher Level needs sustained oral practice that a weekly session can direct but cannot supply. The work between sessions is the subject. A tutor who sets none is lighter on your calendar and worth less, and a tutor who sets four hours of it for a DP2 student with two IAs due in the same fortnight is not reading the calendar at all.

This is why a first session should be diagnostic rather than instructional. Which papers and components is this student losing marks on, what does the relevant IA criterion actually ask for, and how many hours a week does she have before anything is added. A home tuition plan written without those three answers gets rewritten within a month, and the rewriting is paid for in term time that the exam calendar will not give back.
bullets: Physics and Chemistry Internal Assessments: several weekends of data and uncertainty work
Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level: expect remedial algebra before new content
IGCSE Extended Mathematics after a Core start: roughly a term of catch-up
English A Language and Literature: reading time no session can substitute for
Language B oral practice: daily minutes matter more than weekly hours

sections.heading: Travel time across the six zones of Mumbai, honestly counted
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is six working geographies rather than one city, and IB tutor cost in Mumbai is partly a map problem: the same tutor is a sensible match in one zone and a fantasy in the next. South Mumbai is short in kilometres and long in minutes. A tutor moving from Worli to Colaba or Cuffe Parade covers single-digit distances and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening, so matches here are made within the island rather than pulled down from the suburbs. Families around Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Fort generally get a tutor who already lives south of Mahalaxmi, served by the Western Line out of Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line from CSMT, and Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and BKC.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, and matching along that line works while matching across it does not. Khar West to Santacruz is ten minutes at noon and twenty-five at half past six; Malad to Kandivali is similar; Bandra to Andheri West is easy at four in the afternoon and genuinely painful at six. Metro Line 1 across Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 from Dahisar down to Gundavali have made those runs predictable for tutors who travel by train and metro, which matters more than raw distance. The Bandra–Worli Sea Link and the Coastal Road help a Juhu or Khar tutor going south, not one going north.

The Central Suburbs hang off the Central Line, JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway, and Powai shapes every schedule there because it has no station of its own. A tutor arrives by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Chandivali or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road is the difference between a thirty-minute and a seventy-minute approach. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund are strung along the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway makes a Wadala or Chembur tutor reachable from the island faster than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion–Panvel Highway, and the Atal Setu has shortened the crossing without making a weekday evening lesson across it sensible. Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, where a tutor living near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at eight at night. The student's own travel counts here too. A DP student driven from Thane to a tutor's flat in Mulund spends more of her evening in a car than in the lesson, which is the strongest practical argument for home tuition in Mumbai over anything that requires her to move.

Khar West to Santacruz: ten minutes at noon, twenty-five at half past six

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar decides when the hours hurt most
paragraphs: The academic year here starts in June and the pressure points are predictable. Internal Assessment drafts cluster in the weeks after the Diwali break, mocks land in January and February, and the May examination session means a DP2 student's last genuinely free evenings are in November. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort and Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu are all working to a version of the same rhythm, and a tutor who starts in February is starting after the useful window has closed.

Co-curricular calendars make it worse in exactly the months you would want free. Inter-school Model United Nations season, sports day, the school production and Creativity, Activity, Service deadlines sit on top of the assessment calendar, and the student doing all of it well is the one with no spare hours at all. A Grade 10 student at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane facing January mocks and a December production has a two-week window in which new tuition can be absorbed, and it is rarely the fortnight in which the parent happens to be worrying.

Board transitions add a second kind of cost. A student moving from IGCSE at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai into the Diploma Programme, or from a state board into IGCSE at NES International School in Mulund West or D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, needs a diagnostic term rather than a crash course, and parents who compress that into six weeks before an exam usually pay for it twice. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools or with any board; naming them here is local context about calendars and nothing more.

The practical use of the calendar is timing. June, July and the first half of August are the emptiest weeks of the year, so a tutor can run a diagnostic without displacing anything the student cares about. November is workable. February of DP2 is expensive in hours and thin in return, not because the tutoring is worse but because there is nothing left in the week to give it, and a student who is already tired cannot convert an added session into marks.
bullets: June to mid-August: the emptiest weeks, diagnostics fit without displacing anything
Post-Diwali: Internal Assessment drafts cluster, new arrangements land badly
January and February: mocks, plus school productions and sports day

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which one costs the least time?
paragraphs: Home tuition costs the student the least time and gives the household the most flexibility. Nobody travels, the books are already open on the dining table, and a ninety-minute slot takes ninety minutes plus about ten of settling. That is why home tutoring leads on this page, and why IB tutor cost in Mumbai is misleading when it is read as the quoted hour alone. The hour is the smallest part of what the arrangement actually takes from your week.

The honest trade-off is that home tuition imports the tutor's travel into your family's schedule. A tutor crossing from Ghatkopar to Powai on a Tuesday at seven is in traffic whether or not the lesson goes well, which narrows the set of people who can hold your slot reliably week after week, and travel distance is one of the things any quote depends on. It also fixes the evening. The arrangement works precisely because it is the same day every week, and that regularity is what reorganises the household around it.

Online removes both commutes and buys the student's evening back. For a DP2 student in Kharghar who needs a Higher Level Chemistry specialist who happens to live in Bandra, an IB online tutor in Mumbai is not a compromise; it is the only version of that match that survives a full term. The cost moves rather than disappearing. Attention is harder to hold on a screen, diagram-heavy work runs slower, and a tired student at nine at night is less present online than she would be in a room with someone.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without naming it: in person for the sessions that need paper, a shared screen for past-paper review and for the weeks when Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway makes a visit a coin flip. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai can be run this way. The deciding question is never which mode is better in the abstract; it is which mode costs this particular student the fewest hours out of the week she actually has.
bullets: Home tuition: no travel for the student, one fixed evening for the household
Online: buys back both commutes, costs attention and diagram-heavy work
Hybrid: paper in person, past-paper review on a shared screen
An IB private tutor in Mumbai holds a slot only if the travel is realistic
